Published electronicallyis that not absurd? Zhōu Yǔ 1.1 "Jì Gōng Moufù Admonishes King Mù Regarding Conquering the Quǎnróng"
King Mù was about to campaign against the Quǎnróng. Jì Gōng Moufù admonished him, saying: "It is not permissible. The former kings displayed virtue, not military might. Now, weapons are stored away and moved only when necessary. When moved, they inspire awe. To display them is to trifle with them. To trifle with them is to lose the power to inspire dread. Therefore, the *Song* of Duke Wen of Zhou says: 'We store away shields and spears, We case bows and arrows. I seek excellent virtue, Extending it throughout this Xia, Truly the king protects it.' The former kings treated the people by diligently rectifying their virtue and enriching their nature, increasing their resources and seeking to benefit their tools and implements, making clear the directions of profit and harm, and cultivating them with culture, causing them to strive for profit and avoid harm, to cherish virtue and fear power. Therefore, they were able to preserve their dynasty and grow greater.
"In the past, our former kings served Hou Ji for generations, in order to serve the虞 and 夏 dynasties. And when the 夏 dynasty declined, they abandoned agriculture and did not attend to it. My ancestor, Buzhu, therefore lost his office, and fled into the midst of the Rong and Di peoples. He dared not be idle, he ordered their virtues according to the seasons, he continued and cultivated their undertakings, he cultivated their instructions and rules, he was respectful and diligent morning and night, he guarded them with sincerity and faithfulness, he honored them with loyalty and trust, he passed on virtue through successive generations, not disgracing his predecessors. As for King Wen and King Wu, they illuminated the brightness of their predecessors and added to it kindness and harmony, they served the gods and protected the people, none were not pleased and joyful. King Di Xin of Shang was greatly hated by the people. The common people could not bear it, and joyfully supported King Wu, leading to the battle at Muye against Shang. Thus, the former kings did not engage in warfare for its own sake, but diligently cared for the people's sufferings and removed their harms. "The system of the former kings was: Within the state, the *dian* service; outside the state, the *hou* service; the *hou* and *wei* offer guest service; the *yi* and *man* offer required service; the *rong* and *di* offer wilderness service. Those who offer the *dian* service, offer sacrifices; those who offer the *hou* service, offer ancestral rites; those who offer guest service, offer tribute; those who offer required service, offer contribution; those who offer wilderness service, acknowledge the king. Daily sacrifices, monthly ancestral rites, seasonal tribute, yearly contribution, ultimate acknowledgement of the king, are the teachings of the former kings. If there is failure to sacrifice, then cultivate sincerity; if there is failure to perform ancestral rites, then cultivate proper speech; if there is failure to offer tribute, then cultivate proper customs; if there is failure to offer contribution, then cultivate reputation; if there is failure to acknowledge the king, then cultivate virtue. If, after the sequence is established, there are those who do not arrive (to perform their duty), then apply punishment. Thus, there are punishments for those who do not sacrifice, attacks for those who do not perform ancestral rites, expeditions for those who do not offer tribute, rebukes for those who do not offer contribution, announcements against those who do not acknowledge the king. Thus, there are examples of criminal punishment, There are troops for attacking and punishing, there are preparations for expeditions and campaigns, there are decrees for awe-inspiring concessions, there are pronouncements in the form of written announcements. If issuing decrees and declarations still does not bring submission, then one should cultivate virtue and not trouble the people in distant lands. Therefore, those nearby will have no reason not to obey, and those far away will have no reason not to submit.
"Now, from the time of Da Bi and Bo Shi until the present, the Quanrong tribe have come to court with their tribute. The Son of Heaven said: 'I will certainly punish them for failing to offer tribute, and show them my military might.' Is it not that you are abandoning the teachings of the former kings, and the royal foundation is about to falter! I have heard that the Quanrong tribe sincerely follow the old virtues, and uphold their principles consistently and firmly. They have the means to resist us!"
The king did not listen, and so campaigned against them, obtaining four white wolves and four white deer to bring back. From then on, those in the distant territories did not come to court.
1.2 "The Mother of Duke Kang of Mi Discusses How a Petty Person Who Acquires Too Much Will Inevitably Perish"
Duke Gong was traveling on the Jing River, and Duke Mi Kang followed him. Three women ran to him. Their mother said: "You must present them to the king. Beasts gather in groups of three, people gather in crowds of three, and women in threes are beautiful. When the king hunts, he does not take a whole herd, when a duke travels, he does not take all the commoners, and when the king takes wives, he does not include an entire clan. These beautiful women are things of beauty. The people offer you beautiful things, but what virtue do you have to bear them? Even the king could not bear this, how much less a petty fellow like you? When a petty fellow possesses fine things, he will surely perish in the end." Duke Kang did not present them. One year later, the king destroyed Mi.
1.3 "Duke Shao Admonishes King Li to Stop Slander"
King Li was cruel, and the people of the country slandered the king. Duke Shao announced, "The people cannot endure their fate!" The king was angry, and obtained a sorcerer from Wei. He ordered him to monitor those who criticized, and to report them, whereupon they would be killed. The people of the kingdom dared not speak, and exchanged glances on the roads. The king was pleased, and told Duke Shao, "I have been able to stop criticism; they now dare not speak." Duke Shao said, "This is blocking them. Preventing the people's mouths is more dangerous than preventing a river. If a river is blocked and bursts, it will certainly injure many people; the people are the same. Therefore, those who manage rivers dredge them to guide the water, and those who govern the people encourage them to speak. Therefore, when the Son of Heaven listens to government, he causes dukes and ministers down to lower officials to present poems, blind musicians to present songs, historians to present books, instructors to offer admonitions, blind singers to recite odes, blind reciters to chant, The blind recite, the artisans remonstrate, the common people spread the word, the close ministers offer their advice, the relatives make up for omissions and observe, the blind musicians and historians teach and instruct, the elders and experienced men improve upon it, and then the king deliberates upon it. Therefore, affairs are carried out without going astray. The people having mouths is like the land having mountains and rivers; wealth and resources come forth from it. It is like the low-lying wetlands having fertile soil; clothing and food are produced from it. Words spoken from the mouth, good or bad, arise from them. To practice good and prepare against bad, is how to enrich resources and clothing and food. Now, the people deliberate in their hearts and express it from their mouths, accomplishing it and carrying it out. How can this be blocked? If you block their mouths, how much can you achieve with them?" The king did not listen. Thereupon, no one in the state dared to speak out. After three years, they exiled the king to Zhì.
1.4 *Ruì Liángfū's Discourse on Róng Yígōng's Monopoly*
King Lì favored Róng Yígōng. Ruì Liángfū said: "The royal house will soon decline! Now, Róng Yígōng loves monopolies and does not understand the great danger. Now, profit is what gives rise to the myriad things, and is what Heaven and Earth sustain. But if someone monopolizes it, the harm will be great. Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things will all draw from it. How can it be monopolized? What provokes much resentment, yet he does not prepare against great danger. To teach the king in this way, how can the king last long? Now, a king, should guide profit and distribute it to those above and below, so that spirits, men, and all things all obtain their due. Even then, he should be fearful and cautious, afraid that resentment will come. Therefore, the *Odes* say: 'Thoughtful and cultivated was Hou Ji, able to match that Heaven. He established our many people, none did not conform to your standard.'" The *Da Ya* says: "He presented his offerings and bore the charge of Zhou." Was this not because he did not spread profit and feared difficulty? Therefore, he was able to bear the charge of Zhou up to the present day. Now, if the king studies to monopolize profit, is that permissible? If even a common man monopolizes profit, he is still called a thief. If the king practices this, his prospects are few indeed. If Rong Gong is employed, Zhou will surely fail." Later, Rong Gong became a high minister, the feudal lords did not present tribute, and the king was exiled to Zhi.
1.5 *Shao Gong Sacrificed His Son to Save King Xuan*
During the rebellion in Zhi, King Xuan was in Shao Gong's palace, and the people of the state surrounded it. Shao Gong said: "In the past, I repeatedly admonished the king, but the king did not listen, and that is why this difficulty has arisen. Now, if I kill the prince, Will the king consider me an enemy and be angered? To serve a ruler, one must be forthright without animosity, resentful without anger, how much more so when serving a king?" Thereupon, he had his son replace King Xuan, and when King Xuan grew up, he installed him.
1.6 *Duke Wen of Guo Admonishes King Xuan Against Not Plowing the Thousand Acres*
King Xuan ascended the throne, and did not plow the thousand acres. Duke Wen of Guo admonished him, saying: "This is not permissible. For the great affair of the people lies in agriculture, the offerings to God come from this, the abundance of the people comes from this, the supplies for affairs are dependent on this, harmony and concord originate from this, the prosperity of wealth and resources begins from this, abundance, solidity and purity are achieved from this, therefore, the Minister of Agriculture is a great official. In ancient times, the Grand Historian observed the seasons and surveyed the land, when the yang energy was vigorous and full, and the earth's qi vibrated and erupted, and the agricultural signs appeared in the morning, and the sun and moon were at the Heavenly Temple, then the farmers began to exert their strength.
"Nine days before the appointed time, the Grand Scribe informed Ji, saying: 'From now until the first auspicious day, all the yang energy will rise and steam, and the fertility of the soil will move. If it is not stirred and not changed, its veins will be full of calamities, and the grain will not grow.' Ji told the King, saying: 'The Scribe, leading the officials in charge of yang affairs, instructed me, the one in charge of affairs, saying: "Nine days from now, the soil will move together. The King must reverently purify himself, and oversee the farmers without fail."'" The King then ordered the Minister of Education to warn all dukes, ministers, officials, and commoners. The Minister of Works cleared the altar for the ploughing ceremony, and ordered the agricultural officials to prepare all farming implements.
"Five days before the appointed time, the blind musicians announced the arrival of harmonious winds. The King then went to the fasting palace, and all the officials attended to their duties, each remaining in their respective fasting quarters for three days. The King then purely washed and offered sweet wine. When the appointed time arrived, The libationer offers the fragrant sacrificial wine (chàng). The sacrificial official offers the sweet wine (lǐ). The king pours out the fragrant wine as a libation. Then, after the offering of the sweet wine, he proceeds. All the officials, and the common people, completely follow. When it comes to the first plowing (jí), Houji oversees it. The cook and the agricultural supervisor present the ceremony of the plowing. The grand scribe assists the king. The king respectfully follows (the instructions). The king plows one furrow (fá). He shares in the plowing, completing three (furrows). The common people complete (the plowing of) a thousand mu. Then Houji examines the results, the grand scribe oversees it. The minister of education examines the people, the grand tutor oversees it. When it is finished, the steward presents the offerings, the chief cook oversees it. The cook assists the king. The king enjoys the great sacrifice (dà láo). He shares in the tasting. The common people finish eating.
"On this day, the blind musicians The music officials used (music) to influence the local customs. Grain was stored southeast of the registry and preserved in bell-shaped containers. It was then distributed to the farmers according to the seasons. Ji then extensively instructed the people, recorded agricultural achievements, and harmonized labor. He said: “Yin and yang are distributed, and thunder rumbles forth to dispel stagnation.” If the land is not fully cultivated, the punishment lies with the Minister of Justice. Then he ordered his subordinates, saying: “Inspect: The agricultural teacher inspects it once, the agricultural director inspects it twice, Hou Ji inspects it three times, the Minister of Works inspects it four times, the Minister of Education inspects it five times, the Grand Protector inspects it six times, the Grand Tutor inspects it seven times, the Grand Scribe inspects it eight times, the Minister of Rites inspects it nine times, and the king then makes a grand inspection. Weeding and harvesting are also done in this way.” The people were all stirred into action, diligently and respectfully engaging in agriculture, repairing their field boundaries, and constantly using their hoes, Not understanding the times, yet material resources were not lacking, and the people lived in harmony.
"In those times, the king's affairs focused solely on agriculture, and no one sought profit through their office to interfere with agricultural work. Three seasons were devoted to farming, and one season to military training. Therefore, when campaigning, there was power; when defending, there were resources. If this is the case, then one can please the gods and harmonize with the people. Then sacrifices will be timely and distributions will be generous.
Now, Your Majesty wishes to follow the path of the former kings but abandons their great achievements, diminishes offerings to the gods, impoverishes sacrifices, and exhausts the people's wealth. How then will you seek blessings and employ the people?"
The king did not listen. In the thirty-ninth year, they fought at Qianmu, and the king's army was utterly defeated by the Rong of the Jiang clan.
1.7 Zhongshan Fu Advises King Xuan Against Establishing a Concubine
Duke Wu of Lu presented Kuo and Xi to the king. The king established Xi (as a concubine). Fan Zhongshan's father remonstrated, saying: "He cannot be established! If he is not compliant, he will certainly offend. If he offends the king's command, he will certainly be punished. Therefore, an order must be followed. If orders are not carried out, government will not be established. If carried out but not obeyed, the people will abandon their ruler. That the lower serves the higher, and the younger serves the elder, is the reason for compliance. Now the Son of Heaven establishes feudal lords and sets up their younger, this is teaching rebellion. If Lu follows this and the feudal lords imitate it, the king's commands will be obstructed. If you do not follow it and punish them, it is punishing the king's command yourself. In this matter, punishing is also a mistake, not punishing is also a mistake, may the Son of Heaven consider it carefully!" The king eventually established him. The Marquis of Lu returned and died, and the people of Lu killed Duke Yi and established Bo Yu.
1.8 "Mu Zhong Discusses the Marquis of Lu's Filial Piety"
In the spring of the thirty-second year, King Xuan attacked Lu and established Duke Xiao. From then on, the feudal lords were not harmonious. King Xuan wanted to find someone among the sons of the states who was capable of guiding and instructing the feudal lords. Fan Muzhong said, "The Marquis of Lu, Xiao, is capable." The King said, "How do you know this?" He replied, "He is reverent and respectful to the spirits and respectfully serves the elders; in assigning tasks and administering punishments, he always asks about the teachings of the past and consults the old records; he does not interfere with what he asks, nor does he violate what he consults." The King said, "In that case, he is capable of instructing and governing his people." Therefore, he summoned Duke Kao of Lu to the Yi Palace.
1.9 Zhongshan Gong Advises King Xuan Against Counting the People
King Xuan, having lost the army in the southern states, then counted the people in Taiyuan. Zhongshan Fu remonstrated, saying, "The people cannot be counted! In ancient times, they did not count the people but knew their number; the Simin coordinated the orphans and the bereaved, the Sishang coordinated the people's surnames, The Minister of Education coordinates travelers, the Minister of Justice coordinates the licentious, the Pasture Official coordinates occupations, the Minister of Works coordinates leatherworking, the Market Official coordinates entry, the Granary Official coordinates exit. In this way, the small and the large, death and life, going out and coming in, comings and goings, all can be known. Then, furthermore, examine them through affairs. The king manages agriculture in the tax fields, and hunts during the agricultural off-season; weeding and harvesting are also done in the tax fields, and autumn hunts are conducted after the summer sacrifice, and winter hunts are conducted after the harvest is complete. These are all ways of becoming familiar with the people's numbers, so what else is there to count? Not considering them few and yet excessively counting them, is to show (the people) "few" and to dislike affairs. If governing demonstrates "few," the feudal lords will avoid him. If governing dislikes affairs, there will be no way to issue orders. Moreover, counting the people without a reason is what Heaven dislikes, harmful to governance and detrimental to descendants." The king ultimately counted them, and King You was then overthrown.
1.10 "The Three Rivers of Western Zhou All Shook, and Boyang Fu Discussed the Impending Fall of Zhou"
In the second year of King You, the three rivers of Western Zhou all shook. Boyang Fu said: "Zhou is about to perish! The qi of Heaven and Earth does not lose its order; if it exceeds its order, the people will be thrown into chaos. When the yang lies hidden and cannot emerge, and the yin presses and cannot rise, then there are earthquakes. Now the three rivers have truly shaken, which means the yang has lost its place and is suppressing the yin. When the yang loses its place and is in the yin, the sources of the rivers will surely be blocked; when the sources are blocked, the state will surely perish. Now, water and earth flow, and the people use them. ( If) the earth has nothing to flow, the people will lack resources and supplies; if it does not perish, what are we waiting for? In the past, when the Yi and Luo dried up, Xia perished; when the Yellow River dried up, Shang perished. Now, the virtue of the Zhou is like the end of the second dynasty, its rivers and sources are also blocked, what is blocked will surely be exhausted. A state must rely on mountains and rivers, when mountains collapse and rivers dry up, it is a sign of destruction. When rivers dry up, mountains will surely collapse. If the state perishes, it will be no more than ten years, for it is the limit of the cycle. What Heaven abandons will not exceed its limit." In that year, the Three Rivers dried up, and Mount Qi collapsed. Eleven years later, King You was then overthrown, and the Zhou then moved eastward.
1.11 Duke Li of Zheng and Uncle Guo Killed Zi Tui and Installed King Hui
In the second year of King Hui, Bian Bo, Shi Su, and Wei Guo expelled the king and established Zi Tui. The king stayed in Zheng for three years. Prince Tui made the three grand officers drink wine, Zi Guo was the guest, Music and ubiquitous dancing. Duke Li of Zheng met with Uncle Guo and said, "I have heard that when the Minister of Justice carries out executions, the ruler refrains from feasting; how much more should he avoid rejoicing in disaster! Now I hear that Zi Tui sings and dances without cease, rejoicing in disaster. To expel the king and usurp his position, what disaster could be greater! To forget worry when facing disaster is called rejoicing in disaster. Disaster will surely befall him; why not welcome back the king?" Uncle Guo agreed. The Earl of Zheng brought the king in through the Yu Gate, Uncle Guo entered through the North Gate, and they killed Zi Tui and three great officers, and then the king entered.
1.12 "The Inner Historian Guo Discusses Spirits"
In the fifteenth year, a spirit descended in Xin. The king asked the Inner Historian Guo, "What is the reason for this? Has this happened before?" He replied, "It exists. When a state is about to rise, its ruler is upright and intelligent, sincere and just, refined and pure, kind and harmonious. His virtue is sufficient to manifest his fragrant offerings, his benevolence is sufficient to unite his people. The spirits enjoy it and the people listen, the people and spirits have no grievances. Therefore, the enlightened spirits descend to him, observing his governance and virtue, and evenly distributing blessings. When a state is about to perish, its ruler is greedy and covetous, perverse and wicked, licentious and dissolute, negligent and indolent, crude and filthy, violent and tyrannical. His governance is foul and putrid, fragrant offerings do not ascend, his punishments are false and deceitful, the people are alienated and divided. The enlightened spirits do not purify (him), and the people have distant aspirations. The people and spirits resent and grieve, having nowhere to rely on or find solace. Therefore, the spirits also depart, Observing their harsh and evil deeds, it sends down calamity upon them. Therefore, sometimes a spirit is seen to bring rise, and sometimes to bring ruin. In the past, when the Xia dynasty was rising, Rong descended upon Mount Chong; when it was falling, Hui Lu was believed to reside in Ting Sui. When the Shang dynasty was rising, Taowu resided on Mount Pi; when it was falling, the Yi sheep was at pasture. When the Zhou dynasty was rising, the Yuezhuo bird cried on Mount Qi; when it was declining, Du Bo shot the king in Hao. These are all manifestations of the will of the clear spirits."
The king said: "What spirit is it now?" He replied: "In the past, King Zhao married a woman from Fang, called the Queen of Fang, who truly had flawed virtue, and aligned herself with Danzhu. Danzhu possessed her body to take control of her, and she gave birth to King Mu. It is this spirit that oversees the descendants of Zhou and brings fortune and misfortune upon them. A spirit is singular, Not far off is the move and relocation. If viewed from this perspective, could it be the spirit of Danzhu?" The King said, "Who will receive it?" He replied, "It resides in the land of Guo." The King said, "Then what will it do?" He replied, "I have heard it said: To obtain divine favor through the proper path is called encountering good fortune; to obtain divine favor through excess is called coveting disaster. Now Guo is somewhat desolate; will it perish?" The King said, "What should I do about it?" He replied, "Send the Grand Steward with the prayer-officials and scribes, leading the Li surname people, bearing sacrificial animals, offerings of millet and rice, and jade and silk to offer them, without making any prayers."
The King said, "How long will Guo last?" He replied: "In the past, Yao governed the people by five [virtues]; now that his descendant appears, it is a manifestation of the spirit, but it will not exceed its [natural] term. If we judge by this, it will not exceed five years." The king sent the Grand Steward Jifu to lead the Fu clan, as well as the invocators and historians, to offer sacrifices and jade libation vessels to Guo. The Inner Historian Guo followed along to Guo; the Duke of Guo also sent invocators and historians to request territory. The Inner Historian Guo returned, and reported to the king, saying: "Guo is certain to perish. They do not offer pure sacrifices to the spirits but seek blessings, the spirits will surely bring disaster upon them; they are not close to the people but seek their service, the people will surely disobey them. To offer with a pure heart, is to make a pure sacrifice; to kindly protect the common people, is to be close to them. Now the Duke of Guo constantly exhausts the people to indulge his extravagance, alienating the people and angering the spirits while seeking gain, is this not difficult!" Year nineteen, Jin took Guo.
1.13 "The Inner Scribe Guo Discusses Why Duke Hui of Jin Will Surely Have No Successor"
King Xiang sent Shao Gong Guo and the Inner Scribe Guo to bestow an order upon Duke Hui of Jin. Lü Sheng and Xi Rui, assisting the Marquis of Jin, were disrespectful. The Marquis of Jin held the jade low, and bowed without touching his head to the ground.
The Inner Scribe Guo returned, and reported to the King, saying: "If Jin does not perish, its ruler will surely have no successor. Moreover, Lü and Xi will not escape [punishment]." The King said: "Why?" He replied: "The *Xia Shu* has it, saying: 'If the multitude does not support the primary ruler, whom will they uphold? If the ruler does not support the multitude, there will be none to defend the state.' In the *Oath of Tang* it says: 'If I, the one man, am guilty, let it not involve the myriad people; "If the myriad people are guilty, the fault lies with me alone." In the "Pan Geng" it says: "If the state is good, it is due to you all. If the state is not good, the fault lies with me alone, and I shall receive the punishment for negligence." Thus, in governing the multitude and employing the people, one must be cautious. What the people urgently need lies in important matters. The former kings knew that important matters must be accomplished by benefiting the multitude. Therefore, they purified their hearts to harmonize and show kindness to the people. They examined what was central and measured what was equitable to approach them. They illuminated and clarified the standards of things to instruct them. They established righteousness that would be widely trusted and then implemented it. Purifying their hearts is purity; examining what is central and measuring what is equitable is loyalty; illuminating and clarifying the standards of things is ritual; establishing righteousness that is widely trusted is trustworthiness. Therefore, the way to govern the multitude and employ the people cannot be harmonious without purity, cannot be established without loyalty, To act contrary to propriety will not lead to harmony; To act without trustworthiness will not lead to progress. Now that the Marquis of Jin has ascended the throne and renounced the tributes paid to both external and internal parties, and mistreats those residing within his borders, he has abandoned his trustworthiness; by not respecting the King's commands, he has abandoned propriety; by inflicting what is detested on others, he has abandoned his loyalty; by filling his heart with wickedness, he has abandoned his sincerity. Having abandoned all four of these, then those from afar will not come, and those nearby will not be at peace; with what will he defend his state?
"In ancient times, after the former kings possessed the empire, they also deeply revered and served the High God [上帝] and the enlightened spirits [明神].
Consequently, they had morning sun [朝日] and evening moon [夕月] sacrifices to teach the people to serve their ruler.
The feudal lords received their responsibilities from the king in the spring and autumn to govern their people. The high officials and lower officers carefully maintained their positions daily to warn their subordinates. The common people, artisans, and merchants each adhered to their professions to serve their superiors. They were still afraid that there might be failures or losses, so they created carriages and clothing, Banners and flags are used to signal them; gifts and tribute, and auspicious tokens are used to secure them; ranks and titles, and distinctions of nobility and lowliness are used to array them; good commands and fine reputations are used to proclaim them. Still, there are those who scatter, move away, or become lax and negligent, and these are recorded in the penal laws and exiled to distant lands. From this, we have the countries of the barbarians, and peoples subject to axes and knives and ink marks (branding), how much less can one indulge their own desires?
"Now, the Marquis of Jin did not inherit his position, but obtained it. He is diligent, cautious, and fearful, entrusting responsibilities with vigilance and apprehension, yet still says it is not enough. If he were to broaden his ambition and alienate his neighbors, oppress his people and belittle his superiors, how would he secure his position?
"To hold jade is to show humility, and to neglect one's tribute is to fail in one's obligations; to bow without touching one's head to the ground is to deceive one's ruler. To replace the established offerings is to have no stability; to deceive the king is to have no people. For the affairs of Heaven follow constant patterns, and those who bear heavy responsibilities and enjoy great benefits will surely be reached quickly [by consequences]. Therefore, if the lord of Jin deceives the king, others will also deceive him; if he desires to replace his established offerings, others will also replace him. The high officials who enjoy their emoluments and do not remonstrate but flatter him will also surely be reached [by consequences]."
King Xiang in his third year established the lord of Jin [as a hegemon]; in his eighth year, he died in Han; in his seventeenth year, the people of Jin killed Duke Huai. Duke Huai had no descendants; the people of Qin killed Zi Jin and Zi Gong.
1.14 "The Intendant of the Interior Xing Argues That Duke Wen of Jin Will Certainly Become a Hegemon."
King Xiang sent the Grand Steward Wen Gong and the Intendant of the Interior Xing to bestow investiture upon Duke Wen of Jin. The highest minister greeted them at the border; the lord of Jin performed a suburban labor offering; he lodged them in the ancestral temple; he presented nine pens of sacrificial animals; he set up torches in the courtyard. When the day arrived, He was bidden to the Martial Temple. A mulberry wood stand was set up. Tables and mats were arranged. The Grand Steward oversaw it. The Marquis of Jin, in proper attire, entered. The Grand Steward, with the king's mandate, bestowed the ceremonial robes. The Inner Scribe assisted him. After three pronouncements, he then donned the ceremonial robes. Once this was completed, the welcoming, the feasting, the gifting, and the farewells were done according to the rites for a duke or marquis, and were augmented with a friendly banquet. The Inner Scribe eagerly returned, and reported to the king, saying: "Jin must be treated well. Its ruler will surely become a hegemon. He meets the king's commands with reverence, and completes them by upholding ritual and righteousness. Reverencing the king's commands is following the proper path; completing ritual and righteousness is the standard of virtue. If he guides the feudal lords with virtue, the feudal lords will surely return to him. Moreover, ritual is how one observes loyalty, trustworthiness, benevolence, and righteousness. Loyalty is the means of distribution; benevolence is the means of action; trustworthiness is the means of guarding; righteousness is the means of moderation. If loyalty distributes fairly, if benevolence is acted upon, it will be rewarded; if trustworthiness is guarded, it will be secure; if righteousness is moderate, it will be measured. If distribution is fair, there will be no resentment; if action is rewarded, there will be no lack; if guarding is secure, there will be no negligence; if moderation is measured, there will be no disharmony. If the people do not resent and wealth is not lacking, if commands are not negligent and actions are not disharmonious, what affair will not be accomplished! That the inner aligns with the outer is loyalty; bestowing benefits according to the three categories of clothing is benevolence; guarding one's principles and not being excessive is trustworthiness; conducting rituals without fault is righteousness. When your servant entered the borders of Jin, these four were not lost, therefore your servant said: "The Marquis of Jin knows propriety, may the king approve of him! If you plant with propriety, the people will surely be prosperous."
The king followed his advice. Those sent as envoys to Jin encountered each other on the road. When the disaster of the Queen Hui occurred, the king fled to Zheng, and the Marquis of Jin received him.
In the seventeenth year of King Xiang, he established Duke Wen of Jin. In the twenty-first year, he had the lords pay homage to the king at Hengyong, and presented the spoils of victory over Chu. He then held the alliance of Jiantu, and from this he began to achieve hegemony.
1.15 *Fu Chen Admonishes King Xiang Regarding Using the Di to Attack Zheng and Making a Di Woman His Queen*
In the thirteenth year of King Xiang, the people of Zheng attacked Hua. The king sent You Sunbo to plead for Hua, but the people of Zheng seized him. The king was angry and planned to use the Di to attack Zheng. Fu Chen admonished, saying: "This is not permissible. The ancients had a saying: "When brothers slander and quarrel, others will insult them from a hundred *li* away." The *Book of Poetry* of Duke Wen of Zhou says: "Brothers may quarrel within the walls, but together they will resist external insults." If this is so, then quarreling is an internal insult, and even though they quarrel, they do not ruin the bond of kinship. Zheng is to the Son of Heaven as a brother. Zheng Wu and Zheng Zhuang had great meritorious service during the reigns of Ping and Huan; when our Zhou moved east, Jin and Zheng were the ones we relied on; the rebellion of Prince Tui was also put down by Zheng. Now, to abandon them because of a minor resentment is to put a great favor aside for a small grievance, is it not unseemly? Moreover, the resentment of brothers should not be sought elsewhere; to seek it elsewhere is to allow advantage to fall to outsiders. To publicize resentment and grant profit to outsiders is unrighteous; to abandon relatives and cleave to the barbarians is inauspicious; to repay kindness with resentment Is unbenevolent. Now, righteousness is that by which profit is generated; auspiciousness is that by which the spirits are served; benevolence is that by which the people are protected. If there is no righteousness, then profit will not be abundant; if there is no auspiciousness, then blessings will not descend; if there is no benevolence, then the people will not come. The enlightened kings of old did not lose these three virtues, therefore, they were able to gloriously possess the world and harmoniously pacify the common people, so that their good reputation was not forgotten. Your Majesty, you cannot discard them." The king did not listen. In the seventeenth year, the king brought down Di troops to attack Zheng.
The king favored the Di people and was going to make their daughter his queen. Fu Chen remonstrated, saying: "This is not permissible. Marriage is the step to fortune and misfortune. Following it, if the benefit is internal, then there is fortune; if the benefit is external, then misfortune is taken. Now, Your Majesty benefits externally, is it not perhaps stepping towards misfortune? In the past, Zhi and Chou were established through Da Ren; Qi and Zeng through Da Si; Qi, Xu, Shen, and Lü through Da Jiang; Chen through Da Ji; these all were able to internally benefit their relatives. When officials are not replaced frequently, wealth does not become depleted, every request is fulfilled, every action is successful. The common people, all bring benefits and return them to their superiors, this is internal benefit. If the Seven Virtues are separated and divided, the people will be of two minds, each withdrawing for their own benefit, superiors' requests will not reach them, this is external benefit. The Di tribes were not ranked in the royal court, and Zheng Bo was in the south. To treat them as king yet demean them is to fail to respect the noble. The Di have the nature of wolves and jackals, Zheng had not lost the Zhou customs, to treat them as king yet despise them is to fail to recognize the worthy. Kings Ping, Huan, Zhuang, and Hui all received the labor of Zheng, to treat them as king yet abandon them is to fail to reward merit. Zheng Bo Jie's teeth are old, to treat him as king yet weaken him is to fail to honor the elderly. The Di are of the Kui lineage, Zheng originated from King Xuan, but the king mistreated them. This is not loving one's relatives. Now, in ritual, the new should not exclude the old. The king used a Di woman to estrange Jiang and Ren. This is not ritual, and it is also abandoning the old. With one action, the king abandoned seven virtues. Therefore, your servant said it was "profiting the outsiders." The *Book* says: "There must be forbearance, if one is to succeed." The king did not forbear a small anger and abandoned Zheng, and even elevated Shu Wei to provide a ladder for the Di. The Di are like great boars and wolves; they can never be satisfied." The king did not listen.
In the seventeenth year, the king deposed the Di queen. The Di people came and killed Tan Bo. Fu Chen said: "In the past, I repeatedly remonstrated with the king, but the king did not listen, and thus this calamity has come about. If I do not go out [to fight], Does the king consider me an enemy!" Thereupon, he had his subordinates kill him.
Initially, Queen Hui wanted to establish Prince Dai, so she used her party to incite the Di people. The Di people then invaded, and the Zhou king fled, residing in Zheng, where Duke Wen of Jin received him.
1.16 "King Xiang Refuses Duke Wen of Jin's Request for a Tunnel"
After Duke Wen of Jin had settled King Xiang in Jia, the king rewarded him with land. He declined and requested a tunnel. The king did not permit it, saying, "In the past, when our former kings possessed the world, they measured a square of a thousand li to form the royal domain, in order to provide for the sacrifices to God, the mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits, to prepare for the needs of the common people, and to await the troubles of the disobedient and the unforeseen. The remainder was equally divided among dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons, so that each had a peaceful dwelling, in order to comply with Heaven and Earth, and not encounter disasters, how would the former kings have relied on that? The number of inner officials does not exceed the Nine Concubines, and the number of outer officials does not exceed the Nine Ranks, sufficient only to provide for the spirits. How dare I indulge my senses, desires, and inner circle to disrupt the established order? It is only through the garments and insignia of life and death that I govern the common people, distributing them according to their importance. How is this different for the king? Now Heaven has sent down calamity upon the House of Zhou, and I, the One Man, can barely maintain my position. Moreover, I am not so virtuous as to burden my uncle by distributing the great treasures of the former kings as rewards for private merits. My uncle would surely resent this, considering it inappropriate for me, the One Man. How dare I indulge such favoritism? The ancient people had a saying: "Change the jade, change the ways." If my uncle can greatly expand his virtue and change his surname and possessions to create a new order for the world, his merit will be self-evident. But if he merely takes these treasures to pacify the people, then I, the One Man, will flee to the distant lands, and what excuse could I offer? If he remains of the Ji surname, he should still be ranked among the dukes and marquises to restore the duties of the former kings. The great treasures should not be changed lightly. My uncle should diligently cultivate his clear virtue; the treasures will come naturally. How dare I, with my personal efforts, alter the great ordinances of the past, and disgrace the world? What would become of the former kings and the people? What would be the purpose of government orders? If it were not so, and my uncle had land and a tunnel there, how would I possibly know it?" Duke Wen then did not dare to request it, accepted the land and returned.
1.17 "The People of Yang Do Not Submit to the Marquis of Jin"
The King returned from Zheng, and bestowed Yangfan upon Duke Wen of Jin. The people of Yang did not submit, so the Marquis of Jin besieged them. Cang Ge called out, saying: "The King considered the Lord of Jin to be capable of virtue, therefore he rewarded him with Yangfan. Yangfan cherishes the King's virtue, and therefore has not yet submitted to Jin. What virtue does the Lord intend to display in order to comfort and pacify us, so that we may have no further aspirations? Now you are about to utterly destroy our ancestral temples and slaughter our people. It is right that we dare not submit! The forces of the army are employed to seek out the arrogant and disrespectful The Rong and Di tribes are arrogant, dissolute, and irreverent, and therefore invite military action. These weaklings are the people of Yang, not yet accustomed to Your Lordship's governance, and thus have not accepted Your Lordship's orders. If Your Lordship extends kindness to them, and only demands tribute through officials, how would they dare to defy Your Lordship's orders? How could they be worthy of disgracing Your Lordship's army! Your Lordship's military might is overwhelming, but is it not being trifled with and blunted? Your servant has heard it said: "Military force should not be displayed, and civil virtue should not be hidden. Displaying military force without achieving brilliance, hiding civil virtue without making it manifest." The people of Yang have not been granted the opportunity to present tribute, and are only being met with displays of military force, which is why Your servant is fearful. Otherwise, how would they dare to love themselves (more than Your Lordship)? Moreover, the people of Yang, are they not also descendants (of the royal family)? They are all fathers, brothers, nephews, and uncles of the Son of Heaven. How can they be treated so cruelly?" The Marquis of Jin heard this and said, "These are the words of a gentleman." Therefore, he released the people of Yang.
1.18 *Duke Xiang Refuses to Kill Duke Cheng of Wei*
At the meeting of Wen, the people of Jin seized Duke Cheng of Wei and returned him to Zhou. The Marquis of Jin requested to kill him, but the King said, "It is not permissible. Governance comes from above. When the superior makes policy, and the inferior implements it without resistance, then superiors and inferiors have no grievances. Now, Uncle makes policy, but it is not implemented; is that not impermissible? There should be no litigation between ruler and subject. Now, although Yuan Xuan is in the right, he cannot be listened to. If ruler and subject both litigate, fathers and sons will litigate; this is without order. And Uncle, if you listen to him, that is one act of disobedience. Moreover, to have a subject kill his ruler, why would you employ punishments? To promulgate punishments and not employ them is a second act of disobedience. To assemble the lords once and again conducts government in a way that goes against the grain, I fear that he will have no descendants. If not, why would I have a private agenda regarding the Marquis of Wei?" The people of Jin then returned the Marquis of Wei.
1.19 *Wang Sun Man Observes the Qin Army*
In the twenty-fourth year, the Qin army was about to attack Zheng, passing by the north gate of Zhou. Those on the left and right all removed their helmets and dismounted to bow, but three hundred chariots sped past without dismounting. Wang Sun Man observed this and said to the king, "The Qin army will surely have a misadventure." The king said, "Why?" He replied, "The army is frivolous and arrogant. Being frivolous means few plans, being arrogant means no propriety. Without propriety they will be detached, with few plans they will fall into danger themselves. Entering danger and yet detached, how can they avoid defeat? If the Qin army has no misadventure, then the Way has been abandoned." On this journey, the Qin army retreated, but the Jin people defeated them at Xiao, capturing their three commanders, Bing, Shu, and Shi.
1.20 "King Ding's Argument Against Using Whole Steamed Offerings"
The Marquis of Jin sent Sui Hui to Zhou on a diplomatic mission. King Ding entertained him with a *yao zheng* steamed offering. Lord Yuan assisted in the ceremony. Fan Zi spoke privately to Lord Yuan, saying, "I have heard that the rites of the royal house have no destruction or breakage. What kind of rite is this now?" The King overheard his words, summoned Lord Yuan and questioned him about it. Lord Yuan told him the truth.
The King summoned Shi Ji, and said, "Have you not heard that in the matters of the *di* sacrifice and suburban sacrifice, there are whole steamed offerings (*quan zheng*); when kings and dukes hold establishment banquets (*li yu*), there are chamber steamed offerings (*fang zheng*); when relatives have feasts and banquets, there are *yao zheng* steamed offerings. Now, you are not like others. Your uncle has sent Shi Ji to come and truly restore the old virtues, in order to assist the royal house. It is only the banquet rites of the former kings that I wish to bestow upon you. How could I, the one person, dare to set up a feast and sacrifice, with loyalty that is not based on family affection, and interfere with old duties, so as to disrupt previous harmony? Moreover, only the Rong and Di have the practice of presenting the raw offering. The Rong and Di are reckless, disrespectful, and intrusive, greedy and unyielding. Their blood and qi are ungoverned, like birds and beasts. When they come regularly to offer tribute, they do not wait for fragrant and delicious flavors. Therefore, they are seated outside the gate, and we send interpreters to pass on the physical offerings to them. Now, you are one of the few brothers of our royal house, meeting from time to time. We will harmonize and agree on the proper rituals, in order to show the people models and rules. Should we not choose the gentle and good, select the fragrant, purify the wine and sweet wine, arrange the hundred platters, They repair the food containers and sacrificial vessels, present the sacrificial animals, set out the wine vessels, arrange the tripods and stands for offerings, cleanse the cloths and covers, respectfully perform the purifications, disassemble the sacrificial animal piece by piece and share the food and drink together. Thus, there are the arrangements of food on stands, the exchanging of gifts and banqueting, in order to show acceptance and harmony. How could it be that one stands alone, emulating the Rong and Di barbarians?
"Now, the banquets of kings, dukes, and princes are intended to discuss affairs and establish regulations, to establish great virtue and make great things manifest. Therefore, they establish complete rites and offer sacrifices in due season. Banquets are used to display objects, feasts are used to foster harmony. Therefore, the yearly banquets are not tiring, the seasonal feasts are not excessive, the monthly meetings, the decadal reviews, the daily completion are not forgotten. The clothing and objects display merit, the colors and decorations are clearly visible, the patterns and designs are allegorical, His movements were orderly and harmonious, his appearance was dignified, his deportment had rules, the five flavors nourished the vital energy, the five colors concentrated the spirit, the five sounds manifested virtue, the five principles recorded what was appropriate, food and drink were fit to be offered, harmony and concord were worthy of observation, resources were praiseworthy. Thus, compliance led to the establishment of virtue. The ancients who were skilled in ritual, what need did they have for complete steaming?"
Wu Zi then did not dare to answer and withdrew. Upon returning, he studied and collected the rituals of the three dynasties, and consequently, he revised the holding of office to become the law of Jin.
1.21 "Shan Xiangong Discusses How Chen Will Surely Perish"
King Ding sent Shan Xiangong on a mission to Song. He then borrowed a road through Chen in order to travel to Chu. It was already the time of the Fire Star's morning visibility, the road was overgrown and impassable, scouts were not stationed at the borders, the Minister of Works did not inspect the roads, the marshes were not dammed, The rivers are not bridged, the fields have accumulated grain, the work in the threshing floor is not yet finished, the roads have no rows of trees, the reclaimed fields are like gardens, the kitchen officer does not deliver rations, the village administrator does not provide lodging, the state has no places for travelers to stay, the county has no alms-houses, the people will build a platform at the house of the Xia clan. When they arrived at Chen, Duke Ling of Chen, along with Kong Ning, and Yi Xingfu, dressed in southern caps went to the house of the Xia clan, but were not received as guests.
Shan Zi returned and reported to the king, saying: "If the Marquis of Chen does not have a great fault, then his state must perish." The king said: "What is the reason?" He replied: "When the stars of Chen and Jiao appear, the rains cease; when the Heavenly Root star appears, the waters dry up; when the root appears, the grass and trees shed their knots; when the star Si appears, frost falls; when the Fire star appears, a clear wind warns of cold. Therefore, the teachings of the former kings say: "After the rain stops, the roads are cleared; when the water recedes, bridges are built; when the grass and trees shed their leaves, preparations are made for storage; when frost falls, winter furs are readied; when cool winds arrive, city walls and palaces are repaired." Therefore, the *Xia Calendar* says: "In the ninth month, clear the roads; in the tenth month, build bridges." The seasonal warnings say: "Gather and complete the threshing floor work; Prepare baskets and shovels; Within the planned buildings, earthworks will begin. When the fire star first appears, report it to the Sili (officials in charge of districts)." This is how the former kings did not rely on wealth and treasures, but broadly bestowed virtue upon the world. Now in the state of Chen, the fire star has appeared, yet the roads are as if blocked, the fields are as if abandoned, the marshes are not dammed and protected, the rivers have no boats or bridges. This is abandoning the teachings of the former kings.
"The Zhou system had it that: 'Rows of trees are planted to mark the roads, village inns are established to guard the roads. The state has suburban pastures, The borders had defensive overlooks, the marshes had nurseries of grasses, the parks had forests and ponds— all for the purpose of warding off disasters. The remaining land was all grain-producing soil; the people had no idle plows; the fields had no hidden weeds. They did not seize the people's time, nor did they scorn the people's labor. There was abundance without want, and ease without fatigue. The state had assigned duties, and the districts had well-ordered people." Now, in the state of Chen, the roads are unrecognizable, the fields are overgrown with weeds, labor is completed but the harvest is not gathered, and the people are exhausted by idle pleasures. This is abandoning the laws and institutions of the former kings.
"The 'Rank of Officials' in the Zhou regulations states: 'When a guest from a hostile state arrives, the gatekeeper reports it, the travel official respectfully welcomes him, the scout guides him, the minister goes out to the suburbs to greet him, the gate warden clears the gate, the ceremonial official performs sacrifices, the neighborhood head assigns lodging, The Minister of Education prepares disciples; the Minister of Works surveys the roads; the Minister of Justice investigates transgressions; the Forester gathers timber; the Superintendent of Fields collects firewood; the Fire Master oversees the burning sacrifices; the Water Master oversees the washing; the Chief Cook provides cooked food; the Granary Official presents provisions; the Master of Horse provides fodder; the Artisan displays chariots; all officials arrive with their respective goods; the guests enter as if they were at home. Therefore, none, small or great, do not cherish affection. When distinguished guests of the state arrive, they are treated one rank above their station, with increased reverence. As for the king’s officials, all officials properly attend to their duties, overseen by a senior minister. If the king makes a tour of inspection, then the ruler personally oversees it." Now, although Chao is untalented, having a branch clan in Zhou, and receiving the king's command to be a guest passing through Chen, yet the officials in charge do not fulfill their duties, this is to disregard the offices of the former kings.
"The commands of the former kings contain this saying: 'Heaven's Way rewards good and punishes excess. Therefore, in all our founding of the state, let there be no following of what is not the norm, let there be no indulging in dissoluteness and excess, each should guard your norms, in order to receive Heaven's blessings.'" Now, the Marquis of Chen does not consider the continuity of his line, abandoning his proper consort and concubines, and leading his ministers to indulge in debauchery with the Xia clan. Is this not adultery with a different surname? Chen is a descendant of our great Ji. Abandoning the royal robes and crown to wear southern attire to go out, is this not neglecting the norms? This is again violating the commands of the former kings.
"In the past, the teachings of the former kings were to strive to guide one's virtue, yet they still feared falling into error. If one abandons their teachings and discards their regulations, disregards their officials and violates their commands, how will one be able to protect the state? Living among the great states, and lacking these four things, can one last long?"
In the sixth year, Shanzi went to Chu. In the eighth year, the Marquis of Chen was killed by the Xia clan. In the ninth year, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen.
1.22 "Duke Kang of Liu Discusses the Frugality and Extravagance of Lu Grandees"
In the eighth year of King Ding, he sent Duke Kang of Liu to visit Lu as an envoy, distributing gifts to the grandees. Ji Wenzi and Meng Xianzi were both frugal, while Shusun Xuanzi and Dongmen Zishi were both extravagant.
Upon returning, the King asked which Lu grandees were virtuous. He replied: "Ji and Meng will likely long remain in Lu! Shusun and Dongmen will likely perish! If their families do not perish, their persons will certainly not escape." The King said, "Why?" He replied, "I have heard it said: To be a minister, one must act like a minister; to be a ruler, one must act like a ruler. Generosity and solemnity, promulgation and beneficence these are qualities of a ruler. Respect and diligence, reverence and frugality these are qualities of a minister. Generosity is what preserves the foundation; solemnity is what manages the times; promulgation is what extends teachings; beneficence is what harmonizes the people. If the foundation is preserved, it will surely be secure; if the times are met with management, there will be no failed accomplishments; if teachings are extended through promulgation, they will be widespread; if beneficence harmonizes the people, there will be abundance. If the foundation is secure and accomplishments are achieved, if teachings are widespread and the people are abundant, then the ruler can permanently protect the people. What affairs will not be thoroughly managed? Respect is what receives commands; diligence is what guards one's duties; reverence is what attends to matters; frugality is what provides sufficiency. If one receives commands with respect, one will not disobey; if one guards one's duties with diligence, one will not be lax; if one attends to matters with reverence, one will be generous in facing death; if one has sufficient resources through frugality, one will be far from worry. If one receives commands without disobeying, guards one's duties without being lax, If one is generous in dealing with death and distant from worry, then there will be no division between superiors and inferiors. What task would one be unable to undertake? When superiors act with thoroughness, and inferiors can bear their responsibilities, this is how one gains lasting fame that is passed down through the generations. Now, if these two men are frugal, their resources will be sufficient for their needs. If their resources are sufficient, then their clan can be protected. If these two men are extravagant, then their extravagance will lead to disregard for scarcity. If they are scarce and yet do not take it to heart, worry will inevitably befall them. If this is the case, then they will surely expand their own power. Moreover, if a subject is extravagant, the state cannot bear it; it is the way to ruin." The king said, "How so?" He replied, "The position of Dongmen is not equal to that of Shusun, yet he is excessively extravagant; he cannot serve two lords. The position of Shusun is not equal to that of the Ji and Meng families, yet he is also excessively extravagant; he cannot serve three lords. If they both die young, it would still be acceptable, but if they live to an old age and accumulate their poison, will surely perish."
In the sixteenth year, Duke Xuan of Lu died. Before those going to attend the funeral arrived, Dongmen Shi came to report the rebellion, and Zija fled to Qi. In the eleventh year of King Jian, Shusun Xuanbo of Lu also fled to Qi, two years before Duke Cheng died.
1.23 "Wangsun Yue Requests That Shusun Qiaoru Not Be Given Gifts"
In the eighth year of King Jian, Duke Cheng of Lu came to court, and sent Shusun Qiaoru ahead to present gifts and inform the court. He met Wangsun Yue and spoke with him. Yue said to the King, "This coming of Shusun of Lu must be for a special purpose. His tribute for audience is meager, but his words are flattering, he is probably making a request; if he is making a request, he surely desires to be given something. The powerful are the only ones in power in Lu, therefore they are displeased and then send him; moreover, his appearance is broad at the top and narrow at the bottom, They are likely to offend people. Your Majesty, please do not grant it. If greedy and overbearing people come and have their wishes fulfilled, it is rewarding evil, and furthermore, the resources will not suffice. Therefore, the sage deliberates before bestowing gifts; his joy, anger, acceptance, and rejection are also deliberated. Therefore, he does not prioritize leniency and generosity, nor does he prioritize fierceness and resolution, but only prioritizes virtue and righteousness." The King said: "Agreed." He secretly sent someone to inquire in Lu, to request it. The King then did not grant it, and treated him with the etiquette appropriate for a traveling official. When the Marquis of Lu arrived, Zhongsun Mie acted as his second. Wangsun Yue spoke with him, and Yue rebuked him. Yue reported this to the King, and the King generously rewarded him.
1.24 Duke Dan Xiang Discusses Xi Zhi's Presumptuous Exploits
After Jin defeated Chu at Yan, they sent Xi Zhi to report the victory to Zhou. Before the ceremony, Wang Shuzhong gave Gong Ziju wine to drink. They exchanged toasts and offered each other generous gifts. They drank, feasted, and spoke words that pleased each other.
The next day, Wang Shuzi praised him at court. Xi Zhi met with Shao Huan Gong and spoke with him. Shao Gong told Dan Xiang Gong, "Wang Shuzi praises Wen Ji, believing he will surely become the prime minister of Jin. If he becomes the prime minister of Jin, he will surely gain great influence among the feudal lords. He advises the two or three gentlemen to take the lead with him, and they can establish themselves. Now, the master sees me, because Jin has been victorious, and he is truly scheming for himself, saying: 'Without me, Jin would not have fought! Chu has five defeats, but Jin does not know how to capitalize on them; I will strengthen them. Breaking the alliance with Song, is the first; being of little virtue and bribing the feudal lords with land, is the second; To abandon strong, good soldiers and use young, weak ones, is the third defeat; to establish high officials but not heed their advice, is the fourth defeat; when the Yi and Zheng follow them, the three battle lines are unorganized, is the fifth defeat. The fault does not lie with Jin, Jin has won over its people, the leaders of the four armies, their combined strength is at its peak; the ranks of soldiers are well-ordered, the feudal lords are allied with them. These are the five victories: to have a just cause, is the first victory; to have the support of the people, is the second victory; the army leaders are strong and fierce, is the third victory; the ranks are well-ordered, is the fourth victory; the feudal lords are harmonious and united, is the fifth victory. Having one victory is already sufficient to engage, but to have five victories to attack five defeats, and to avoid it, is not human. It is impossible not to fight. Though Luan and Fan do not desire it, I will force them. If we fight and win, it will be due to my strength. Moreover, in warfare, subtle strategies are key, and I have three virtues: courage with propriety, and requiting evil with benevolence. I thrice pursued the soldiers of the Chu army, this is courage; upon seeing their ruler, I would invariably descend and hasten forward, this is propriety; being able to capture the Earl of Zheng and then pardon him, this is benevolence. If they know that such is the governance of the state of Jin, Chu and Yue will surely come to court.'"
"I said, 'You are indeed virtuous. However, concerning the procedures of the state of Jin, if one does not lose the proper sequence, I fear that governance has not yet reached your turn.' He said to me, 'What proper sequence is there? In the past, the former grand master Xun Bo governed from the position of assistant commander of the lower army, and Zhao Xuanzi governed without having led an army. Now Luan Bo is going with the lower army. These three men I surpass even the four who lack nothing. If I were to assist the new army and be promoted to government, would that not be acceptable? The general will surely seek me out." This is what he said. What do you, my lord, think of it?"
Duke Xiang said: "There is a saying: 'The sword is at his neck.' Is this not referring to Xi Zhi? A gentleman does not boast of himself, not to yield [the position], but because he dislikes overshadowing others. Human nature is to surpass those above; one cannot overshadow it. To seek to overshadow others only suppresses those below even more. Therefore, the sage values yielding. Furthermore, a proverb says: 'Beasts hate their nets, the people hate those above them.' The *Book [of Documents]* says: 'The people can be approached [with kindness], but they cannot be pushed too far.' The *Book of Poetry* says: "The kind and amiable prince, seeks blessings without perversity." According to propriety, an opponent must yield three times. This is because the sage knows that the people cannot be further burdened. Therefore, one who reigns over the world must first consider the people, and then protect them, so that he can benefit them in the long run. Now, Xi Zhi is below seven people and yet wants to be above them. This is to seek to overshadow the seven people, and he will surely incur the resentment of those seven. Resentment, even when held by lowly people, is unbearable. How much more so when held by extravagant ministers? How will he deal with it?
"The victory of Jin was because Heaven had a dislike for Chu. Therefore, it warned Chu with Jin. But Xi Zhi regards Heaven's accomplishment as his own strength, is that not difficult to accept? To usurp Heaven is inauspicious; to take advantage of others is unrighteous. Inauspiciousness leads to Heaven abandoning him, unrighteousness leads to the people rebelling against him. Moreover, what of Xi Zhi's three campaigns? Benevolence, propriety, and courage These are all actions of the people. To die for righteousness in battle is called valor; To uphold righteousness and be compliant is called propriety; To cultivate righteousness and achieve great merit is called benevolence. Violating benevolence is recklessness; Violating propriety is shame; Violating valor is treachery. In war, completely defeating the enemy is paramount; In maintaining peace, harmony and conformity to righteousness are paramount. Therefore, one controls barbarians with decisiveness and firmness; One governs the court with order and accomplishment. To abandon battle and presumptuously leave the prince of Zheng, is treachery; To abandon firmness and indulge in indulgence, is shame; To betray the country and join the enemy, is recklessness. To have these three violations and seek to replace one's superior, is far from attaining governance. As I see it, with the sword at his neck, it cannot last long. Even if he is my royal uncle, he cannot escape the difficulty. In the "Great Oath" it says: "What the people desire, Heaven will surely follow." If Wang Shu wants to reject Zhi, can you avoid following him?”
Zhi returned, and died in the disaster the following year. When Bo Yu was imprisoned, Wang Shu Chen Sheng fled to Jin.
1.25 *Shan Xiang Gong Discusses the Impending Turmoil in Jin*
At the meeting of Keling, Shan Xiang Gong saw that Duke Li of Jin looked far and walked with high steps. Jin's Xi Qi's speech was offensive. Xi Chou was seen, his speech was circuitous; Xi Zhi was seen, his speech was boastful; Qi's Guo Zuo was seen, his speech was exhaustive; Duke Cheng of Lu was seen, he spoke of the troubles in Jin and the slander of Xi Chou.
Shanzi said: "What are you worried about, my lord! Jin is about to have turmoil, its ruler and the three Xis will bear it!" The Marquis of Lu said: "I fear I will not escape from Jin, Now, you, sir, say "There will be chaos." May I venture to ask, is this due to the way of Heaven or to human causes?" He replied, "I am neither a blind musician nor a historian, how would I know the way of Heaven? I have seen the countenance of the Lord of Jin and heard the words of the three Xis, and I believe disaster is surely imminent. For a gentleman, the eyes are used to fix the body, and the feet are used to follow them. Therefore, by observing his countenance, one can know his heart. The eyes are used to place righteousness, and the feet are used to pace according to the eyes. Now the Lord of Jin looks afar and his feet step high. His eyes are not on his body, and his feet do not pace according to his eyes. His heart must be different. If the eyes and body do not follow each other, how can he last long? To assemble the lords is a great affair for the people, and it is on such occasions that survival or ruin can be observed. Therefore, if a state is to be without fault, when its lord is at a gathering, his pace, speech, gaze, and hearing must all be without blemish. Then one can understand virtue. If one's vision is far-reaching, one daily severs oneself from righteousness. If one's feet are lifted high (are arrogant), one daily abandons one's virtue. If one's words are discordant, one daily betrays one's trustworthiness. If one's hearing is excessive (listens to lewd things), one daily departs from one's reputation. Now, the eyes are for dwelling in righteousness, the feet are for practicing virtue, the mouth is for protecting trustworthiness, and the ears are for listening to reputation. Therefore, one cannot but be careful. A partial loss brings misfortune, but if all is lost, then the state will follow suit. The Marquis of Jin has erred in two ways, this is why I say this.
"The Xi clan are favored people of Jin, the favored people of Jin. With three ministers and five high officials, they should be cautious and fearful. High position is truly the basis for a quick fall, rich flavors are truly the basis for accumulated poison. Now, the words of Xi Bo are offensive, Shu is unreasonable, and Ji is boastful. To offend is to insult others, to be circuitous is to deceive others, to boast is to overshadow others. To have such favor, and to increase it with these three resentments, who can endure it! Even the son of the state of Qi will join in. To stand in a licentious and disordered state, and to love to speak exhaustively, in order to attract the faults of others, is the root of resentment. Only the virtuous can accept exhaustive speech, does Qi have such? I have heard it said, if a state has virtue and neighbors an unreformed state, it will surely receive its blessings. Now, you are pressed by Jin, and neighbor Qi, if Qi and Jin have misfortune, you can take hegemony, the trouble of lacking virtue, why worry about Jin? Moreover, the people of the Long Di (Long Barbarians) are interested in profit but not in righteousness, their profit is excessive, how should we deal with flowing them away?"
The Marquis of Lu returned, and then expelled Shusun Qiaoru. King's twelfth year, the feudal lords met at Kelin. Jin killed the three Xi. Thirteenth year, the Marquis of Jin was murdered, and buried at the east gate of Yi, with one chariot. The people of Qi killed Guo Wuzi.
1.26 Lord Shan Xiang discusses how Jin Zhou will obtain the state of Jin
Jin Sun Tan's son Zhou went to Zhou, serving Lord Shan Xiang. When standing, he did not limp, when looking, he did not turn back, when listening, he did not prick up his ears, when speaking, he did not speak irrelevantly; when speaking of reverence, he must mention Heaven, when speaking of loyalty, he must mention intention, when speaking of trustworthiness, he must mention oneself, when speaking of benevolence, he must mention others, when speaking of righteousness, he must mention benefit, when speaking of wisdom, he must mention affairs, when speaking of courage, he must mention control, when speaking of teaching, he must mention distinction, when speaking of filial piety, he must mention the spirits, when speaking of kindness, he must mention harmony, when speaking of yielding, he must mention the enemy; The Jin state never failed to grieve in times of sorrow, and never failed to be joyful in times of celebration.
When Duke Xiang of Jin fell ill, he summoned Duke Qing and told him, saying: "Be sure to treat the Jin and Zhou states well, and you will obtain the state of Jin. His actions are refined, and if one is able to be refined, then they will obtain Heaven and Earth. What Heaven and Earth bless, will first be a small thing, and then a state. Respect is the reverence of refinement, Loyalty is the substance of refinement, Trustworthiness is the sincerity of refinement, Benevolence is the love of refinement, Righteousness is the regulation of refinement, Wisdom is the vehicle of refinement, Courage is the leadership of refinement, Teaching is the dissemination of refinement, Filial piety is the foundation of refinement, Kindness is the compassion of refinement, and yielding is the talent of refinement. Imitating Heaven creates respect, Guiding intention creates loyalty, Considering oneself creates trustworthiness, Loving others creates benevolence, Controlling with benefit produces righteousness; Establishing affairs produces wisdom; Leading with righteousness produces courage; Bestowing discourse produces instruction; Manifesting the spirits produces filial piety; Kindness and harmony produce beneficence; Supplanting the enemy produces yielding. These eleven qualities, the Master (Confucius) possesses them all.
"Heaven is six, Earth is five; these are the constant numbers. Weave with Heaven, weft with Earth. If warp and weft are not mismatched, it is a symbol of refinement. King Wen was substantial and refined, therefore Heaven blessed him with the world. The Master is imbued with refinement, and his ancestral line is also recent; he can obtain a state. Moreover, standing without limping is uprightness; seeing without turning back is integrity; listening without pricking up the ears is completion; speaking without exaggerating Caution. Now, rectitude is the path of virtue; integrity is the trustworthiness of virtue; accomplishment is the culmination of virtue; caution is the preservation of virtue. Preserving the culmination purely and firmly, the path being upright and affairs trustworthy, makes manifest excellent virtue. Caution, accomplishment, integrity, and rectitude are the mutual characteristics of virtue. To be concerned for the good and ill fortune of Jin is not to forsake the root. To be adorned with writing and assist virtue, from whom else should the state take it!
"When Duke Cheng returned, I heard that Jin divined about it, encountering *Qian* changing to *Pi*, saying: 'Married but not ending, the lord will leave three times.' One has already passed; those who do not know what comes after the next must certainly be this. Moreover, I heard that at the birth of Duke Cheng, his mother dreamed that a god marked his buttocks with ink, saying: "If he is allowed to possess the state of Jin, it will be thrice that it is given to the grandson of Huan." Therefore, he was named "Black Buttocks," and it has been twice fulfilled by now. Shan Xiang Gong said, "Huan, this is his grandson. And if there is one of superior virtue, filial piety, and reverence, who else could it be but him? Moreover, his dream said: 'Surely the grandson of Huan will possess the state of Jin.' His divination said: 'He will surely take the ruler from Zhou three times.' His virtue is also sufficient to rule a state, thrice it is confirmed. I have heard it said in the "Great Oath" thus: 'My dreams agree with my divinations, confirming auspicious omens, we will surely conquer the Rong and Shang.' It is confirmed thrice. Jin continues to be without principle and lacks descendants, it is about to lose it. You must treat the son of Jin well early, for it is he who should possess it."
Duke Qing agreed to it. When the disorder of Duke Li occurred, they summoned the son of the Zhou [king] and established him, who was called Duke Dao.
1.27 "Crown Prince Jin Admonishes King Ling Concerning Blocking the Gu River"
In the twenty-third year of King Ling, the Gu and Luo Rivers fought [against each other], and were about to destroy the royal palace. The King wanted to block them, but Crown Prince Jin admonished him, saying: "This is not permissible. I have heard that those of old who governed the people did not tear down mountains, did not build up marshes, did not block rivers, and did not dam up lakes. For mountains are gatherings of earth; marshes are places where things return; rivers are conduits of qi; lakes are where water collects. Thus, when heaven and earth are formed, they gather [things] in high places, and cause things to return to lower places. They are channeled into rivers and valleys to guide their qi; and embankments and low-lying areas to collect their beauty. Therefore, gatherings do not crumble and fall apart, and things have a place to return to; vital energy (氣) does not become stagnant, and also does not scatter and dissipate. Because of this, the people in life have resources to use, and in death have a place to be buried. Thus, there are no worries of premature death, blindness, sudden death, or disease, and there are no troubles of hunger, cold, destitution, or scarcity. Therefore, those above and those below can be firmly united, in order to prepare for the unforeseen. The ancient sage kings were only careful about this.
"In the past, Gonggong abandoned this way, indulged in excessive pleasure, licentiously ruined his body, desired to block and dam up all the rivers, tearing down the high and filling in the low, in order to harm the world. August Heaven did not bless him, the common people did not assist him, disasters and chaos arose together, and Gonggong was thus destroyed. In the time of Yu, there was Chongbo Gun, Spread his licentious desires, and alleged that he was following the transgression of Gonggong. Yao therefore executed him at Mount Yu. Afterward, Bo Yu, mindful of the previous lack of measuredness, rectified and altered the system of measurement, modeled on the things of Heaven and Earth, categorized into hundreds of types, and presented them to the people, and measured them against all living things. A descendant of Gonggong, the Four Mountains, assisted him, raising up the high and lowering the low, dredging rivers and guiding stagnant waters, accumulating water and enriching resources. He sealed and elevated nine mountains, cleared and opened nine rivers, banked and dammed nine marshes, enriched and cultivated nine swamps, dredged and crossed nine plains, and settled in nine secluded places, connecting all to the Four Seas. Therefore, Heaven had no hidden Yin, Earth had no scattered Yang, water had no submerged vapor, fire had no disastrous flames, the spirits had no free reign, the people had no licentious desires, time had no reversed order, and things had no harmful existence. Following the achievements of the model Yu, he measured them according to rules and standards. There was nothing that wasn't a commendable accomplishment, truly satisfying the Emperor's heart. August Heaven praised him, and bestowed upon him the empire. He granted him the surname "Si" and the clan name "Youxia," saying that he was able to richly nourish all living things with blessings. He bestowed upon the states of the Four Mountains, appointing them as marquises and counts. He granted them the surname "Jiang," and the clan name "Youlü," saying that they were able to serve as Yu's limbs and vital organs, nourishing things and enriching the people.
"This one king and four counts, is it merely great favor? They are all descendants of deceased kings.
