Only those able to clearly establish commendable righteousness to have descendants below, guarding the sacrifices without abandoning their standards. Though Youxia declined, Qi and Zeng still remained. Though Shen and Lü declined, Qi and Xu still remained. Only those with great merit were granted surnames and clan names that lasted throughout the realm. But when they lost this, there was sure to be a heart of dissolute excess in their midst. Therefore, they lost their clan names, fell prostrate, and could not rise again; their lines were cut off, leaving them without masters, submerged into obscurity, becoming slaves and prison guards. Those who perished, were they truly without favor? They were all descendants of Huang and Yan. It was only because they did not follow the measures of Heaven and Earth, did not comply with the order of the four seasons, did not measure the righteousness between the people and the spirits, and did not emulate the rules of living things, that they were extinguished, leaving no descendants, and are not worshiped even today. And when they gained this, there was sure to be a heart of loyalty and trust in their midst. Measuring themselves by Heaven and Earth, moving in accord with the seasons, harmonizing with the people and the spirits, and emulating the rules of living things, therefore, they ended their lives in nobility and clarity, their glory was radiant and bright, they were granted surnames and clan names, and were attached to them with good reputations. If we open the bequeathed teachings of the former kings, examine their records, maps, laws, and punishments, and observe their rise and fall, all can be understood. Their rise must have had the achievements of Xia and Lü; their fall must have had the failures of Gong and Gun. Now, in our governance, are we not in reality avoiding something, and smoothing over the spirits of the two rivers, causing them to contend for brightness so as to obstruct the royal palace? For the king to then decorate it, is that not unacceptable?
People have a saying: "Do not pass through the gate of someone causing chaos." It is also said: "He who assists in grinding incurs a taste, he who assists in fighting incurs injury." It is also said: "Disaster does not love to cause disaster, (otherwise) it cannot be disaster." The *Book of Poetry* says: "The four steeds trot, the banners flutter, Disorder breeds unevenness, no state is not destroyed. Again it is said: "The people's greed for disorder, they would rather be poisoned." To see disorder and not be wary, what is destroyed will certainly be much, its embellishments will only make it more obvious. If the people resent disorder, it still cannot be stopped, how much more so with the gods? The king is about to dam the Dou River to embellish his palace, this is embellishing disorder and aiding strife, will it not only make the disaster more obvious and invite harm? From our former kings Li, Xuan, You, Ping, and their greed for heavenly misfortune, until now it has not subsided. If I further embellish it, I fear it will extend to my descendants, will the royal house become even more degraded? What is to be done about it?
"Since Houji, pacifying disorder, and by Wen, Wu, Cheng, Kang, they barely managed to secure the people. From the beginning of Houji's foundation of pacifying the people, It took fifteen reigns to bring the state to Wen, and then peace began. It took eighteen reigns for Kang to bring security and tranquility. The difficulty of this was indeed so. When Li began to reform the laws, it had been fourteen reigns already. If a foundation of virtue required fifteen reigns for peace to begin, and the foundation is now fifteen of disasters, how can it succeed? I am constantly vigilant and fearful, saying: "What virtue must be cultivated to slightly illuminate the royal house and thereby counter Heaven's displeasure?" The King is again making clear his aiding and abetting to disorder, how will he be able to bear it? Would the King not also take warning from the kings of Li and Miao, even as far as the final rulers of Xia and Shang, who did not imitate Heaven above, nor model themselves on Earth below, did not harmonize with the people in the middle, nor follow the seasons on all sides, did not revere the gods, but disregarded the five rules. Therefore, people leveled their ancestral temples, and fire burned their ceremonial vessels, their descendants became slaves. They were not merely the same as the common people, but also had not observed the models of former wise rulers and their virtuous conduct. Then these five will receive Heaven's abundant blessings, partake of the people's meritorious labor, have abundant and prosperous descendants, and a reputation that will not be forgotten. All these are things that the Son of Heaven should understand.
"The descendants favored by Heaven may be found in the fields, because they desire to bring chaos to the people. People from the fields may be found in positions of state, because they desire to pacify the people. There is no difference! The *Book of Poetry* says: 'The mirror of Yin is not far, it lies in the era of the Xia sovereign.' What use is there in embellishing palaces? It is to invite chaos. Measured against the heavenly spirits, it is not auspicious. Compared to the products of the earth, it is not righteous. Compared to the rules of the people, it is not benevolent. Compared to the movements of the seasons, it is not compliant. Consulted with the previous teachings, it is not correct. Examining the Odes and Documents, and the people's established words, all speak of the actions of former kings. When superiors and inferiors discuss them, there is no standard to compare them to. May Your Majesty consider this! Affairs that are great do not follow (natural) patterns, and those that are small do not follow mere embellishments. What is above is not in accordance with Heaven's decrees, what is below is not in accordance with Earth's virtues, what is in the middle is not in accordance with the people's principles, and what is in every direction is not in accordance with the timely movement and creation, it will surely lack moderation. If creation lacks moderation, it is a path to harm."
The king ultimately blocked (this advice). When King Jing favored many concubines and attendants, chaos began to arise from this. When King Jing died, the royal house was in great disorder. By the time of King Ding, the royal house had become greatly weakened.
1.28 Lord Yangshe Xi of Jin on Being Sent to Zhou Discusses Lord Jing of Shan’s Reverence, Frugality, Courtesy
Yangshe Xi of Jin was sent as envoy to Zhou, and distributed gifts to the grandees and Lord Jing of Shan. Duke Jing feasted him, with frugality and reverence. In the ceremonies of welcoming, gifts, and farewells, he observed his superior and followed him. In banquets there was no partiality, and send-offs did not exceed the suburbs. Speeches discoursed on "The Great Heaven Has Given Its Mandate."
Shan Zhi's steward saw Uncle Xiang off. Uncle Xiang told him, "How extraordinary! I have heard it said, 'One surname will not rise twice.' Now, Zhou may be about to rise! For they have Shan Zi. Formerly, Shi Yi had a saying, 'Of actions, nothing is better than reverence; of dwellings, nothing is better than frugality; of virtues, nothing is better than yielding; of affairs, nothing is better than consulting.' Shan Zi's gifts to me, in accordance with propriety, all embody these. His palaces are not lofty, and his vessels are without vermillion carvings, this is frugality; his person is attentive, clean and purified, both outwardly and inwardly complete, To be respectful; In feasts and bestowals, Not to overstep those above, Is deference; In matters of treating guests, To follow the lead of superiors and then act, Is seeking advice. If so, And adding to it impartiality, Emphasizing it with integrity, One can avoid resentment. Living frugally and acting respectfully, Being virtuous and deferential, consulting on matters, And being able to avoid resentment, If employed as a minister or assistant, How could one not prosper!
Furthermore, its words explain "The Mandate of Hao Heaven is Accomplished," Praising its great virtue. The poem says: "The Mandate of Hao Heaven is accomplished, The two rulers received it, King Cheng dared not be complacent. Morning and night, he built upon the mandate with sincerity, Oh, how radiant! Truly, his heart earnestly sought tranquility." This speaks of the virtue of King Cheng. King Cheng was able to understand the shining patterns (of Heaven), They are able to settle the martial and fierce. That the Way completes the Mandate and is called Vast Heaven is to assist its superiors. The two rulers received it out of deference to virtue. King Cheng dared not be at ease out of respect for the people. "Su ye" (early and late) means reverence; "ji" (foundation) means beginning; "ming" (command) means trustworthiness; "you" (forgiveness) means leniency; "mi" (secrecy) means tranquility; "qi" (to weave) means clarity; "xi" (bright) means expansiveness; "dan" (sincere) means generosity; "si" (to release) means stability; "jing" (peace) means harmony. In its beginning, they assisted the superiors with virtue and deference and respected the people. In its midst, they were reverent, frugal, trustworthy, and lenient, leading all to tranquility. In its end, they broadened and thickened their hearts so as to stabilize harmony. It begins with virtue and yielding, continues with trustworthiness and generosity, and concludes with steadfast harmony. Therefore, it is called "accomplishment." Shanzi is frugal, respectful, yielding, and consults others, in order to respond to accomplished virtue. Even if Shan does not flourish, his descendants will surely be numerous, and later generations will not forget him.
The *Book of Poetry* says: "What are their qualities like? They are the model of the household. May the lord live for ten thousand years, and bestow blessings on his descendants forever." "Qualities" refers to not disgracing the former sages. "Model" refers to widely enriching the people. "Ten thousand years" refers to having a good reputation that is not forgotten. "Descendants" refers to having numerous and flourishing children and grandchildren. Shanzi does not forget the virtue of King Cheng morning and night, he can be said to not disgrace the former sages. He embraces and protects bright virtue, in order to assist the royal house, he can be said to widely enrich the people. If one can categorize good things and use them to enrich and stabilize the people, they will surely have the fortune of illustrious reputation and flourishing descendants. Surely, Shanzi will deserve this. If Shanzi has any shortcomings, then surely this lord's descendants will continue his work; it will not come from another."
1.29 *Shan Mu Gong Admonishes King Jing Regarding the Casting of Large Coins*
In the twenty-first year of King Jing, he was about to cast large coins. Shan Mu Gong said, "This is not permissible. In ancient times, when natural disasters descended, they would then measure resources and currency, and adjust weights, in order to relieve and save the people. If the people suffered from a lack of weighty currency, then they would make heavy coins to circulate, and thus there would be a "mother" (heavy coin) controlling its "son" (lighter coin) in circulation, and the people would all benefit. If they could not bear heavy currency, then they would make many light coins to circulate, but also not abandon the heavy ones, and thus there would be a "son" (lighter coin) controlling its "mother" (heavy coin) in circulation, benefiting both small and large transactions.
"Now, if the king abandons lightness and pursues heaviness, the people will lose their resources. How can they not be impoverished? If they are impoverished, the king's resources will be deficient. If deficient, then he will heavily tax the people. If the people are not sufficient, they will have distant ambitions, and this is alienating the people. Moreover, to prepare for what has not yet arrived, and to only rescue after it has arrived, is incompatible. To not prepare when it can be done beforehand, is called negligence. To do it before it's necessary, is called inviting disaster. Zhou is already a weak state, and Heaven has not yet been satiated with calamity. Now, to further alienate the people to assist in the disaster, is this not unacceptable? To live with the people and yet alienate them, to prepare to ward off disaster and yet invite it, then how can the state be managed? If the state has no order, how can commands be issued? If commands are not followed, it is the ruler's misfortune. Therefore, the sage establishes virtue among the people in order to remove (calamities).
"The *Xia Shu* (Book of Xia) has a saying: 'The standards of weight, *guan shi* and *he jun*, are in the royal treasury.' The *Shi* (Book of Odes) also has a saying: 'Look at that dry mountain foot, the hazel and the *hu* trees grow abundantly. The kind and gentle gentleman, easily seeks his salary with joy.' That the hazel and *hu* trees of the dry mountain foot flourish, is why the gentleman can easily and joyfully seek his salary there. If the mountains and forests are exhausted, the forests and foothills scattered and lost, the marshes and swamps all drained, the people's strength depleted, the fields and plots desolate, resources and supplies scarce and deficient, the gentleman will have no time for danger and sorrow, so what easy joy will there be?
"Moreover, to cut off the people's resources to enrich the royal treasury is like blocking rivers and springs to make a stagnant pool. Its exhaustion will not be far off. If the people are alienated and resources are depleted, disasters arrive and preparations are lacking, what will the king do? Our Zhou dynasty officials, in their preparations for disasters, have many areas of neglect and abandonment. And yet you further take away their resources to increase the severity of their plight. This is like removing their stores and then obscuring the people. May Your Majesty consider this!"
The King did not listen, and ultimately cast large coins.
1.30 *Duke Mu of Shan Admonishes King Jing Against Casting Large Bells*
In the twenty-third year, the King intended to cast the *Wushe* bell and make it extremely large. Duke Mu of Shan said: "That is not permissible. To create heavy currency to deplete the people's wealth, and then to cast a large bell to reduce its successors, if the accumulated wealth is already lost, and further its succession is diminished, how shall the people grow? Moreover, a bell is merely for making sound. If the *Wushe* bell is excessively large, the ear will not reach it. The bell's sound is for the ear; what the ear cannot reach is not the bell's sound. That which the eye cannot see, cannot be considered seeing. Now, the eye's ability to discern distances extends no further than a few paces or inches; its ability to discern colors extends no further than shades of black or ordinary hues. The ear's ability to discern harmony lies in distinguishing between clear and turbid sounds; its ability to distinguish between clear and turbid sounds extends no further than what one person can overcome. Therefore, when the former kings made bells, the largest did not exceed a鈞 (jūn); the heaviest did not exceed a石 (shí). Standards of pitch, length, volume, and weight arose from this, and objects of varying sizes and uses came forth from this. Therefore, the sages were careful about this. Now, when the king makes bells, listening to them is beyond comprehension, and comparing them is beyond measure. The sound of the bells cannot reveal harmony, and their measurements cannot produce regularity. They are of no benefit to music and deplete the people's wealth. What use are they then!
Now, music is nothing more than pleasing to the ear, and beauty is nothing more than pleasing to the eye. If listening to music causes trembling To be dazzled by beautiful sights is a calamity than which there is none greater. For the ears and eyes are the pivot and mechanism of the heart. Therefore, one must listen harmoniously and view correctly. Listening harmoniously leads to acuity; viewing correctly leads to clarity. With acuity, words are heeded; with clarity, virtue is illuminated. When words are heeded and virtue is illuminated, then one's thoughts are pure and steadfast. If one speaks of virtue to the people, the people will admire and appreciate it, and thus their hearts will return to it. When the ruler obtains the hearts of the people, and uses them to cultivate righteous principles, then whatever he does will succeed, and whatever he seeks will be obtained. Only then can he be truly happy. If the ears hear harmonious sounds and the mouth speaks beautiful words, which are made into laws and decrees and promulgated to the people, and these are rectified by standards and measures, the people will use their minds and strength to follow them without weariness. Accomplishing matters without fail is the utmost joy. Flavor within the mouth and sound within the ears, sound and flavor generate vital energy. Vital energy in the mouth becomes speech, in the eyes it becomes sight. Speech is named for its trustworthiness, sight is named for its timing and movement. Trustworthiness in speech establishes governance, timely movement cultivates life. When governance is established and life is cultivated, that is the height of joy. If sight and hearing are not in harmony, and there are tremors and dizziness, then the intake of flavors will not be refined, if not refined, then vital energy is lost, if vital energy is lost, then there is disharmony. From this arise mad and rebellious speech, deluded and confusing sight, mutable and changeable reputations, excessive and wicked measures. Decrees issued are not trusted, punishments and governance are abandoned to chaos, actions do not accord with the times, the people have no foundation to rely on, not knowing where to exert their strength, each has a divided heart. The ruler loses his people, what he does will not succeed, what he seeks will not be obtained, How can they find joy in this? Within these three years, there are two instruments of alienating the people. The state is in danger!"
The king did not listen and asked Lingzhou Jiu about it. He replied, "Your servant's duty is beyond my ability. I have heard that, the qin and se should emphasize the *gong* note, the bells should emphasize the *yu* note, the stone chimes should emphasize the *jiao* note, gourds and bamboo are good for regulation. The largest (sound) should not exceed *gong*, and the smallest should not be less than *yu*. Now, *gong* is the master of the sounds. Arrange them in order until *yu*. The sage preserves music and cherishes wealth. Wealth is used to prepare instruments, and music is used to cultivate wealth. Therefore, heavy musical instruments follow the small (sounds), and light instruments follow the large (sounds). Therefore, metal emphasizes *yu*, stone emphasizes *jiao*, pottery and silk emphasize *gong*, gourds and bamboo emphasize harmony, Leather and wood produce a single sound.
“Now, government is like music; music follows harmony; harmony follows balance. Sound is used to harmonize music, musical pitch is used to balance sounds. Metal and stone are used to initiate it, silk and bamboo are used to conduct it, poetry is used to guide it, song is used to chant it, the gourd is used to express it, the earthenware instrument is used to praise it, and leather and wood are used to regulate it. When things obtain their regularity, it is called the perfection of music; the place where perfection gathers is called sound; sounds responding and protecting each other are called harmony; nothing, whether small or large, oversteps its bounds, is called balance. Thus, it is cast in metal, ground in stone, bound with silk and wood, enhanced with gourd and bamboo, regulated by drums, and conducted to follow the eight winds. Thereupon, the vital energy has no stagnant yin, nor scattered yang. Yin and yang are ordered in sequence, When the wind and rain arrive in their season, auspicious growth flourishes, the people are harmonious and benefit, resources are prepared, and joyful completion is achieved, those above and below are not weary, therefore it is called "Music Master." Now, if petty faults of the ruler obstruct correctness, excessive use of resources obstructs wealth, and obstructed correctness and depleted wealth obstruct joy. Petty things suppress the great, and are unacceptable to the ear; this is not harmony. If the sound travels too far, it is not balanced. Obstructing correctness and depleting wealth, sounds that are not harmonious and peaceful are not what the Grand Minister is responsible for.
"When there are sounds of harmony and peace, then there is flourishing wealth. Therefore, guide them with moderate virtue, sing them with moderate tones, virtuous sounds without error, to unite gods and men, the gods are thus at peace, and the people thus listen. As for depleting resources, exhausting the people's strength, to indulge his licentious desires, listening to it does not bring harmony, comparing it is not according to standards, it is of no benefit to instruction, and alienates the people and angers the gods, this is not what your servant has heard."
The King did not listen, and ultimately cast the great bell. In the twenty-fourth year, the bell was completed, and the musicians proclaimed its harmony. The King said to Lingzhou Jiu, "The bell is indeed harmonious." He replied, "It is not yet known." The King said, "Why?" He replied, "When the ruler makes instruments, and the people all delight in them, then there is harmony. Now, wealth is lost and the people are exhausted, and all are resentful and hateful, your servant does not know of its harmony. Moreover, what the people as a whole love, rarely does it fail; what they as a whole hate, It is rare that it will not be abandoned. Therefore, a proverb says: "The hearts of the people build a city, the mouths of the people melt gold." Within three years, the harm to gold re-emerges, fearing the abandonment of the "one." The King said: "You are old and senile! How would you know?" Twenty-five years later, the King died, and the bells were not harmonious.
1.31 *King Jing Asks Ling Zhou Jiu about Bell Pitch*
The King was about to cast a Wu She (a pitch pipe) and asked Ling Zhou Jiu about pitch standards. He replied: "The pitch standards are the means by which to establish the averages and produce the measures. The ancient divine blind musicians examined the middle tones and measured them to create pitch standards, measures, equal temperament for the bells, the norms for all officials, and recorded them with threes, leveled them with sixes, completing them with twelve; this is the way of Heaven. Now, six is the color of the center, therefore it is named Yellow Bell, which is used to propagate and nourish the six qi and nine virtues. From this, they are arranged in order: the second is Tai Cu. In the fourth space, Lin Zhong, harmoniously arranges all affairs, so that none are not entrusted to solemn purity and reverence. In the fifth space, Nan Lü, praises the flourishing of Yang things. In the sixth space, Ying Zhong, equally distributes beneficial tools, so that there is a response and return.
"If the lü and lǜ do not change, there will be no treacherous things. In the small harmony (fine tuning), there are bells but no bó (large bells), to make its greatness apparent. In the large harmony (coarse tuning), there are bó but no bells, and at its greatest there are no bó, to make its smallness resound. Greatness made apparent and smallness made to resound, is the Way of harmony. Harmony leads to longevity, longevity leads to firmness, firmness leads to clarity, clarity leads to completion and return which brings joy. This is how government is achieved; therefore, the former kings valued it."
The king said: "What are the seven lǜ?" He replied: "In the past, when King Wu attacked Yin, the year was in Quail Fire (鶉火, a zodiacal division), the month was in Celestial Quadriga (天駟, a zodiacal division), the day was in the Ford of Separating Trees (析木之津, a zodiacal division), the hour was in the Handle of the Dipper (斗柄), and the star was in Celestial Turtle (天黿). The positions of the star, the day, and the hour were all in the northern corner. This was established by Zhuanxu, and Emperor Ku received it. Our Ji clan originated from Celestial Turtle, and from Separating Trees there are Construction Star (建星) and Oxherd (牽牛), which are descendants of Bo Ling, the nephew of our ancestral mother, Da Jiang, and the spirits relied upon by Lord Pang. The location of the year is the division of territory belonging to our Zhou. The location of the month is the auspicious sign for the horse and agriculture. These were surveyed and organized by our great ancestor, Hou Ji. The king wishes to combine these five positions and three locations and utilize them. From Quail Fire to Celestial Quadriga, there are seven orders. The measurements from north to south are in sevenfold agreement. All men and spirits are united by numbers, and revealed by sounds. When numbers agree and sounds harmonize, then they can be united. Therefore, their numbers are made consistent with seven, and used the pitch-pipes to harmonize their sounds, and thus there were the seven pitch-pipes.
"The King arrayed (his troops) on the night of Guihai in the second month, and before it was finished, it rained. He used the Shang Gong mode of the Yi Ze pitch-pipe to complete it, at the hour of Chen. Chen is located above Xu, therefore, lengthening the Shang Gong mode of the Yi Ze pitch-pipe, it is named Yu, which is to serve as a fence and screen for the people. The King used the Xia Gong mode of the Huang Zhong pitch-pipe to deploy the Rong at the fields of Mu, therefore it is called Li, which is to encourage the six armies. He used the Xia Gong mode of the Tai Cu pitch-pipe to issue orders in Shang, clearly displaying virtuous conduct, reaching the many crimes of Zhou, therefore it is called Xuan, which is to proclaim the virtue of the three kings. Returning to and reaching within Ying, he used the Shang Gong mode of the Wu She pitch-pipe to generously bestow favors and dispensations upon the common people, therefore it is called Lei Luan, which is to be gentle and accommodating to the people."

4.24 "Qín Invades Jìn and Stops Duke Huì of Qín"
Six years later, when Qín had settled its affairs for the year, they led an army to invade Jìn, do not give them grain!" The Duke said: "I detest their ruler, but what crime have the people committed? Heavenly disasters occur, nations experience them in turn. Supplying deficiencies and recommending grain during famine is the proper way, we cannot abandon this principle to the world." He asked Gōngsūn Zhī, "Should we give it to them?" Gōngsūn Zhī said: "Your Lordship has shown kindness to the ruler of Jìn, but the ruler of Jìn has not shown kindness to his people. Now, in this drought, they listen to your Lordship; this is the way of Heaven. It would be better to give it to them in order to please the people. If the people are pleased, they will certainly blame their ruler. If their ruler does not listen, then punish him. Even if he wants to resist us, who will support him?" so the people are certainly displeased. Now he has also killed my father and the seven senior officials, thus his enemies make up half the state. If you, my lord, attack him, their ruler will surely flee." Duke Mù said: "How can losing the people lead to someone's death? Moreover, misfortune is only inevitable if one doesn't prepare for it. Those who have enough do not dwell in distress, those who dwell in distress do not have enough, victory and defeat transform. If you take misfortune as an excuse to disobey, who will be able to help the ruler? Wait for me!"
4.23 *Qin Recommends Grain Sale to Jin During Famine, But Jin Does Not Give Qin Grain*
Jin was experiencing famine and requested grain from Qin. Pī Bào said: "The ruler of Jin has been impolite to you, everyone knows this. In past years they faced hardship, and now they are experiencing famine again. They have already lost the people, and now they have lost Heaven, they will surely suffer many disasters. Your lordship should attack them, There were no scouts, ambushers, or guards along the way, yet the Chǔ 楚 people dared not plot against them, for they feared the trustworthiness of Jìn 晉. From this point on, even after Píng Gōng 平公 died, there were no troubles from Chǔ 楚.
4.98 "Shū Xiàng 叔向 on Emphasizing Virtue and Avoiding Striving to be First"
At the alliance of Sòng 宋, the Chǔ 楚 people persistently requested to be the first to smear the blood in the oath. Shū Xiàng 叔向 said to Zhào Wénzǐ 趙文子, "The power of a hegemon or true king lies in virtue, not in smearing the blood first. If you can support your ruler with loyalty and trustworthiness, and make up for the shortcomings of the other lords, even if the smearing is done last, the lords will still uphold it. Why strive to be first? If you deviate from virtue and accomplish matters through bribes, even if you smear the blood first now, the lords will abandon you. What is the desire in being first? In the past, King Chéng established an alliance with the feudal lords at Qíyáng. Chǔ was considered a southern barbarian, so they placed straw mats, erected observation posts, and along with the Xiānbēi people, guarded the beacon fires, and therefore did not participate in the alliance. Now, you are about to make an alliance with the feudal lords, only virtue matters, you must focus on virtue and not strive to be first, focus on virtue, this is how to subdue Chǔ." So they put the people of Chǔ first.
4.99 《Zhào Wénzǐ Requests the Release of Shūsūn Mùzǐ》
At the meeting of Guó, the people of Lǔ broke their word. The Chǔ chancellor surrounded the city and intended to execute Shūsūn Mùzǐ of Lǔ. Yuè Wángfù sought bribes from him, but they were not given. Zhào Wénzǐ said to Shūsūn: "That Chǔ chancellor has desires concerning Chǔ, and is somewhat afraid of the feudal lords. Concerning the feudal lords' affairs, he seeks to resolve them, but not to the extreme. As for his character, he is strong and values favor, If they reach [him], they will certainly not avoid [him]. Why don't you flee? Unfortunately, they will certainly reach you." He replied: "Bào has received orders from the lord to attend the covenant of the various lords for the sake of the state. If Lǔ is guilty, and the one who received the covenant flees, he will certainly not escape [punishment]. That would be me going out and endangering it. If I am executed by the various lords, Lǔ will be completely punished. They will certainly not add [troops]. Please, let me be executed. For execution to come from oneself is truly difficult; if it comes from others, what harm is there? If it can bring peace to the lord and benefit the country, good and evil are of one mind."
Wén Zǐ was about to request this from Chǔ, Yuè Wáng Fù said: "The covenant of the various lords has not yet ended, and Lǔ has turned its back on it. What use are the alliances of Qi? Even if we cannot punish (him), and further excuse the one who accepted the alliance, how can Jin be the leader of the alliance? We must kill Shūsūn Bào." Wénzǐ said: "There is someone who does not hesitate to die to secure the safety and benefit of his state, can we not cherish him? If everyone were as concerned for the state as he is, then the great would not lose their prestige, and the small would not be insulted. If this way (of acting) is indeed sincere, it can be taught, how could there be ruin for the state? I have heard it said: 'If a good person is in office and is concerned about (something) but does not remedy it, it is inauspicious; if a bad person is in office and is not removed, it is also inauspicious.' We must spare Shūsūn." He persistently pleaded with Chǔ and secured his release.
4.100 《Zhào Wénzǐ Builds a House, and Zhāng Lǎo Says it Does Not Meet Propriety》
Zhào Wénzǐ was building a house, hewing its rafters and smoothing them. Zhāng Lǎo saw this in the evening, did not announce himself, and returned home. Wén Zǐ heard of it, and drove his carriage to go there, and said: "I am not good, you should also tell me, why are you so quick to leave?" He replied: "For the emperor's palace, the rafters are hewn and polished, and closely fitted with stone; for the feudal lords, they are polished; for the high officials, they are hewn; for the lower officials, they are simply made smooth. Preparing the materials according to their rank, is appropriate; following the proper level, is proper etiquette. Now, you are noble and forget righteousness, rich and forget etiquette, I fear I cannot escape implication, how dare I then inform you?" Wén Zǐ returned, and ordered them not to polish them. The craftsmen requested to hew them all, Wén Zǐ said: "That would be a shame. It would be seen by later generations, that those who hew them, It is the benevolent who do this; as for grinding/sharpening them, it is the unbenevolent who do that."
4.101 "Zhào Wénzǐ Praises Suí Wǔzǐ as Worthy"
Zhào Wénzǐ toured Jiǔyuán with Shū Xiàng, and said: "If the dead could be brought back to life, who would I go back to?" Shū Xiàng said: "Would it be Yángzǐ!" Wénzǐ said: "Yángzǐ practiced incorruptibility in the state of Jìn, but was not able to protect himself, his wisdom is not enough to be praised." Shū Xiàng said; "Would it be Jiù Fàn!" Wénzǐ said: "Jiù Fàn saw profit and did not consider his lord, his benevolence is not enough to be praised. Would it be Suí Wǔzǐ! He accepted advice and did not forget his teacher, his words about himself did not lose his friends, serving his lord, he did not seek advancement through flattery, he did not fawn in order to retreat."
4.102 "Qín Hòuzǐ Says Zhào Mèng is About to Die"
The son of the ruler of Qín fled and came to see Zhào Wénzǐ. He asked, "Is the ruler of Qín virtuous?" The son replied, "I do not know." Wénzǐ said, "Since the prince has deigned to come to our humble state, it must be to avoid his ruler's lack of virtue." The son replied, "That is so." Wénzǐ said, "Can it last long like this?" The son replied, "Zhēn has heard that when a state is without virtue but the harvests are bountiful, it rarely lasts for more than five years." Wénzǐ looked at the sun and said, "Morning and evening do not wait for each other, who can wait for five years!" Wénzǐ went out, and the son said to his followers, "Zhào Mèng is going to die! Even if a virtuous man is generous and concerned for the future, he is still afraid of not succeeding. Now, Zhào Mèng is the prime minister of the state of Jìn, presiding over the alliances of the various lords. Thinking of cultivating virtue for ages to come, and calculating the length of distant years, one still fears not being able to complete it in one's lifetime; now, indulging in days and delaying years, being lazy and indolent is excessive, if death doesn't catch up with them, there will surely be great calamity." In winter, Zhào Wénzǐ died.
4.103 "Doctor Hé Examines Duke Píng's Illness"
Duke Píng was ill. The Duke Jǐng of Qín sent Doctor Hé to examine him, who came out and said: "It is incurable. This is what is called being distant from men and close to women, infatuation that breeds corruption; neither caused by ghosts nor food, infatuation that leads to the loss of one's will. Good ministers do not arise, Heaven's mandate does not bless. If the ruler does not die, he will surely lose the feudal lords." Zhào Wénzǐ heard of this and said: "I have followed the other ministers to assist the ruler as the leader of the feudal lords, for eight years now, there has been no internal harshness or evil, The feudal lords are not of two minds. Zǐ Hú said: "Good ministers are not born, Heaven's Mandate does not bless."? He replied: "It is speaking of from now on. Hé heard it said: "The straight does not assist the crooked, the bright does not advise the dark, the embraceable wood does not grow in danger, the pine and cypress do not grow on low ground." You, sir, cannot advise against delusion, causing it to reach the point of generating illness, and you do not withdraw yourself and instead indulge his governance. Eight years is considered long enough, how can it be prolonged!" Wénzǐ said: "Does medicine extend to the state?" He replied: "The best doctor treats the state, the next best treats people's illnesses, indeed, they are medical officials." Wénzǐ said: "You speak of *gǔ* (蛊, a kind of hex or illness caused by poison), what actually causes it to arise?" He replied: "The evil of *gǔ*, the flying seeds of grain produce it. Among all things, nothing is more subjugated to *gǔ* (蠱) than grain. Among all *gǔ*, nothing is more excellent than grain. The flourishing of grain and the suppression of *gǔ* are what make things manifest and clear. Therefore, those who eat grain should, in the daytime, select men of virtue to emulate the brightness of grain, and at night, cultivate the quiet virtue of women to suppress the wickedness of *gǔ*. Now, Your Lordship does only one of these. This means you are not enjoying the benefits of grain but rather feeding on *gǔ*; this means you are not illuminating the brightness of grain but rather accumulating *gǔ* in vessels. The character *wén* 文 with 'insect' (蟲) and 'vessel' (皿) composes the character *gǔ* 蠱. That is why I say this." Wénzǐ 文子 asked: "How much time does he have left?" He replied: "If the feudal lords submit, no more than three years; if they do not submit, no more than ten years. Beyond that, it will be the calamity of Jìn 晉." In that year, Zhào Wénzǐ 趙文子 died. The feudal lords rebelled against Jìn. Ten years later, Píng Gōng died.
4.104 "Shū Xiàng Equalizes the Stipends of the Two Princes of Qín and Chǔ"
The heir of Qín came to serve, with a thousand chariots. Gōngzǐ Gàn of Chǔ came to serve, with five chariots. Shū Xiàng was the Grand Tutor, and he was in charge of assigning stipends. Hán Xuānzǐ asked about the stipends of the two princes. He replied: "The minister of a great state receives the land of a brigade (lǚ), and a senior grand master receives the land of a troop (zú). These two princes are senior grand masters; each should receive the stipend of a troop, which is acceptable." Xuānzǐ said: "The prince of Qín is wealthy, how can we equalize his stipend?" He replied: "Titles are established to manage affairs, stipends are provided to sustain the titles, virtue is used to allocate them, and merit is used to assess them. How can wealth be used to assign stipends! The wealthy merchants of Jiàng, How can one enrich the stipends and emoluments? The wealthy merchants of Jiàng (made) Wéi Pān's carriages and wooden awning pass beyond the court. It was only because their meritorious service was little that they could adorn their carriages with gold and jade, embellish their clothing with intricate designs, and be able to traffic in the goods of the feudal lords, yet have no emolument the size of a xún or a chǐ, because they had no great accomplishments for the people. Moreover, Qín and Chǔ are comparable. How could they be reverting in wealth?" Thereupon he equalized their stipends.
4.105 "Zhèng Zǐchǎn Comes to Pay a Formal Visit"
Zhèng Jiǎn Gōng sent Gōngsūn Chéngzi to pay a formal visit. Píng Gōng was ill. Hán Xuānzi assisted in assigning (him) to the guest house. The guest inquired about the lord's illness. (Hán Xuānzi) replied: "Our lord's illness has been long-standing, and there is no deity, high or low, that we have not universally informed, yet there is no remedy. Now (he) dreamt of a yellow bear entering the bedroom door. I don't know whether someone killed (it), or whether it is a fierce ghost!" Zǐchǎn said: "With your wisdom, you are undertaking great governance. What fierce ghost could there be? Qiáo has heard it said, formerly Gǔn violated the Emperor's commands and was executed at Mount Yǔ. transforming into a yellow bear, entering the abyss of Yǔ. Indeed, it was for the suburban altar of the Xià, and the three dynasties upheld this. As for what the spirits can influence, if not their own kind, then it is those who share their position. Therefore, the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Shàngdì, dukes and marquises sacrifice to the various lords, and those from qing ministers downwards do not go beyond their own kin. Now the house of Zhōu is somewhat diminished, and Jìn is truly succeeding it. Could it be that those who are confused have not yet performed the suburban sacrifice of the Xià?" Xuānzǐ told him, and sacrificed to the suburban altar of the Xià. Dǒng Bó served as the representative of the dead, and after five days he recovered. The Duke saw Zǐchǎn, and bestowed upon him a Jǔ ding tripod.
4.106 "Shū Xiàng Discusses Worrying About Virtue, Not Worrying About Poverty"
Shū Xiàng saw Hán Xuānzǐ. Xuānzǐ was worried about poverty. Shū Xiàng congratulated him. Xuānzǐ said: "I have the title of a high minister, but without the substance of it. I have no means to follow the other ministers. This is why I am worried. You congratulate me. Why?" He replied: "In the past, Luán Wǔzǐ had only enough land for one infantryman. His palace did not have a complete set of ritual vessels. He proclaimed his virtue, obeyed the laws, and thus surpassed the other lords. The lords befriended him, the Róng and Dí tribes were loyal to him. He rectified the state of Jìn, executed justice without causing resentment, and thus avoided disaster. When Huánzǐ became arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and unrestrained, he pursued his ambitions through plunder, engaging in lending and hoarding wealth. He should have met with disaster, but he relied on the virtue of Wǔzǐ to live out his days. If you, Huái Zi, change Huán's actions, and cultivate Wǔ's virtues, you can avoid disaster, and escape Huán's crimes, so as to avoid destruction by Chǔ. Now, Xì Zhāo Zi, his wealth was half the ducal house's, his family was half of the three armies', relying on his wealth and favor, he was arrogant in the state, his body was displayed in the court, his clan was wiped out in Jiàng. If not, consider the eight Xì, five were senior officials and three were ministers, their favor was great, yet they were destroyed in a single day, and no one mourned them, solely because they lacked virtue. Now you, my son, possess the poverty of Luán Wǔ Zi, I believe you can cultivate his virtue, that is why I congratulate you. If you do not worry about not establishing virtue, but fret about the inadequacy of wealth, I will have no time for congratulations, what congratulations would there be?" Xuān Zi bowed, kowtowed to him, He said: "Qǐ (起) is about to perish, relying on you to preserve it. It is not that Qǐ (起) dares to take this entirely upon myself, but that from Huán Shū (桓叔) downwards, they will all appreciate your kindness."
4.107 *Shū Xiàng (叔向) Discusses the Equal Guilt of the Three Villains*
Shì Jǐngbó (士景伯) went to Chǔ (楚), Shū Yú (叔魚) served as his assistant. Xíng Hóu (邢侯) and Yōng Zǐ (雍子) were disputing over land. Yōng Zǐ (雍子) offered his daughter to Shū Yú (叔魚) to seek a favorable judgment. When the day came to adjudicate the case, Shū Yú (叔魚) suppressed Xíng Hóu (邢侯). Xíng Hóu (邢侯) killed Shū Yú (叔魚) and Yōng Zǐ (雍子) in the court. Hán Xuānzǐ (韓宣子) was troubled by this. Shū Xiàng (叔向) said: "The three villains are equally guilty. Please kill the one who is alive and mutilate the corpses of the dead." Xuānzǐ (宣子) said: "What do you mean?" He replied: "Fú (鮒) sold justice, Yōng Zǐ (雍子) bought it with his daughter, and Xíng Hóu (邢侯) interfered even though it was not his official duty. To sell the country's justice for personal gain, to sever family ties to buy a favorable judgment, and for someone not holding the position of Chief Justice to take matters into his own hands and commit murder: "Their crime is the same." Xíng Hóu heard of this and fled. Consequently, he executed the Xíng Hóu clan and publicly displayed the corpses of Shū Yú and Yōng Zǐ in the marketplace.
4.108 Zhōngháng Mùzǐ Leads Troops to Attack the Dí and Besieges Gǔ
Zhōngháng Mùzǐ led troops to attack the Dí and besieged Gǔ. Some people of Gǔ requested to surrender the city, but Mùzǐ refused. A military officer said, "We can obtain the city without expending effort; why do you not do it?" Mùzǐ said, "It is not in accordance with the proper way to serve one's ruler. Those who offer a city must seek profit from me. To guard with two hearts is the greatest of treachery. Rewarding good and punishing treachery are the fundamental laws of the state. To promise and not give is to lose our credibility. If we were to give, it would be to reward great treachery. If treachery is rewarded with rank, what will happen to goodness? Furthermore, the Dí people were regretful that they came to seek their desires through surrendering cities. Does Jìn have nothing of the kind? This is how I would teach the people on our borders to be disloyal. Now, one who serves a ruler advances according to his ability; if he cannot, then he retreats, and does not rely on safety for disloyalty." He ordered the army officers to call on the city to be wary and attack it. Before the siege ramps were even completed, the drums signaled surrender. Zhōngháng Bó having conquered it, brought the drum master Yuàn Zhī with him. He ordered the drummers each to return to their places, and those who were not officials should not follow.
A subject of the drum master, named Sùshā Lí, was traveling with his family. The army officers arrested him. He said: "I serve my lord, not the land. We are called lord and subject, how can we be called subjects of the land? Now that my lord has indeed moved, on what should I rely in Gǔ?" Mù Zǐ summoned him and said: "Gǔ has a ruler now, if your heart serves a ruler, I will fix your salary and rank." He replied: " but I have not pledged myself to the drums of Jìn. I have heard it said: 'Pledging oneself as a subject allows for no divided loyalty. Pledging oneself and then being put to death by the whip is an ancient law.' You, my lord, have a renowned name, and I, your subject, must not betray my pledge. How dare I pursue private gain, trouble the Minister of Justice, and disrupt the old laws! What if I were caught off guard?!" Mùzǐ sighed and said to his attendants: "What virtue have I cultivated to deserve such a subject?" He then allowed him to proceed. After the offering was made, he spoke to the duke about granting Gǔzǐ land at Héyīn, and he appointed Sùshā Lí to oversee it.
4.109 *Fàn Xiànzǐ's Admonition Against Neglecting Learning*
Fàn Xiànzǐ was on a diplomatic mission to Lǔ. He inquired about Jùshān and Áoshān, and the people of Lǔ used their local names to answer. Xiànzǐ said: "Is it not Jù, He replied, "They are the taboo names of the former lords Xiàn and Xiàn Zǐ returned and Ao, perhaps?" Wǔ." widely cautioned those he knew, saying, "People must not fail to learn. I went to Lǔ and mentioned the two taboo names, and was laughed at, solely because of my lack of learning. A person having learning is like a tree having branches and leaves. A tree having branches and leaves can provide shade for people, how much more so a learned gentleman?"
4.110 "Dǒng Shū Desires to Create a Bond"
Dǒng Shū was about to marry from the Fàn family. Shū Xiàng said, "The Fàn family is rich, why not stop it?" He said, "I wish to create a bond through marriage." Another day, Dǒng Qí complained to Fàn Xiànzǐ, saying, "He does not respect me." Xiànzǐ held him and had him spin thread by the locust tree in the courtyard. Shū Xiàng passed by him and said, "Why don't you ask him to release me?" Shū Xiàng said, "You sought imprisonment, and now you are imprisoned; you sought help, and now you have help. You desired and obtained it, so what is there to request?"
4.111 *Zhào Jiǎnzǐ Wanted to Have Fighting Retainers*
Zhào Jiǎnzǐ said, " Mèng Xiànzǐ of Lǔ has five fighting retainers. I don't have even one. Why is that?" Shū Xiàng said, "You don't desire it. If you desired it, Xī would be waiting to grapple with people."
4.112 *Yán Mò and Shū Kuān Advise Wèi Xiànzǐ Not to Accept Bribes*
A man from Gěngyáng was involved in a lawsuit, and was about to lose. He requested to offer a bribe to Wèi Xiànzǐ. Xiànzǐ was about to agree to it. Yán Mò said to Shū Kuān, "Shall we remonstrate with him? Our lord is known among the lords for not taking bribes. Now, to bring disaster upon him with the bribe from Gěngyáng, this is not acceptable." The two men went to court, and did not withdraw. Xiànzǐ was about to eat, and asked who was in the courtyard. Someone said: "Yán Míng and Shū Bāo are there." He summoned them and made them assist at the meal. After he had finished eating, he sighed three times. When he was full, Xiànzǐ asked them, saying: "There is a saying: Only food can make one forget worries. My lords sighed three times during the meal; what is the reason?" They answered with the same words: "We are small men and greedy. When the food was first brought in, we were afraid there would not be enough, Therefore, he sighed. He ate in the middle of the meal and blamed himself, saying, "Could it be that the master's food is insufficient?" This is why he sighed again. After the master had finished eating, he wished to take the heart of a gentleman for the belly of a small man, and only wished to be full, this is why he sighed a third time." Xiànzǐ said: "Good." Then he dismissed the man from Gěngyáng.
4.113 "Dǒng Ānyú Declines Zhào Jiǎnzǐ's Reward"
In the campaign at Xiàyì, Dǒng Ānyú achieved much. Zhào Jiǎnzǐ rewarded him, but he declined. He insisted on rewarding him, and Dǒng Ānyú replied: "When your servant was young, I stepped forward to hold the writing brush, assisting in establishing fame and commands, praised in previous generations, establishing righteousness among the lords, but you, my lord, did not record it. And when your servant was strong, I strengthened my arms and legs to follow the Sīmǎ, and harsh wickedness did not arise. When I grew older, dressed in formal attire with ceremonial apron and belt, I followed the steward, and the people had no divided loyalties. Now, if I suddenly act like a madman, and you say, "I will certainly reward you," that would be rewarding me for my madness; I would rather die!" He rushed out, and they then released him.
4.114 *Zhào Jiǎnzǐ Uses Jìnyáng as a Fortress*
Zhào Jiǎnzǐ sent Yǐn Duó to govern Jìnyáng. Yǐn Duó requested, "Should I treat it like a place for producing silk? Or treat it as a fortress?" Jiǎn zǐ said, "A fortress!" Yǐn Duó reduced the number of households there. Jiǎn zǐ warned Xiāngzǐ, saying, "If the state of Jìn faces difficulties, do not underestimate Yǐn Duó because of his youth, and do not think Jìnyáng is too far; you must return there."
4.115 *Yóu Wú Zheng Righteously Reproves Zhào Jiǎnzǐ from Killing Yǐn Duó*
Zhào Jiǎnzǐ sent Yǐn Duó to govern Jìnyáng, saying, "You must tear down its ramparts. I will go there; if I see the ramparts, it is as if I see Yín and Jí Shè." Yǐn Duó went and added to them. Jiǎn zi went to Jìnyáng, saw the fortifications, and angrily said, "I must kill Duó before entering." The grandees pleaded with him, but he would not listen, saying, "He is the enemy of Zhāoyú." Yóu Wúzhèng came forward, saying, "In the past, our former lord Wénzi, though young, skillfully avoided difficulty. He followed the Jī clan in the palace, possessed filial virtue to emerge among the ducal lineage, possessed respectful virtue to ascend to his position, possessed martial virtue to be ashamed of merely being a senior minister, and possessed mild virtue to establish his reputation. He lost the norms of the Zhào clan and dismissed his tutors, yet relied on his own person to recover what he had lost. When Jǐngzi grew up in the palace, wèi jí jiàoxùn ér sì lì yǐ, [Before having received instruction, he was enthroned as successor.] yì néng zuǎnxiū qí shēn yǐ shòu xiān yè, [He was still able to cultivate himself and inherit the ancestral legacy,] wú bàng yú guó, [without being criticized by the state,] shùn dé yǐ xué zǐ, [following virtue to teach his son,] zé yán yǐ jiào zǐ, [choosing words to teach his son,] zé shī bǎo yǐ xiàng zǐ. [choosing teachers and guardians to assist his son.] Jīn wú zi sì wèi, [Now, my son inherits the throne,] yǒu Wén zhī diǎnxíng, [he has the model of Wén,] yǒu Jǐng zhī jiàoxùn, [he has the teachings of Jǐng,] zhòng zhī yǐ shī bǎo, [reinforced with teachers and guardians,] jiā zhī yǐ fù xiōng, [supplemented by father and elder brothers,] zi jiē shū zhī, [yet you all alienated them,] yǐ jí cǐ nán. [and brought about this disaster.] Fú Yǐn Duó yuē: [Yǐn Duó said:] 'Sī lè ér xǐ, [Thinking of joy and being joyful,] sī nán ér jù, [thinking of hardship and being fearful,] rén zhī dào yě. [is the way of man.] Wěi tǔ kěyǐ wèi shī bǎo, [Even a clod of dirt can serve as a teacher or guardian,] wú hé wéi bù zēng?' [why wouldn't I increase my efforts?'] Shì yǐ xiū zhī, [Therefore, he cultivates it,] shù yuē kěyǐ jiàn ér jiū Zhào zōng hū! [hoping it can be a mirror to gather the Zhào clan!] Ruò fá zhī, [If you punish him,] shì fá shàn yě. [it is punishing good.] Fá shàn bì shǎng è. [Punishing good will surely reward evil.] Chén hé wàng yǐ!" [What hope do I have then!"] Jiǎn zi shuō, [Jiǎn zi was pleased,] yuē: [and said:] "Wēi zi, [“Wēi,] "Wú jǐ bù wéi rén yǐ!" He was rewarded with the reward for averting disaster, Yǐn Duó. Initially, Bólè and Yǐn Duó harbored a grudge. Because his reward was like that of Bólè, he said: "You saved me from death, how dare I not return the emolument." He declined, saying: "I planned for the lord, not for you. Let the grudge remain."
4.116 "The Iron Battle: Zhào Jiǎnzǐ and two others boast of their achievements"
In the Battle of Iron, Zhào Jiǎnzǐ said: "The people of Zhèng attacked me, I lay prostrate, drawing the blood of the wound, and the sound of the drum did not wane. In today's affair, none is like me." The Duke Zhuāng of Wèi was on the right, and said: "I went up and down nine times, and all those I struck were killed. In today's affair, none can surpass me." Yóu Wúzhèng, the charioteer, He said: "My two straps are about to break, but I can stop it. In today's affair, I am next in line." He drove and rode on the lumber, and both straps broke.
4.117 "Wèi Zhuāng Gōng's Prayer"
Wèi Zhuāng Gōng was about to pray, and said: "Your great-grandson Kuǎi Kuì, because of his loyalty to Zhào Yáng, dares to solemnly announce to his August Ancestor King Wén, Venerable Ancestor Kāng Shū, Esteemed Ancestor Xiāng Gōng, Illustrious Deceased Father Líng Gōng, I, Yí, request to be without tendons or bones, without facial wounds, without failure in employment, without falling or fear. Even in death, I dare not ask." Jiǎn Zǐ said: "The will is entrusted to the father."
4.118 "Shǐ Àn Advises Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ Against Hunting at Lóu"
Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ hunted at Lóu, Shǐ Àn heard of it, and waited at the gate with a dog. Zhào Jiǎnzi saw him and asked, "What are you doing?" He replied, "I acquired a dog and wanted to test it in this park." Zhào Jiǎnzi said, "Why didn't you inform me?" He answered, "When the lord travels, the vassal does not follow, which is disobedient. When the lord intends to go to Lóu, if Lù does not hear of it, how dare the vassal trouble the day?" Zhào Jiǎnzi then returned.
4.119 "Shàoshì Zhōu Knows Worthiness and Yields"
Shàoshì Zhōu was the right-hand man of Zhào Jiǎnzi. He heard that Niú Tán was strong and requested to compete with him. Unable to win, he yielded his position as right-hand man. Zhào Jiǎnzi granted it and made Shàoshì Zhōu the steward, saying, "Knowing worthiness and yielding is something "It is permissible to dismiss them."
4.120 "Shǐ Àn on Good Ministers"
Zhào Jiǎnzi said: "I wish to obtain good ministers like those of the Fàn and Zhōngháng families." Shǐ Àn was in attendance and said: "What will you use them for?" Jiǎn zi said: "Good ministers are what people desire, so why ask?" He replied: "Your servant believes it's because they were not good. Now, serving a ruler involves pointing out faults and rewarding good deeds, recommending the capable and removing the incompetent, presenting abilities and advancing the worthy, selecting talent and recommending them, reciting good and bad deeds morning and evening and presenting them [to the ruler]. Guiding them with culture, acting with compliance, being diligent with strength, dedicating oneself to the death. If listened to, then advance; if not, then retreat. Now, the ministers of the Fàn and Zhōngháng families could not rectify and assist their lords, leading them to hardship. When their lord was abroad, they were again unable to stabilize the situation, and abandoned him. What good are they? If they did not abandon him, then how would the ruler obtain them? If these two were truly good ministers, they would diligently strive to restore their lord, and enable him to reestablish himself abroad, not stopping until death. When would they come back? If they return, then they are not good ministers." Jiǎn Zǐ said, "Excellent. My words were truly excessive."
4.121 "Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ Asks Zhuàng Chízī About Worthies"
Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ asked Zhuàng Chízī, "Which of the eastern scholars is the best?" Zhuàng Chízī bowed and said, "I dare to offer congratulations!" Jiǎn Zǐ said, "You haven't answered my question, "What congratulations are these?" He replied, "I have heard it said: When a state is about to rise, gentlemen consider themselves insufficient; when it is about to perish, it seems to have more than enough. Now you are in charge of the government of the state of Jìn and ask about petty people, and also seek out virtuous people, it is for this reason that I congratulate you."
4.122 "Dòu Chōu Says that a Gentleman Grieves for the Lack of Men"
Zhào Jiǎnzi sighed and said, "A sparrow entering the sea becomes a clam, a pheasant entering the Huái becomes a mirage. Soft-shelled turtles, fish and turtles, none cannot transform, only man cannot. How sad!" Dòu Chōu was in attendance, and said, "I have heard it said: Gentlemen grieve for the lack of men, not for the lack of wealth; grieve for the lack of virtue, not for the lack of favor; grieve that one's reputation is not good, Not grieving over the year's poor harvest. Fú Zhōngháng shì did not care for the people's difficulties, desiring to monopolize the Jìn state. They ordered their sons and grandsons to go plow in Qí, the sacrificial animals of the ancestral temple were made to toil in the fields. Such is the transformation of the people, what day is there to look forward to!"
4.123 *Zhào Xiāngzǐ sent Xīn Zhìmùzi to attack the Dí*
Zhào Xiāngzǐ sent Xīn Zhìmùzi to attack the Dí. He defeated the Zuǒrén and Zhōngrén. A messenger came to report. Xiāngzǐ was about to eat a solitary meal, and had a look of fear. An attendant said, "The matter of the dogs is great, yet your countenance is not pleased, why is that?" Xiāngzǐ said, "I have heard it said: If virtue is not pure, yet fortune and emoluments arrive together, it is called luck. But luck is not a blessing, and without virtue, one should not enjoy peace. Peace is not brought by luck, "This is what I fear."
4.124 *Zhì Guǒ's* Argument that *Zhì Yáo* Would Certainly Destroy His Clan
*Zhì Xuānzǐ* was planning to make *Yáo* his successor. *Zhì Guǒ* said: "It would be better to choose *Xiāo*." *Xuānzǐ* said: "*Xiāo* is stubborn." He replied: "*Xiāo's* stubbornness is on the surface, *Yáo's* stubbornness is in his heart. Stubbornness in the heart ruins a state; Stubbornness on the surface does no harm. *Yáo* surpasses others in five ways, but there is one area where he is deficient. Handsome features and tall stature are considered virtuous; Skill in archery and horsemanship, and physical strength are considered virtuous; Mastery of various skills is considered virtuous; Eloquent writing and clever arguments are considered virtuous; Strength of will, decisiveness, and courage are considered virtuous. But he is extremely unbenevolent. He uses his five virtues to overpower others, and he acts with unbenevolence; who can endure this? If you insist on establishing *Yáo*, the *Zhì* clan will certainly be destroyed." He was not listened to. Zhì Guǒ separated his clan from the Tài Shǐ (太史), and became the Fǔ clan. When the Zhì clan perished, only Fǔ Guǒ remained.
4.125 *Shì Zhuó Tells Tǔ Mùshèng of His Fear That It Will Make the People Uneasy*
Zhì Xiāngzǐ (智襄子) built a beautiful house, and Shì Zhuó (士茁) was present in the evening. Zhì Bó (智伯) said, "Isn't the house beautiful!" He replied, "It is beautiful indeed, but I also have my fears." Zhì Bó said, "What do you fear?" He replied, "I serve you with the writing brush. Records say: 'On high mountains and steep plains, grass and trees do not grow. In places where pines and cypresses thrive, the soil is not fertile.' Now that the construction of earth and wood is excessive, I fear that it will make the people uneasy." The house was completed, and three years later the Zhì clan perished.
4.126 "Zhì Bó Guó Advises Zhì Xiāngzǐ"
Returning from Wèi, the three ministers feasted at the Lán Terrace. Zhì Xiāngzǐ jested with Hán Kāngzǐ and insulted Duàn Guī. Zhì Bó Guó heard of this and advised, "If the lord is not prepared, disaster will surely arrive." He replied, "Disaster will originate from me. If I do not create disaster, who would dare to instigate it!" Zhì Bó Guó answered, "It is different. The Xì clan had the misfortune of the carriage pole incident; the Zhào clan had the slander of Mèng Jī; the Luán clan had the accusation of Shū Qí; the Fàn and Zhōngháng clans had the misfortune of hasty governance. All of these are known to the lord. The *Xià Shū* (Book of Xia) says: 'One person makes three mistakes, is resentment only found in the open? Not seeing this, it is to be planned against.' The *Zhōu Shū* (Book of Zhou) says: 'Resentment is not determined by size, it is also not determined by smallness.' A gentleman can diligently handle small matters, therefore he has no great troubles. Now, the lord, in one feast, shames the rulers and ministers of others, and is unprepared, saying 'They dare not instigate disaster,' is this not inadvisable?" Indeed, who is not worthy of being pleased, and who is not worthy of being feared? Gnats, ants, wasps, and scorpions can all harm people, how much more so rulers and ministers!" He did not listen. From that time, five years later, there was the Difficulty of Jìnyáng (晉陽). Duàn Guī (段規) rebelled, initiating the difficulty, and killed Zhì Bó (智伯) in the army, and thus destroyed the Zhì (智) clan.
4.127 *The Siege of Jìnyáng (晉陽)*
During the Siege of Jìnyáng (晉陽), Zhāng Tán (張談) said: "The former lord valued weighty matters, for the difficulties of the state. Why not temporarily cease being stingy with treasures toward the feudal lords?" Xiāng Zǐ (襄子) said: "I have no envoys." Zhāng Tán said: "The territory is acceptable." Xiāngzǐ said: "Unfortunately, I am afflicted with illness, I have not followed the ways of my ancestors, and I have taken bribes without virtue. To seek to satisfy my desires with territory is to nurture my illness and encroach upon my livelihood. I will rather perish with all than grant it." Xiāngzǐ went out and said: "Where should I flee?" His attendant said: "Zhǎngzǐ is nearby, and its city walls are thick and complete." Xiāngzǐ said: "The people exhausted their strength to complete it, and they will again die to defend it, who will support me?" His attendant said: "The granaries of Hándān are full." Xiāngzǐ said: "They have drained the people's fat and marrow to fill them, and then will kill them, who will support me? It must be Jìnyáng! It is what the former lord entrusted to me, and Yǐn Duó treated the people leniently there, the people must be harmonious." So he fled to Jìnyáng. The Jìn army surrounded it and flooded it, the stoves sank and frogs spawned within, yet the people had no intention of rebellion.
Zhèng Yǔ 5.1 *Shǐ Bó Discusses Rise and Fall for Duke Huán*
Duke Huán was the Minister of Education, and was very popular with the Zhou people and the people of the eastern lands. He asked Shǐ Bó, saying, "The royal house is in turmoil, and I fear it will reach me. Where can I escape death?" Shǐ Bó replied, "The royal house will decline, and the Róng and Dí will surely prosper; they cannot be resisted. Those who border Chéngzhōu in the south are Jīngmán, Shēn, Lǚ, Yīng, Dèng, Chén, Cài, Suí, Táng; in the north are Wèi, Yān, Dí, Xiānyú, Lù, Luò, Quán, Xú, Pú; in the west are Yú, Guó, Jìn, Kuí, Huò, Yáng, Wèi. and Ruì; to the east are Qí, Lǔ, Cáo, Sòng, Téng, Xuē, Zōu, and Jǔ. If these are not the sons, grandsons, maternal brothers, nephews, or maternal uncles of the king, then they are all people of the Mán, Jīng, Róng, and Dí tribes. If they are not relatives, they are intractable and cannot be admitted. Those between the Jì, Luò, Hé, and Yǐng rivers! These are the states of viscounts and barons, Guó and Kuài being the largest. Shū of Guó relies on his power, and Zhòng of Kuài relies on his strategic location. These all have arrogant, extravagant, and negligent hearts, and add to this their greed and avarice. If you, my lord, because of the troubles of the Zhōu, were to entrust your wives, children, and wealth to them, they would not dare to refuse. Zhōu was in chaos and exhausted. They were arrogant and greedy, and they would surely betray their lord. If you, my lord, were to take the people of Chéngzhōu, and using eloquent words, punish their crimes, there is nothing you could not conquer. If you conquer these two cities, Wū, Bì, Bǔ, Zhōu, Yī, Xiè, Lì, and Huá, these will be your lord's territory. If you have Huá to the front and the Hé River behind, the Luò River to the right and the Jǐ River to the left, and you preside over Fú and Guī while eating from the Qín and Wěi, establishing laws and punishments to guard it, this would be a way to make it somewhat secure."
The Duke said, "Is the south not feasible?" He replied, "The Jing son Xióng Yán had four sons: Bó Shuāng, Zhòng Xuě, Shū Xióng, and Jì Xún. Shū Xióng fled to Pú due to hardship and became a barbarian. Jì Xún was established. The Wěi clan were about to raise him up, but calamity ensued, and they did not succeed. This is Heaven's will. Moreover, he is extremely intelligent and harmonious, truly like his former kings. Your servant has heard that what Heaven ordains will not be diminished for ten generations. Indeed, his descendants will illuminate and expand the territory. He cannot be forced. Furthermore, he is a descendant of Zhòng 重 and Lí 黎.
Lí 黎 was the fire official for Gāo Xīn Shì 高辛氏, who, with his brilliant and vast fire, illuminated Heaven's brightness and Earth's virtue, shining light upon the four seas. Therefore, he was given the name 'Zhù Róng' 祝融. His merit was great.
"Those who accomplish the fiery deeds of Heaven and Earth, their descendants have never failed to shine brightly. Yú 虞, Xià 夏, Shāng 商, and Zhōu 周 are examples of this. Yú Mù 虞幕 was able to harmonize the winds, thus enabling the flourishing of all things. Xià Yǔ 夏禹 was able to single-handedly pacify the waters and earth, They were those who classified and managed the various kinds of things. Shāng Qì 商契 was able to harmonize the five teachings, thereby protecting the common people. Zhōu Qì 周棄 was able to sow and cultivate the various grains and vegetables, thereby providing clothing and food for the people. Afterwards, all of them became kings, dukes, marquises, or counts. Zhù Róng 祝融 was also able to illuminate the brightness of heaven and earth, thereby producing pliable and excellent materials. His descendants formed eight clans, but among them, none were marquises or counts under the Zhōu 周 dynasty. Those who assisted in creating things in previous dynasties: Kūn Wú 昆吾 was a count during the Xià 夏 dynasty; Dà Péng 大彭 and Shǐ Wéi 豕韋 were counts during the Shāng 商 dynasty. They did not exist under the Zhōu 周 dynasty. The Jǐ 己 clan's Kūn Wú 昆吾, Sū 蘇, Gù 顧, Wēn 溫, and Dǒng 董, the Dǒng 董 clan's Zōng Yí 鬷夷 and Huàn Lóng 豢龍, were extinguished by the Xià 夏 dynasty. The Péng 彭 clan's Péng Zǔ 彭祖, Shǐ Wéi 豕韋, and Zhū Jī 諸稽, were extinguished by the Shāng 商 dynasty. The Tū 禿 clan's boatmen were extinguished by the Zhōu 周 dynasty. The Yún 妘 clan's Wū 鄔, Kuài, Lù, Bīyáng, the Cáo lineage of Zōu, Jǔ, all served as fiefs and guards. Some were in the royal court, some among the Ī and Dí peoples, too numerous to count. Moreover, they had no notable reputation, so they will certainly not rise. The Zhēn lineage has no descendants. Among the flourishing lineages, could it be the Mǐ lineage? The Mǐ lineage of Kuí and Yuè are not worth mentioning. The Mán of the Mǐ lineage are indeed barbaric, but only Jīng truly possesses brilliant virtue. If the Zhōu decline, they will surely rise. The Jiāng, Yíng, Jīng, and Mǐ lineages have indeed alternately intermarried with the various Jī lineages. The Jiāng are descendants of Bó Yí, the Yíng are descendants of Bó Yì. Bó Yí was able to perform rites to the spirits to assist Yáo, Bó Yì was able to discuss all things to assist Shùn. Their descendants have all continuously maintained sacrifices, but none have yet risen. When the Zhōu decline, "They are about to arrive."
The Duke said, "How would it be to seize the Jiǔzhōu west of Xiè?"
He replied, "The people there are deceitful, greedy, and cruel; they cannot be relied upon. Only in the area between Xiè and Jiá, their lord is extravagant and arrogant, and the people are lazy and despise their lord, and have not yet received the beneficence of the Zhōu; if you were to replace their lord and instruct them in the Zhōu teachings, it would be easy to take, and they could be used for a long time."
The Duke said, "Is the Zhōu about to decline?" He replied, "It is almost certain to decline. The "Tài Shì" says, 'What the people desire, Heaven will surely grant.' Now the king abandons high intelligence and clear manifestation, and favors slanderous evil and darkness; he detests those who are acute and wealthy, and is close to stubborn children and the impoverished. Discard harmony and pursue sameness. Indeed, harmony produces things, while sameness leads to stagnation. Using one thing to balance another is called harmony, therefore it can enrich and grow, and things will return to it. If one uses the same thing to supplement the same thing, it will be exhausted and then discarded. Therefore, the former kings mixed earth with metal, wood, water, and fire, in order to create all things. Thus, they harmonized the five flavors to please the mouth, strengthened the four limbs to protect the body, harmonized the six musical tones to sharpen the ears, corrected the seven emotions to guide the heart, balanced the eight categories to cultivate a person, established the nine rules to establish pure virtue, combined the ten numbers to instruct the hundred body parts. They produced a thousand goods, prepared for ten thousand regions, calculated a hundred million affairs, measured a trillion things, collected standard revenues, managed the utmost limits. Therefore, the king dwells in the fields of the nine realms, collects standard revenues to feed the myriad people, comprehensively teaches and is able to use them, and harmony and joy are as one. Indeed, like this, it is the pinnacle of harmony. Therefore, the former kings betrothed queens from different surnames, Sought wealth from those who had methods, Chose ministers and accepted remonstrances from skilled artisans, And discoursed on a multitude of things, Striving for harmony and agreement. A single sound has nothing to listen to, A single thing has no refinement, A single flavor yields no fruit, A single thing is not discussed. The king is about to abandon these kinds of things, And be aligned with what is singular. Heaven has taken away his clarity, How can he avoid ruin, Can he achieve it?
"That Guó Shí Fǔ, Is a person who flatters and skillfully follows, Yet he is established as a high official, Aligned with what is singular. Abandoning the betrothal of a queen and instead establishing a concubine, Favoring narrow stubbornness. Dwarfs and hunchbacks, Truly attend by his side, Keeping near foolish children. The laws of the Zhōu are not clear, And the words of women are followed, Employing slander and wickedness. Not establishing worthy officials, Because portents are lucky errors, they are actions done in darkness. This thing, cannot last long. Moreover, in the time of King Xuān, there was a children's rhyme that said: 'Quercus goblets and mulberry bows, will truly destroy the Zhōu state.' Thereupon King Xuān heard of it, there was a husband and wife selling these things, the king ordered them seized and executed. A concubine of the palace gave birth to a daughter, and not a son, so she was afraid and abandoned her. This person, was taken in and fled to Bāo. Heaven's mandate for this has been long in the making, what more can be done? The "Instructive Sayings" has it, saying: 'In the decline of the Xià dynasty, the god of the people of Bāo, transformed into two dragons, to copulate in the royal court, and said: "We, are the two lords of Bāo." The Xià ruler divined whether to kill them, or to drive them away, or to keep them, none were auspicious. He divined about asking for their spittle and storing it away, it was auspicious. Therefore, he presented silks and recorded the event, the dragons vanished and the spittle remained, it was put in a box and stored away, and deliver it to the outskirts (for sacrifice)." Throughout the Yin and Zhou dynasties, no one opened it. Until the end of the reign of King Lì, they opened it and looked at it, and the essence flowed into the courtyard, and could not be removed. The king ordered women to shout at it without veils, and it transformed into a black turtle, and entered the king's treasury. A young concubine in the treasury, who had not yet lost her milk teeth, encountered it, and became pregnant when she came of age, and gave birth during the reign of King Xuān. She conceived without a husband, so she was afraid and abandoned it. A man who made bows and arrows was being punished on the road, and a couple pitied its night cries, and took it to hide it, and fled to Bāo. The people of Bāo, Bāo Xū, had a lawsuit, and (the child) was used as a gift to the king, the king then kept her, And he favored this woman, causing her to become queen and give birth to Bófú. Heaven has brought this about for a long time; the poison he represents is great. He will cause him to indulge in immoral conduct and add to it. When the most potent of poisons is dried, its killing power is even faster. The states of Shēn and Zēng, and the Western Róng are now strong; the royal house is now in turmoil. To indulge in desires with this situation, would that not be difficult? If the king wants to kill the heir apparent to establish Bófú, he will certainly seek him in Shēn. If the people of Shēn do not give him up, he will certainly attack them. If he attacks Shēn, and then Zēng and the Western Róng unite to attack Zhōu, Zhōu will not be able to defend itself! Zēng and the Western Róng are now aligning themselves with Shēn; Shēn and Lǚ are now strong. Their deep affection for the heir apparent is surely knowable. If the royal army is present, their rescue of him is also certain. The king's heart is filled with anger. Guó Gōng will follow him. The survival of Zhōu, will not last three years! If you, my lord, wish to avoid this calamity, you should quickly plan for a place of refuge! To seek support when the time arrives will likely be too late!"
The Duke said: "If the Zhōu 周 dynasty declines, among the various Jī 姬 (states), which will rise?" He replied: "I have heard it said that Wǔ 武's achievements illuminate the merits of Wén 文. When Wén 文's blessings are exhausted, Wǔ 武 will succeed him! Among the sons of King Wǔ 武王, Yīng 應 and Hán 韓 are out of the question, it must be Jìn 晉! It is situated near a strategic pass and neighbors small states. If you add virtue to this, it can greatly expand." The Duke said: "Jiāng 姜 and Yíng 嬴, which will rise?" He replied: "The state that is large and virtuous will rise sooner. Qín Zhòng 秦仲 and Marquis of Qí 齊侯, are the most outstanding of the Jiāng 姜 and Yíng 嬴 families, and are large. "Is he about to rise?" The duke was pleased. Thereupon, he sent treasures and bribes eastward. The states of Guó and Kuài accepted them. All ten cities had places where these were deposited.
5.2 "At the End of King Píng, the Rise of Qín, Jìn, Qí, and Chǔ as Successors"
In the eighth year of King Yōu, Duke Huán became Minister of Education. In the ninth year, the royal house began to be disturbed. In the eleventh year, he perished. And at the end of King Píng, Qín, Jìn, Qí, and Chǔ rose as successors. Qín Jǐng and Xiāng took territory from Zhōu because of this, Jìn Wénhóu stabilized the Son of Heaven because of this, Qí Zhuāng and Xī became minor hegemons because of this, Chǔ Fénmào began the opening of Pú because of this.
Chǔ Yǔ (Discourses of Chǔ) 6.1 "Shēn Shūshí on the Way to Tutor the Crown Prince"
King Zhuāng sent Shì Wěi to tutor the Crown Prince Zhēn. He declined, saying: "Your servant is untalented, and has nothing to add." The king said: "I rely on you to teach him to cherish goodness." He replied: "Goodness resides in the Crown Prince. If the Crown Prince desires goodness, good people will come. If he does not desire goodness, then goodness will not be employed. Therefore, Yáo 有 Dānzhū, Shùn 有 Shāngjūn, Qǐ 有 Wǔ Guān, Tāng 有 Tàijiǎ, King Wén 有 Guǎn, Cài. These five kings all possessed great virtue, yet they had wicked sons. It was not that they did not desire their goodness, but they were unable to make them good. If the people are troublesome, they can be taught and trained. The Mán 蠻, Yí 夷, Róng 戎, and Dí 狄 have long been disobedient, and the Middle Kingdom cannot employ them." The king finally ordered him to tutor the crown prince.
He asked Shēnshū Shí 申叔時, Shūshí 叔時 said, "Teach him the *Chūnqiū* 春秋, and make him value good and suppress evil, to warn and encourage his heart. Teach him history, and make him promote manifest virtue and abolish hidden darkness. in order to give rest and fear to their actions. Teach them the *Shī* 詩 (Book of Poetry), and thereby lead them to broaden and make manifest virtue, in order to illuminate their will. Teach them the *Lǐ* 禮 (rites), causing them to know the rules of superiors and inferiors. Teach them *Yuè* 樂 (music), in order to dredge away their filth and settle their fickleness. Teach them the orders (Lìng 令), causing them to seek information about objects and officials. Teach them discourse (Yǔ 語), causing them to understand virtue, and to know that the former kings were diligent in using manifested virtue among the people. Teach them about the records of past aspirations (Gù Zhì 故志), causing them to know about things being abandoned and flourishing, and to be warned and to feel fear. Teach them about the normative books (Xùndiǎn 訓典), causing them to know their kin, and to conduct themselves according to righteousness.
"If after all this they do not follow, and act without repentance, then intone and recite. Employ people based on their abilities, seek out virtuous and capable individuals to assist them.
