If they repent but are not supervised, then be diligent in their affairs, repeatedly provide them with instructive examples and laws to guide them, and strive for carefulness and sincerity to solidify them. If supervision is implemented but not thorough, then clearly bestow and relinquish to guide them toward loyalty, clearly emphasize permanence to guide them toward trustworthiness, clearly demonstrate measurement to guide them toward righteousness, clearly define ranks to guide them toward propriety, clearly promote reverence and frugality to guide them toward filial piety, clearly emphasize respect and caution to guide them in their affairs, clearly emphasize love and kindness to guide them toward benevolence, clearly emphasize revealing benefits to guide them toward culture, clearly emphasize eliminating harm to guide them toward martial skill, clearly emphasize precision to guide them in punishment, clearly emphasize upright virtue to guide them in rewards, and clearly emphasize solemnity and reverence to illuminate their leadership. If, after all this, it still doesn't succeed, it cannot be done.
Furthermore, recite poetry to assist and guide them, use dignified bearing to precede and follow them, use deportment to support them on the left and right, use clear conduct to proclaim and support them, establish principles of righteousness to motivate their actions, use respect and reverence to oversee and supervise them, Diligence to encourage him, filial piety to accept him, loyalty and trustworthiness to express him, virtuous words to praise him. If teaching is complete and one does not follow, he is not human. How can he be revitalized! If the gentleman retreats when he assumes office, then he will be respected after the retreat, otherwise he will be destroyed."
6.2 *Zǐ Náng* Discusses King *Gōng*'s Posthumous Title
King *Gōng* had an illness. He summoned the high officials and said, "I, being without virtue, have lost the legacy of my late lord, and overturned the army of the *Chǔ* state. This is my crime. If I am able to preserve my head and neck until death, and follow the traditions of my late lord in the spring and autumn sacrifices, then please give me the posthumous title 'Líng' or 'Lì'. The high officials agreed."
The king died, When the burial approached, Zǐnáng 子囊 discussed the posthumous title. The grandees said, "The King has already given his orders." Zǐnáng 子囊 said, "That will not do. For those who serve a lord, they should highlight his virtues first, and not follow his faults. How mighty is the state of Chǔ 楚, and he ruled over it, pacifying the southern sea, and instructing even the various Xia 夏 peoples. His favor was great indeed. To have such favor, and yet recognize his own faults, can it not be called 'Gōng 恭' ('Respectful')? If the late lord was virtuous, then I request to use 'Gōng 恭' as his title." The grandees followed his advice.
6.3 *Qū Jiàn's 屈建 Sacrifice to his Father Doesn't Include Water Chestnut*
Qū Dào 屈到 loved water chestnuts. When he fell ill, he summoned the elders of his clan and entrusted them, He said: "When sacrificing to me, be sure to use *jì* (water caltrop)." When the grand sacrifice arrived, the senior clan member was about to present the *jì*, Qū Jiàn ordered it to be removed. The elder said: "The Master instructed so." Zǐ Mù said: "That is not so. The Master bore the responsibility of the government of the State of Chǔ. Its laws and punishments are in the people's hearts and stored in the royal treasury. In its higher aspects, it can be compared to the former kings; in its lower aspects, it can instruct later generations. Though small the State of Chǔ, the feudal lords all praise it. Its sacrificial regulations state: 'The ruler of the state has an ox offering, the grand master has a sheep gift, the knight has a pig and dog as a libation, the common people have roasted fish as an offering, bamboo utensils and dried meat and minced meat sauce are shared by all, high and low. It does not shame precious and unusual items, nor does it display extravagance.' The Master would not use his personal desires to interfere with the state's regulations." Therefore, it was not used.
6.4 *Cài Shēngzǐ* Discusses Chǔ Talent Used by Jìn
Jiāo Jǔ married the daughter of Shēn Gōngzǐ Mù. Gōngzǐ Mù committed a crime and fled. Kāng Wáng believed that Jiāo Jǔ had sent him away, so Jiāo Jǔ fled to Zhèng, intending to then flee to Jìn. Cài Shēngzǐ was about to go to Jìn, and met him in Zhèng. He feasted him, presenting him with a jade disc as a gift, and said: "You should eat well. May your two ancestors both assist you, and may you be able to serve the ruler of Jìn and become a lord among the feudal lords." Jiāo Jǔ declined, saying: "It is not my wish. If I can return my bones to Chǔ, even in death, I will not decay." Shēngzǐ said: "You should eat well. I will return you." Jiāo Jǔ descended and bowed three times, and presented his carriage horses. Shēngzǐ accepted them.
Returning, he saw the Chancellor Zǐmù, who spoke with him, and said: "Although you are like brothers to Jìn, "However, Cài and Wú are my nephews. Which of the two states is more virtuous?" He replied, "The Jìn minister is not as good as the Chǔ minister, but their officials are more virtuous. Their officials are all material for ministers. It is like the qǐzǐ (Catalpa and Tilia trees) and leather. Chǔ actually abandons them. Even though Chǔ has talent, it cannot use it." Zǐmù said, "They have nephews and uncles from the ducal clan. How can they abandon talent?" He replied, "In the past, during the troubles of lìngyǐn Zǐyuán, someone slandered Wángsūn Qǐ to Chéngwáng. The king did not believe it. Wángsūn Qǐ fled to Jìn, and the people of Jìn employed him. At the Battle of Chéngpú, the Jìn general was about to flee. Wángsūn Qǐ participated in the military affairs and said to Xiān Zhěn, 'This army, only Zǐyù desired it. It goes against the king's wishes. 故唯 Dōnggōng yǔ Xīguǎng shí lái. Of the followers of the feudal lords, half were rebellious. The Ruò Áo clan had deserted. The Chǔ army would surely be defeated. Why abandon them!'" Xiān Zhěn followed this advice. He greatly defeated the Chǔ army; this was the doing of Wángsūn Qǐ.
"In the past, when King Zhuāng was still weak, Shēn Gōngzǐ Yífù was his teacher, and Prince Xiè was his tutor. He sent Shī Chóng and Zǐ Kǒng to lead the army to attack Shū. Xiè and Yífù each commanded an army and divided their responsibilities. When the army returned, they presented the king to Lú Jílí as though he were a captive, and Lú Jílí killed the two princes and restored the king. Someone slandered Xī Gōng's minister to the king, but the king did not believe it. Xī Gōng fled to Jìn, and the people of Jìn employed him. It was truly slander that ruined Chǔ, preventing them from planning for the eastern regions; this was the doing of Xī Gōng.
"In the past, Yōng Zǐ's father and elder brother slandered Yōng Zǐ to King Gōng, Wáng Fú shì, Yōng Zǐ fled to Jìn, and the people of Jìn employed him. During the campaign at Yān, when the Jìn generals were about to retreat, Yōng Zǐ participated in the military affairs and said to Luán Shū: "The Chǔ army can be assessed. It only matters to attack the royal clan in the central army. If you weaken the middle and lower ranks, Chǔ will surely rejoice. If we combine forces and trap their center, our upper and lower ranks will surely defeat their left and right flanks, and then we can concentrate our forces to attack their royal clan, and surely greatly defeat them." Luán Shū followed his advice, greatly defeating the Chǔ army. The king himself suffered a facial wound; this was the doing of Yōng Zǐ.
"In the past, Chén Gōngzǐ Xià married the daughter of Zhèng Mù Gōng for Yù Shū, who gave birth to Zǐ Nán. Zǐ Nán's mother caused chaos in Chén, leading to its downfall, and caused Zǐ Nán to be executed among the lords. King Zhuāng had already bestowed the mansion of the Xià family to Shēn Gōng Wūchén, then he further granted it to Zǐ Fǎn, who eventually died at Xiāng Lǎo's place. Xiāng Lǎo died at Bì, The two sons contended for her, but no agreement was reached. Gōng Wáng sent Wū Chén on a diplomatic mission to Qí, taking Xià Jī with him, and subsequently fled to Jìn. The people of Jìn employed him, and he thereby connected Wú and Jìn. He sent his son, Hú Yōng, to be an envoy to Wú, and taught them archery and charioteering, guiding them to attack Chǔ. That it continues to be a problem to this day, is due to the actions of Shēn Gōng Wū Chén.
"Now, Jiāo Jǔ married into Zǐ Mǒu's family, Zǐ Mǒu offended and fled, the officials in power disapproved of this, and said to Jiāo Jǔ: 'It was you who sent him away.' He was afraid and fled to Zhèng, wistfully stretching his neck and looking south, saying: 'Perhaps I will be pardoned for my crime.' Receiving no such outcome, he then fled to Jìn, and the people of Jìn have again employed him. If he plots against Chǔ, there will surely be both gains and losses."
Zǐ Mù looked worried, and said, "What is Master doing? If we summon him, will he come?" He replied, "A man who was as good as dead has been brought back to life; why wouldn't he come?" Zǐ Mù said, "If he doesn't come, then what should we do?" He replied, "Master will no longer stay. During the Spring and Autumn period, they served each other, in order to return Zhěn to the feudal lords. If you finance the bandits of Dōngyáng, and have them kill him, would that be acceptable? If not, he won't come." Zǐ Mù said, "That is unacceptable. I am a minister of Chǔ, and to bribe bandits to harm a man of Jìn is not righteous. You go and summon him for me; I will double his house." Then he sent Jiāo Míng to summon his father and bring him back.
6.5 《Wǔ Jǔ Lùn Tái Měi Ér Chǔ Dài》
King Líng of Chǔ built the Zhānghuá Terrace. He ascended it with Wǔ Jǔ and said, "The terrace is beautiful!" Wǔ Jǔ replied, "Your servant has heard that a ruler considers it beautiful to wear proper regalia, finds pleasure in pacifying the people, considers it wise to listen to virtuous advice, and considers it insightful to reach distant places. I have not heard that he considers the height of earth and timber and vermilion carvings beautiful, or considers the grandeur of metal, stone, gourds, and bamboo and clamorous crowds a source of joy. I have not heard that he considers it insightful to observe extravagance, gaze upon luxury, and indulge in licentious pleasures, or considers it wise to discern clarity and turbidity.
"The late ruler, King Zhuāng, built the Páojū Terrace, no higher than allowing one to observe the smoke of the state, no larger than to accommodate banquets and ritual vessels, its timber not hindering defense, its use not troubling the government, the people not delaying their seasonal tasks, and the officials not changing their regular duties. If one asked who feasted there, it was Duke Sòng and Earl Zhèng. If one asked who assisted in the ceremonies, it was Huá Yuán and Sì Fēi. I, your servant, do not understand its beauty.
"Now, as for what is beautiful, above and below, inside and outside, small and large, near and far, all are without harm, therefore it is called beautiful. If it is beautiful to the eye, but causes depletion when it comes to resources, it is hoarding the people's wealth to enrich oneself while impoverishing the people. How can it be beautiful? The one who governs a state will dwell together with the people. If the people are truly impoverished, how can the ruler be wealthy? Moreover, if private desires are excessively indulged, then virtuous conduct will be scarce. If virtuous conduct is not practiced, then those nearby will be restless and separated, and those far away will resist and disobey. The nobility of the Son of Heaven [Tiānzǐ] lies solely in employing dukes and marquises as officials, and counts, viscounts, and barons as the army. The origin of their fine reputation lies solely in bestowing virtuous governance on the near and far, and the small and great being content with it. If one gathers the people's wealth to fulfill their private desires, causing the people to be weary and forget their peace and happiness, and to harbor distant hearts, The evil it embodies is extreme. What need is there to look at it?
"Therefore, the purpose for which the former kings built terraces and pavilions was that pavilions were merely for practicing military drills, and terraces were merely for observing atmospheric omens. Therefore, the size of pavilions was determined by the accommodation of large troops, and the height of terraces was determined by the height from which observations could be made. They did not seize arable land, and their construction did not deplete resources. Their construction did not burden official duties, and their construction did not interfere with seasonal work. Barren and infertile land was where they built them; timber used for city defense was what they used; officials' leisure time was when they supervised; and the gaps between the four seasons were when they completed them. Therefore, the *Zhou Shi* (Book of Odes of Zhou) says: 'They began to build the Língtái (Spirit Terrace), planning and constructing it. The common people worked on it, completing it in no time. Beginning the construction, they did not rush, and the common people came like children. The king was in the Língyòu (Spirit Park), "The doe deer peacefully lie down." "Now, to construct a pavilion," "is meant to teach the people about benefit," "but they do not understand that it is actually exhausting them." "If Your Lordship calls this pavilion beautiful and insists on its correctness," "then Chǔ is probably in danger!"
6.6 Fàn Wúyǔ discusses how building large cities is not beneficial to the state.
King Líng built cities in Chén, Cài, and Bùgēng. He sent his servant Zǐ Xī to ask Fàn Wúyǔ, saying: "The various Xia states do not submit to us but exclusively serve Jìn. Why is this? Only because Jìn is near and we are far. Now I have built cities in three states, each with a revenue of a thousand chariots. This is equivalent to Jìn. And added to that is Chǔ, will the feudal lords come to us then?" He replied: "The key lies in the intention. Building large cities for a state, has never been beneficial. In the past, Zhèng had Jīng, Lì; Wèi had Pú, Qī; Sòng had Xiāo, Méng, Lǔ had Biàn and Fèi, Qí had Qúqiū, Jìn had Qūwò, Qín had Zhēng and Yá. Shū Duàn, with Jīng, caused worry for Zhuāng Gōng; Zhèng nearly did not succeed. The person of Lì truly caused the son of Zhèng to not attain his position. The Pú and Qī of Wèi truly expelled Xiàn Gōng. The Xiāo and Méng of Sòng truly murdered Zhāo Gōng. The Biàn and Fèi of Lǔ truly weakened Xiāng Gōng. The Qúqiū of Qí truly killed Wúzhī. The Qūwò of Jìn truly admitted the Qí army. The Zhēng and Yá of Qín truly troubled Huán and Jǐng. All had ambitions regarding the feudal lords. These were the disadvantages of such actions.
"Furthermore, the control of cities and towns is like (governing) the human body. There are head, neck, limbs, even down to fingers, toes, hair, and veins. The large can easily control the small, therefore, changes occur without much effort. The land has highs and lows, the sky has darkness and light, The people have rulers and ministers, the state has capitals and suburbs; these are ancient institutions. The former kings feared that they would not be followed, therefore they regulated them with righteousness, implemented them with attire, practiced them with ritual, distinguished them with titles, recorded them in writing, and guided them with speech. Once they are lost, the reasons for changing things [arise]. Now, the borders are the tail of the state, like cattle and horses. When the height of summer arrives, and the flies and gadflies become numerous, if it cannot wag its tail, I, your minister, am afraid of it. If not, these three cities would surely cause the hearts of the feudal lords to tremble."
Zǐ Xī (子晳) reported back, and the king said: "He knows how close Heaven is, but how does he know the rules of the people? These are absurd words." Yòu Yǐn Zǐgé was in attendance, and said, "The people are born of Heaven. To know Heaven, one must know the people. Are these words not frightening!" Three years later, the people of Chén, Cài, and Bùgēng installed Qì Jí and assassinated Líng Wáng.
6.7 "The Left Historian Yǐ Xiàng Admonishes Shēn Gōngzǐ Wěi"
The Left Historian Yǐ Xiàng went to visit Shēn Gōngzǐ Wěi, but Zǐ Wěi did not come out. The Left Historian criticized him and used Bó to report it. Zǐ Wěi became angry and came out, saying, "Are you not also saying that I am old and feeble and abandoning me, and now you slander me!"
The Left Historian Yǐ Xiàng said, "Precisely because you are old and feeble, I desired to see you in order to mutually admonish you. If you were in your prime, capable of managing all affairs, Yǐ Xiàng would be running about taking care of things in order, and being insufficient at that, How could you possibly find the time to see him? In the past, Wèi Wǔ Gōng 衛武公 was ninety-five years old, yet he still offered admonitions and warnings to the state. He said: "From the ministers down to the teachers and officers, anyone who is in court, do not say that I am old and senile and abandon me. You must be respectful and diligent in court, and warn me morning and night. If you hear one or two words of advice, you must remember them and accept them, in order to instruct and guide me." When he was in his carriage, there were the regulations of the guards; when he was at ease, there were the ordinances of the officials and teachers; when he leaned on his armrest, there were remonstrances from those who recited instructions; when he was in his bedroom, there were admonitions from the intimate attendants; when he attended to affairs, there was guidance from the blind historians; when he was at leisure, there were recitations from the music masters. The historians did not fail to record, and the blind did not fail to recite, in order to instruct and control him. Thus, he composed the "Yì" (懿) (Admonitions) to warn himself. And when he died, he was called the wise and sage Wǔ Gōng 武公. You are certainly not as wise and sage-like, so what harm could relying on an advisor do? The *Zhōu Shū* 周書 says: "Wén Wáng, even when the sun reached its zenith and then declined , did not dare to take time for leisure or food. He was kind to the common people and exceedingly respectful in matters of governance." Wén Wáng still dared not be arrogant. Now, you are growing old in the state of Chǔ and wish to rest in ease, using guards to ward off frequent admonishments. What will the King do? If things continue as they are, Chǔ will surely be in trouble!" Zǐ Wěi said: "It is my fault for being old." Thereupon, he quickly summoned the Grand Scribe.
6.8 《Bái Gōngzǐ Zhāng Fěng Líng Wáng Yí Nà Jiàn》 (Bái Gōngzǐ Zhāng Satirizes Líng Wáng for Being Receptive to Criticism)
Líng Wáng was tyrannical, and Bái Gōngzǐ Zhāng frequently remonstrated with him. The King was troubled by this and said to the Old Scribe: "I wish to put an end to Zǐ Zhāng's remonstrances. What should I do?" The Old Scribe replied: "To employ his advice is truly difficult, but to silence it is easy. If he remonstrates, your Majesty can say: 'In my left hand I hold the "Guǐ Zhōng" (Demon Suppressor), "You hold the position of Shāng Palace," "all the countless admonitions and remonstrations," "I have heard them all," "why would I listen to other words?"
Báigōng again remonstrated, but the King followed the words of Shǐ Lǎo. Báigōng replied, "In the past, Yīn Wǔdīng was able to elevate his virtue," "to the point of divine enlightenment," "to the point of entering the Hé River," "from the Hé to Cú Bó," "whereupon he remained silent for three years to contemplate the Dao." "The high officials worried about this," "saying," "'The King's words are used to issue orders," "if he does not speak," "then there is nothing from which to receive orders.'" "Wǔdīng then wrote a document," "saying," "'Because I rectify the four quarters," "I fear that my virtue is not up to the task," "therefore, I do not speak.'" "Thereafter, he even used dreams and omens to seek worthy men from all around," "and obtained Fù Yuè and brought him here," "promoted him to the position of Duke," "and had him counsel and remonstrate morning and night," "saying," "If (I am like) gold, use you as a whetstone. If (I am like) a fordable stream, use you as a boat. If there is a drought, use you as copious rain. Open up your heart, enrich my heart. If medicine doesn't cause dizziness, the illness will not be cured. If one walks barefoot without looking at the ground, one's feet will surely be injured." Although Wǔ Dīng was so intelligent and insightful, his sagacity was so profound and vast, and his wisdom was not hasty, he still considered himself not yet well-governed, therefore he remained silent for three years to contemplate the Way. Having attained the Way, he still dared not act arbitrarily, and sent Yǐ Xiàng to seek out a sage to assist him. Having found someone to serve as his assistant, he still feared he might become negligent, lose his way, or forget, so he had people advise, teach, and remonstrate with him morning and night, saying, "You must mutually cultivate me, and not let me abandon (the right path)." Now, perhaps you are not as good as Wǔ Dīng, yet you hate those who offer advice and remonstrance— Is it not difficult!
Qí Huán and Jìn Wén, neither of them were the designated successors. They controlled and pacified the various lords, not daring to indulge in excessive pleasures. Their hearts were akin to virtuous sounds, and they possessed the kingdom through virtue. Close ministers offered remonstrances, distant ministers voiced criticisms, and the common people sang praises, all as a means of self-admonishment. Therefore, when they entered [a state], the four borders were not uniformly the same, and yet they arrived at having bordering fields, to attach to the feudal lords, and even now they are considered exemplary rulers. Both Huán and Wén were like this. You, O King, do not consider the anxieties of these two exemplary rulers, but wish to indulge yourself in ease. Would that not be inappropriate? The *Book of Zhou* has a saying: 'If you do not act personally and are not close [to the people], the common people will not trust you.' Your servant fears that the people will not trust you, therefore I dare not refrain from speaking. Otherwise, "Why are you so eager to take the blame for his words?"
The king was annoyed by this and said: "You may speak again. Even if I cannot use it, I will still be willing to listen." He replied: "It is because I rely on Your Majesty's willingness to use it that I speak. Therefore, I speak. If not, could the rhinoceros of Bāpǔ, the yak, the rhinoceros, and the elephant be exhausted? Would they then use compasses as earrings?" Thereupon, he hurried away and retreated, returned home, and did not go out behind closed doors. In the seventh month, there was then the rebellion of Gān Xī, and Líng Wáng died because of it.
6.9 "Zuǒ Shǐ Yǐ Xiāng Warns Sīmǎ Zǐqī to Follow the Way Only"
Sīmǎ Zǐqī wanted to make his concubine his primary wife. He consulted Zuǒ Shǐ Yǐ Xiāng, saying: "I have a desirable concubine and wish to perform the hairpin ceremony for her. "Is that acceptable?" He replied: "Formerly, the late minister Zǐnáng disobeyed the king's order regarding posthumous titles; Zǐxī had a fondness for water caltrops, Zǐmù had someone send him mutton, but did not offer water caltrops with it. The gentleman said: 'To disobey is the right way.' The servant of Gǔyáng, cherishing Zǐfǎn's labor, presented him with drink, causing him to die in Yan; Yùyǐn Shēn Hài followed the desires of King Líng, causing him to perish in Gān Xī. The gentleman said: 'To follow is to go against.' The gentleman's conduct desires the right way, therefore, in advancing and retreating, circling and turning, he only follows the right way. Now, Zǐmù was able to disobey Ruò'áo's desires, using the right way to remove the water caltrop offering. You, sir, are managing the state of Chu, and yet you want to offer water caltrops to entice him, is that acceptable?" Zǐqī then stopped.
6.10 "Guān Shèfù's Discourse on Severing the Connection Between Heaven and Earth"
Zhāo Wáng asked Guān Yè Fǔ, saying, "The *Zhōu Shū* says that Zhòng and Lí were indeed those who caused Heaven and Earth to not communicate. What does it mean? If it were not so, would the people be able to ascend to Heaven?"
He replied, "That is not what it means. In ancient times, the people and the gods were not mixed. Those whose spiritual essence was not distracted or divided, and who could also be reverent, solemn, sincere, and upright, whose wisdom could compare affairs above and below, whose sagacity could brightly and distantly proclaim, whose clarity could illuminate, whose hearing could thoroughly perceive, like this, then the bright spirits would descend to them. Among men, they were called *xí*; among women, they were called *wū*. This enabled them to regulate the places and positions of the spirits, and prepare for them sacrificial animals, vessels, seasonal attire, and then enabled the descendants of former sages to possess glorious achievements, and to know the names of the mountains and rivers, the ancestral spirits, the affairs of the ancestral temples, the generations of *zhāo* and *mù*, Qí jìng zhī qín, observe propriety and decorum, follow the rules of majestic bearing, maintain dignified appearance, possess the quality of loyalty and trustworthiness, and wear pure and clean garments, and reverently attend to the bright spirits, were made the *zhù* (invocators/prayers). Those descendants of families who knew the generation of the four seasons, the kinds of sacrificial animals, the types of jade and silk, the rituals of ceremonial attire, the measures of ritual vessels, the standards for ranking the ancestral tablets, the positions of screens and attendants, the location of altars and sacred grounds, the gods above and below, and the origins of clans and surnames, and whose hearts followed the old regulations, were made the *zōng* (masters of ceremony/ancestral guardians). Thus, there were officials for Heaven, Earth, spirits, people, and categories of things; these were called the Five Officials, each administering his order, not interfering with each other. The people were thus able to have loyalty and trust, and the spirits were thus able to have bright virtue. The people and spirits had different tasks, they were revered but not defiled, Therefore, the divine brought down auspicious births; the people used goods to make offerings; disasters and calamities did not arrive; and their requests were never exhausted.
"When Shǎo Hào's 少暭 reign declined, the Jiǔ Lí 九黎 threw morality into disarray; the people and spirits were mixed together; and things could not be distinguished. Every man made offerings; every household was a shaman and a historian; and there was no essential quality. The people were impoverished by sacrifices and did not know their blessings. The seasonal offerings were without measure; the people and spirits were in the same position. The people disregarded solemn covenants; and there was no severe awe. The spirits were familiar with the people's rules; and did not purify their actions. Auspicious births were not brought down; and there were no things with which to make offerings. Disasters and calamities came frequently; and no one could exhaust their effects. Zhuān Xū 顓頊 received this situation and then ordered the Southern Administrator Chóng 重 to be in charge of the heavens, to govern the spirits; and ordered the Fire Administrator Lí 黎 to be in charge of the earth, to govern the people; to restore the old order; Not encroaching on or defiling each other, this is called severing the connection between earth and heaven.
"After that, the Three Miao restored the virtue of the Nine Li, Yao restored the descendants of Chóng Lí, not forgetting the old, and made them govern it again. As for Xia and Shang, therefore the Chóng and Lí clans successively arranged heaven and earth, and distinguished those who were in charge of their respective divisions. In the Zhou dynasty, Chéng Bó Xiūfù was a descendant of them. During the time of King Xuān, he lost his official position, and became the Sima clan. He revered his ancestors as gods, in order to gain authority over the people, saying: 'Chóng embodies the upper heaven, Lí embodies the lower earth.' Encountering the chaos of the world, and no one could resist it. Otherwise, since heaven and earth are formed and unchanging, why should there be any comparison?"
6.11 "Guān Shèfǔ's Discussion on Sacrificial Animals"
Zǐqī was performing a sacrifice for King Píng, offering a sacrificial bull on a stand to the King. The King asked Guān Shèfǔ, saying, "To what extent should sacrificial animals be used?" He replied, "The sacrifice should be increased from the daily offering. The Son of Heaven's daily offering is a *dàláo* (complete sacrificial animal), the sacrifice is a *huì* (a large assembly of offerings); a feudal lord's daily offering is a single bull, the sacrifice is a *tàiláo* (a complete sacrificial animal); a minister's daily offering is a *shǎoláo* (lesser sacrificial animal), the sacrifice is a single bull; a grand master's daily offering is a single animal, the sacrifice is a *shǎoláo*; a scholar eats roasted fish, the sacrifice is a single animal; common people eat vegetables, the sacrifice is fish. When superiors and inferiors are in order, the people will not be disrespectful."
The King said, "How about their smallness and largeness?" He replied, "The sacrifices at the suburban altar and *dì* ceremony should not exceed silkworm cocoons and chestnuts, "The zhēng and cháng sacrifices should not exceed what can be grasped." The king said, "How small is that?" He replied, "The spirits use refined brightness to oversee the people, therefore, they seek completeness in offerings, not lavish abundance. Thus, the sacrifices of the former kings used one pure offering, two refined offerings, three sacrificial animals, four seasons, five colors, six musical pitches, seven affairs, eight kinds of crops, nine sacrifices, ten days, twelve zodiacal branches to achieve this. The common people, a thousand articles, ten thousand officials, hundreds of millions of categories, countless people, all contribute and offer them. Illuminate it with brilliant virtue, listen to it with harmonious sounds. Report the offerings thoroughly, then none will fail to receive blessings. "Presenting hair to indicate the offering, blood to announce the killing, sincerely selecting and taking out the best to offer as provisions, this is to show respect during the sacrifice. Respect cannot be sustained for long, the people's strength cannot bear it, therefore, solemn reverence should be adopted to carry it on."
The king said: "How much livestock is offered?" The minister replied: "For those from afar, no more than three months' supply; for those nearby, no more than ten days' supply." The king said: "Can sacrifices not be stopped?" The minister replied: "Sacrifices are for manifesting filial piety and giving the people respite, for comforting the state, and settling the populace; they cannot be stopped. If the people's spirit is unrestrained, it will sink; if it sinks, it will become stagnant; if it remains stagnant for long without being roused, life will not flourish. If their resources are not properly used, their lives will not flourish; they cannot be entrusted with territory. Therefore, the ancient sage kings had daily sacrifices, Yuè xiǎng (monthly offerings), shí lèi (seasonal categories), suì sì (annual sacrifices). Zhū hóu (feudal lords) offer sacrifices daily, qīng (ministers) and dà fū (grand officers) offer them monthly, shì (scholar-officials) and shù rén (common people) offer them seasonally. The Tiānzǐ (Son of Heaven) widely sacrifices to all kinds of gods and natural objects. Zhū hóu (feudal lords) sacrifice to Tiāndì (Heaven and Earth), Sān chén (the sun, moon, and stars), and the mountains and rivers within their territory. Qīng (ministers) and dà fū (grand officers) sacrifice according to their ritual rank, shì (scholar-officials) and shù rén (common people) do not go beyond sacrificing to their ancestors. When the sun and moon meet at the dragon tail, and the earth's qi is contained and gathered, the sky becomes bright and prosperous deeds arise, all good fortune is fully bestowed, and the gods frequently travel. Therefore, the state performs zhēng cháng (winter and autumn sacrifices), and families perform cháng sì (autumn sacrifices). Common people, husbands and wives, choose an auspicious day, offer their sacrificial animals, reverently prepare their grains, cleanse their grounds, carefully choose their attire, purely offer their wine and sweet wine, lead their children and grandchildren, and follow the seasonal offerings. They are devout in their prayers and ancestral worship, articulating their proper words, In order to clearly sacrifice to their ancestors, solemnly and respectfully, as if they were present. Thereupon he united his district's villagers, friends, and marital relations, drawing together brothers, relatives. Thereupon he eliminated all sorts of troubles, extinguished slander and wickedness, united them in auspiciousness, strengthened their intimacy, harmonized those above and below, in order to consolidate his clan. Those above thereby teach the people reverence, those below thereby show respect in serving those above. In the Son of Heaven's *dì* sacrifice and suburban sacrifices, he must personally shoot his sacrificial animal; the Queen must personally pound her grain. In the feudal lords' ancestral temple affairs, they must personally shoot oxen, slaughter sheep, and kill pigs; the Lady must personally pound the sacrificial grain. How much more so the people below, who would dare not be trembling with caution, in order to serve the hundred spirits! The Son of Heaven personally pounds the grain for the *dì* and suburban sacrifices, the Queen personally reels the silk for the sacrificial garments, from the dukes down to the common people, who would dare not be solemn, respectful, and diligently devoted to the spirits! "It is that by which the people are held together and secured, how could one abandon it!"
The king said, "What are the so-called 'one purity', 'two essences', and 'seven affairs'?"
He replied, "The sagely king correctly wore the duān miǎn (ceremonial cap), because it did not violate his heart (intent), leading his assembled ministers in refining things to oversee and attend to sacrifices, not having any harshness or evil towards the spirits; this is called 'one purity'. Jade and silk are the 'two essences'. Heaven, earth, the people, and the affairs of the four seasons are the 'seven affairs'." The king said, "What are the 'three affairs'?"
He replied, "Heaven's affair is martial (wǔ), earth's affair is civil (wén), the people's affair is loyalty and trustworthiness." The king said, "What is meant by bǎixìng (the common people), qiānpǐn (thousands of grades), wànguān (ten thousand officials), "What are the 'hundred million ugly' and the 'trillion people' that enter the calculation of '垓' (gāi, a large number)? " The answer is: "The people who are thoroughly versed in their duties as officials are the sons and younger brothers of kings and dukes who are capable of speaking and listening and are thoroughly versed in their duties. Things are bestowed and surnames given to supervise their offices. These are called the 'bǎixìng' (百姓, common people). Surnames have thorough ranks. Ten times that of the king is called 'thousand ranks'. The officials in charge of the five types of resources, with ten thousand attendants, are called 'ten thousand officials'. Officials have ten 'chǒu' (醜, ugliness), which are called 'hundred million ugly'. The Son of Heaven has fields of nine 'gāi' (垓, a large number) to feed the trillion people. The king takes what enters into it to feed the ten thousand officials."
6.12 *Zǐcháng* Questions the Accumulation of Goods, Gathering of Horses, and *Dòu Qiě's* Argument That They Will Inevitably Perish
*Dòu Qiě* *wàng* saw the *lìngyǐn* (prime minister) *Zǐcháng*. *Zǐcháng* spoke with him and asked about accumulating goods and gathering horses. He returned and told his younger brother, saying: "Chǔ is probably going to perish! 不然， the *lìngyǐn* (prime minister) will likely not escape (disaster). I saw the *lìngyǐn*; the *lìngyǐn* asked about accumulating and storing wealth like a hungry jackal or wolf. He is probably someone who will certainly be ruined.
"In ancient times, accumulating goods did not obstruct the people's benefit of clothing and food; accumulating horses did not harm the people's wealth and resources. The state's horses were sufficient for conducting military campaigns, and the government's horses were sufficient for evaluating taxes. This was not excessive. The government's goods were sufficient for hosting guests and offering tributes, and the household's goods were sufficient for common use. This was not excessive. If goods and horses are hoarded, then the people will lack, and if the people lack greatly, then they will have thoughts of separation and rebellion. How will you secure your fief then?
"In the past, Dòu Zǐwén (鬭子文) thrice relinquished the position of *lìngyǐn*, and did not accumulate wealth for even a single day, because he was concerned about the people's welfare. King Chéng (成王) heard that Zǐwén's (子文) provisions did not last from morning till evening. Thereupon, every morning he provided him with a bundle of dried meat and a basket of dried grain to present to Zǐwén (子文). To this day, the *lìngyǐn*'s (令尹) are ranked according to this standard. Whenever King Chéngwáng gave Zǐ Wén his salary, he would always flee. The king would stop him, and then he would return. Someone said to Zǐ Wén: "People seek wealth in life, but you flee from it. Why is this?" He replied: "Those who govern do so to protect the people. If the people are mostly impoverished, and I take wealth, it is exhausting the people to enrich myself. Death will come quickly. I am fleeing death, not fleeing wealth." Therefore, during the reign of King Zhuāngwáng, the Ruò'áo clan was exterminated, but only Zǐ Wén's descendants remained. Even now, they reside in Yún, serving as good ministers of Chǔ. Is this not putting the people's concerns before one's own wealth?
"Now Zǐ Cháng is a descendant of a great official, and serves as minister to the ruler of Chǔ, but has no good reputation in all directions. The weakness and hunger of the people The sun is already far gone. The four borders are filled with ramparts, corpses line the roads, visible everywhere, thieves and bandits watch with eyes open, the people have nowhere to turn. To not care about this, and yet accumulate wealth without satisfaction, the resentment of the people will quickly grow. Accumulating goods more and more, storing up resentment deeper and deeper, if this does not lead to ruin, what are we waiting for?
"The anger in the hearts of the people is like guarding a great river; if it bursts, the devastation it causes will surely be great. Can Zǐcháng possibly be more capable than Chéng and Líng? Chéng was disrespectful to Mù, wishing to eat bear paws, but did not get them and died. Líng did not care for the people, and the whole country abandoned him, like discarding a footprint. Zǐcháng governs, and is without respect and without care, even more so than Chéng and Líng. What strength does he alone have to withstand it!" A year later, Thereupon was the Battle of Bó Jǔ; Zǐ Cháng fled to Zhèng, and King Zhāo fled to Suí.
6.13 "Lán Yǐn Wěi avoids King Zhāo and is not recorded."
The Wú people entered Chǔ, King Zhāo fled, crossing at Chéng Jiù, and saw Lán Yǐn Wěi carrying his family. The king said: "Give me a ride." He replied: "Since the former kings, none have lost their state; when it is lost under your rule, it is your fault." He then left the king. The king returned, and again sought to see him. The king wanted to seize him. Zǐ Xī said: "Please hear his words, for he must have a reason." The king sent someone to say to him: "During the battle at Chéng Jiù, you abandoned me, now you dare to come, why?" He said: "Formerly, Wǎ Wéi harbored old grudges and was defeated at Bǎi Jǔ, therefore, you, my lord, have come to this point. Now you are repeating his actions; wouldn't that be inadvisable? I fled to Chéng Jiù to warn you, my lord, hoping you would repent and change your ways. The reason I dare appear before you now is to observe your virtue, saying: 'Perhaps you will remember the fear and reflect on your past wrongdoings?' If you, my lord, do not reflect but instead continue on this path, then you truly possess the state but do not cherish it. What do I have to fear from death? ◇◇ Death lies in the hands of the Sī Bài (Minister of Justice)! Only you, my lord, should consider this!" Zǐ Xī said: "Reinstate him to his former position so that he does not forget the previous defeat." The king then received him.
6.14 "Yún Gōng Xīn and his younger brother Huái either pay respects to the ruler or pay respects to their father."
When the Wú people invaded Chǔ, King Zhāo fled to Yún. Yún Gōng's younger brother, Huái, intended to assassinate the king, but Yún Gōng Xīn stopped him. Huái said: "Píng Wáng killed my father. If he is in the state, he is the ruler; if he is outside the state, he is my enemy. To see one's enemy and not kill him is not the act of a human being." Yūn Gōng said: "One who serves a ruler does not act based on external or internal considerations, nor make decisions based on plenty or scarcity. If he is your ruler, then high and low are one and the same. Moreover, only those below an equal can be enemies; otherwise, there is no enmity. When a subordinate oppresses a superior, it is called regicide; when a superior oppresses a subordinate, it is called punishment. How much more so with a ruler! If a ruler punishes a subject, what enmity is there? If everyone avenged themselves on their ruler, then what distinction would there be between superior and subordinate? My ancestors served their rulers well, achieving fame among the feudal lords. From Dòu Bó Bǐ onward, we have never failed in this. Now you would bring calamity upon us with this; it is not permissible." Huái did not listen He said: "I am thinking of my father, and cannot attend to other matters." Yún Gōng followed the King as he fled.
When the King returned, the rewards extended to Yún and Huái. Zǐ Xī remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty has two ministers, one of whom is worthy of reward, and the other worthy of execution. If Your Majesty treats them equally, the ministers will be fearful." The King said: "Are you referring to the two sons of Fū Zǐ Qī? I understand. One shows propriety to the ruler, and the other shows propriety to his father. To treat them equally, is it not acceptable?"
6.15 "Lán Yǐn Wěi Discusses the Impending Fall of Wú"
Zǐ Xī sighed in court. Lán Yǐn Wěi said: "I have heard that a gentleman only sighs when alone, contemplating the rise and fall of past dynasties, or when attending funerals and mourning. Only then does he sigh; otherwise, he does not. When a gentleman oversees government, he considers righteousness; when eating and drinking, he considers propriety; when at a shared feast, he considers joy; in joy, he remembers the past; there is no occasion for lamentation. Now, my lord, you oversee government and lament; why is this?" Zǐ Xī said: "Hé Lǘ was able to defeat our army. Hé Lǘ has already passed away, and I hear that his successor is even worse. That is why I lament."
He replied: "You should worry about the lack of cultivation of governmental virtue, and not worry about Wú. Hé Lǘ's mouth did not crave delicacies, his ears did not delight in indulgent sounds, his eyes did not lust after beauty, his body did not indulge in comfort, he diligently applied his will morning and evening, cared for the weariness of the people, he was startled when he heard a good word, he rewarded the acquisition of a worthy man, he certainly repented of any wrongdoing, and he certainly feared any unwholesomeness. Therefore, he won the people to fulfill his ambitions. Now, I hear that Fū Chāi is fond of exhausting the people's strength to fulfill his private desires, If they indulge in excesses and obstruct remonstrance, in a single night's stay, towers and pavilions, ponds and embankments, will surely be built, and the six domestic animals and playthings will surely be acquired. Fūchā is already defeated by his own actions, how can he defeat others? If you cultivate virtue and wait for Wú, Wú will surely perish."
6.16 "Wángsūn Yǔ Discusses the Treasures of a State"
Wángsūn Yǔ was on a diplomatic mission to Jìn. Duke Dìng feasted him. Zhào Jiǎnzi, with jade tinkling, assisted in the ceremony, and asked Wángsūn Yǔ, saying: "Is the white *héng*-stone of Chǔ still there?" He replied: "Yes." Jiǎn zi said: "How much is it valued as a treasure?"
He said: "It has never been valued as a treasure. What Chǔ treasures is Guān Shèfù, who can compose instructive speeches to conduct affairs with the various lords, Make sure you do not use my lord's shortcomings as fodder for gossip. Furthermore, there is the Left Historiographer Yǐ Xiàng, who can expound on exemplary teachings, and classify all things, presenting successes and failures to my lord morning and evening, ensuring my lord does not forget the achievements of the former kings; he can also communicate with the spirits above and below, understanding their likes and dislikes, ensuring the spirits hold no resentment or pain towards the state of Chǔ. Furthermore, there is the marshland called Yúnlián Túzhōu, where metal, wood, bamboo, and arrows are produced. Tortoise shells, pearls, horns, teeth, hides, leather, feathers, and hair are what we prepare as taxes, to be prepared for unforeseen circumstances. These are used to provide ceremonial gifts, to entertain the lords of the various states. If the ceremonial gifts for the lords are complete, and they are guided with instructive words, and there are preparations for unforeseen circumstances, and the august spirits assist us, then my lord may be able to avoid blame from the lords, and the people will be protected. These are the treasures of the state of Chǔ. As for the Bái Héng pendant, it is merely a plaything of the former kings, Hé bǎo zhī yān?
"I have heard that the treasures of a state are but six things. If an enlightened king and sage can regulate and manage all things, so as to assist the state, then they are treasured; if jade is sufficient to shelter and nourish fine crops, so as to prevent disasters of flood and drought, then it is treasured; if tortoises are sufficient to determine good and evil, then they are treasured; if pearls are sufficient to ward off fire disasters, then they are treasured; if gold is sufficient to ward off military disorder, then it is treasured; if mountains, forests, marshes, and swamps are sufficient to provide resources, then they are treasured. As for the beauty of clamorous displays, even though Chǔ is a barbarian state, it would not treasure them."
6.17 "Lǔ Yáng Wénzǐ Declines the Offer of Liáng from King Huì"
King Huì offered Liáng to Lǔ Yáng Wénzǐ, Wénzǐ declined, saying: "Liáng is strategically located within our territory, I fear that my descendants might be disloyal. Now, serving one's lord without resentment is ideal; resentment leads to fear of coercion, and coercion leads to fear of disloyalty. One who is full (of merit) but not coercive, one who holds resentment but is not disloyal, that minister can preserve himself; I know nothing else. Even if indulging me allows me to die with my head and neck intact, I fear that my descendants, relying on the dangerous terrain of Liáng, will lack sacrifices to me." The king said, "You are a benevolent man, not forgetting your descendants, and extending your concern to the state of Chǔ; how dare I not follow your wishes?" He gave him Lǔyáng.
6.18 Yè Gōng Zǐ Gāo Discusses How Bái Gōng Shèng Will Inevitably Throw the State of Chǔ into Chaos
Zǐxī sent someone to summon Wángsūn Shèng. Shěn Zhūliáng heard of it and went to see Zǐxī, saying, "I heard that you summoned Wángsūn Shèng; is that true?" He said, "Yes." Zǐgāo said, "Where would you employ him?" He said: "I have heard that Shèng is upright and strong, I wish to place him in a border region."
Zǐ Gāo said: "It is not permissible. As for his character, he is verbose but untrustworthy, loving but unkind, deceitful but not wise, resolute but not courageous, upright but not sincere, comprehensive in speech but not virtuous. Repeatedly speaking without considering his own well-being, that is verbosity (zhǎn); loving without considering long-term benefits, that is unkindness (bù rén); using schemes to overshadow others, that is deceit (zhà); forcibly enduring to violate righteousness, that is resoluteness (yì); being upright without consideration, that is insincerity (bù zhōng); speaking comprehensively but abandoning virtue, that is lack of goodness (bù shū). These six virtues All of them have their flourish but lack substance; what use would they be?
"His father was killed in Chǔ, and his heart is both narrow-minded and impure. If he is narrow-minded, he will not forget old grievances, and instead of cleansing his virtue with purity, he only thinks of seeking revenge. Then his affection would be enough to win people over, his abilities would be enough to avenge himself, his deceit would be enough to plot, his straightforwardness would be enough to lead, his thoroughness would be enough to cover up, his impurity would be enough to carry things out, and adding to that his lack of benevolence, and upholding him with injustice, there is nothing he would not be able to overcome.
"Those who created the grievances for victory are all gone. If he comes and receives no favor, his anger will quickly arise. If he is favored, he will be resolutely greedy and insatiable, and having gained the trust of the people, and enticing them with great profits, nourishing him with unkindness, He harbors past grievances to cultivate his ambition; should the state have an opening he surely would not remain. If you, Zǐzhí, do not employ him, then who will? He will dwell on past grievances and desire great favor, he moves and gains men's approval, he bears grudges and possesses methods; if he is indeed employed, harm can be awaited. I cherish Zǐ and Sīmǎ, therefore, I dare not remain silent."
Zǐxī said: "Virtue should cause him to forget his grievances! I will treat him well, then he will be at peace." Zǐgāo said: "That is not so. I have heard it said, only the benevolent man can be liked, can be disliked, can be elevated, can be brought low. When liked, he does not become overbearing; when disliked, he does not resent; when elevated, he does not become arrogant; when brought low, he does not fear. Those who are not benevolent are different. If people like them, they will oppress; if they hate them, they will resent; if you elevate them, they will become arrogant; if you demean them, they will be fearful. Arrogance has desires, fear has hates, desire, hate, resentment, oppression, are the means by which deceitful schemes are born. What are you going to do? If you summon and lower them, they will be saddened and fearful; if you treat them as superiors, they will become angry and resentful. The heart of deceitful schemes will have no place to rest. Even one act of injustice can ruin a state. Now, one, five, or six of such people you insist on using, isn't it difficult? I have heard that when a state is about to fall, it must use treacherous people and crave their harmful flavors. Is this not what they are talking about?
"Who is without faults and flaws? Those who are capable will remove them early. Destroying a lineage due to old grievances , is a grave calamity for a state . Even if one constructs gates and barriers to keep it far away and prepare for it , one still fears its arrival . This is called being vigilant every day . If one summons it and brings it close , death will come without delay . People have a saying : "A wolf cub has a wild heart , so it is with a vengeful and rebellious person ." What good can they possibly do? If you, my lord, do not believe me , why not seek out the descendants of Ruò Áo Shì, Zǐyú , and Zǐxī and bring them close? How can you hope to win ? How much (good) can they do?
"In the past, the Qí official Zōumǎ Xū led Hú Gōng into the Bèi River , Bǐng Chù and Yán Zhí assassinated Yì Gōng in the Yuòzhú hunting park , in Jìn, Chángyú Jiǎo killed the three Xì in the pavilion , in Lǔ, the warden Yǔrén Luò killed Zǐ Bān in his chamber . What was the cause of all this ? Was it not old grievances? These are all things you have heard . People seek to hear much about success and failure , in order to learn from them Now that you have heard it and reject it, you are still deaf. What good would it do for me to tell you anything? I know I must flee."
Zǐxī 子西 laughed and said: "You are still seeking to prevail." He did not heed him and consequently made him Báigōng 白公. Zǐ Gāo 子高 retired to Cài 蔡 due to illness. When the Báigōng 白公 rebellion occurred, Zǐxī 子西 and Zǐ Qī 子期 died. Yè Gōng 葉公 heard of it and said: "I resent him for rejecting my words, but I appreciate his governing of the state of Chǔ 楚. He is the one who enabled the state of Chǔ 楚 to be stable and restore the work of the former kings. It was he. To place a small resentment above a great virtue would be unrighteous of me. I will go in and kill him." He led troops from beyond Fāngchéng 方城 to enter, killed Báigōng 白公 and stabilized the royal house, and buried the clans of the two men.
*Wú Yǔ* 吳語 7.1 *Yuè Wáng Gōujiàn Mìng Zhū Jī Yǐng Xíng Chéng Yú Wú* 越王句踐命諸稽郢行成於吳 (King Gōujiàn 句踐 of Yuè 越 Orders Zhū Jī Yǐng 諸稽郢 to Negotiate Peace with Wú 吳)
King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吳 raised an army to attack Yuè 越. King Gōujiàn 句踐 of Yuè 越 raised an army to meet him. The grand master Zhǒng 種 then offered a plan, saying: "Whether Wú 吳 or Yuè 越 prevails, is solely determined by Heaven. Your Majesty should not engage in battle. Shēn Xū 申胥 and Huá Dēng 華登 have been training the soldiers of Wú 吳 with armor and weapons, and have never experienced defeat. Even if one man is skilled in archery, a hundred men can prepare the arrows; victory cannot be assured. A plan must foresee success in its initial stages before it is implemented, one cannot entrust everything to fate. Your Majesty should instead prepare for war, but send envoys with conciliatory words to sue for peace, in order to please their people, and to inflate the pride of King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吳. I will consult Heaven through divination. If Heaven intends to abandon Wú 吳, it will surely grant our peace and yet not satisfy them, and they will certainly have the magnanimous ambition to be the hegemon of all lords. Once they have exhausted their people, and Heaven deprives them of food, who will willingly receive their burning remnants? Then they will have no mandate left."
King of Yuè agreed, and then ordered Zhūjī Yǐng to negotiate peace with Wú, saying: "My lord, Gōujiàn, sends his humble servant Yǐng, daring not openly present gifts and perform ceremonies, but dare privately inform the underlings, saying: In the past, the state of Yuè encountered misfortune and offended the Heavenly King. The Heavenly King personally deigned to visit, showing compassion to the orphaned Gōujiàn, and furthermore pardoned him. Your Majesty's treatment of Yuè is like reviving the dead and adding flesh to the bones. I dare not forget the heavenly disaster, how dare I forget Your Majesty's great gift! Now Gōujiàn, repeatedly beset by misfortune and lacking virtue, a humble and insignificant person, dares to forget the Heavenly King's great virtue, and dwell on petty grievances along the border, thereby further offending the underlings? Gōujiàn employs two or three old men as commanders, personally entrusting them with heavy responsibilities, kowtowing at the border.
Now if Your Majesty does not investigate, but directs troops in great anger, intending to devastate and attack the state of Yuè, the state of Yuè is inherently a tribute-paying city. The king does not use whips and lashes to command them, but humiliates the soldiers, causing them to obey the enemy's orders. Gōujiàn 句踐 requests to make an alliance: a single legitimate daughter will hold a broom and duster to serve the royal household in the palace; a single legitimate son will present basins and ewers to attend to the concubines; spring and autumn tributes will never cease to be offered to the royal treasury. How could the Heavenly King condescend to judge this? It is also a matter of requesting the ceremonies due to the feudal lords.
"There is a proverb that says: 'The fox buries it, and the fox digs it up again, therefore, there is no success.' Now, Your Majesty has already established the state of Yuè 越, making it known throughout the world, and now you want to destroy it again; this is Your Majesty's labor without accomplishment. Even the feudal lords of the four directions, what substance would they use to serve Wú 吳? I dare to have my humble servant exhaust his words, only hoping that Your Majesty upholds benefit and measures righteousness!"
7.2 "King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吳 and the Unsuccessful Alliance with Yuè 越"
King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吳 then announced to the high officials, saying: "Gū jiāng yǒu dà zhì yú Qí, I will grant Yuè peace, and not obstruct my plans. If Yuè changes its ways, what more could I ask for? If it does not change, and rebels, I will mobilize my army."
Shēn Xū advised, saying: "It is not permissible to grant it. For Yuè, is not truly loyal to Wú, nor is it really intimidated by the strength of our armor and weapons. The minister Dàfū Zhǒng is brave and skilled in strategy, he intends to play with our country on the palm of his hand, in order to achieve his goals. He certainly knows that the king overestimates his power and is fond of victory, therefore, he uses subtle and yielding language, to gratify your desire for ease and pleasure, causing indulgence and revelry in the states of China, to bring harm upon ourselves. Causing our armor and weapons to become dull and worn, the people to become scattered and dispersed, and day by day to become weary and weakened, and then they will peacefully accept our embers. For the King of Yuè values trust and loves his people, the four quarters of the land return to him, The year’s grains were ripe in season, the days were long and scorching. While I am still able to fight, if you do not crush it when it is a small viper, what will you do when it becomes a serpent?"
The King of Wú said: "Why do you, Great Officer, elevate Yuè so much? Is Yuè sufficient to become a great threat? If there were no Yuè, then how would I have opportunities in the spring and autumn to display my troops?" Thereupon he agreed to the peace.
About to take the oath, the King of Yuè again sent Zhūjī Yǐng to decline, saying: "Is there benefit in taking an oath? The blood from the previous oath at our mouths has not yet dried, which is enough to establish trust. Is there no benefit in taking an oath? The ruler relinquishes the awe of armor and weapons to oversee matters, but why does he value ghosts and spirits more and belittle himself?" The King of Wú thereupon agreed, hastily concluding the peace without an oath.
7.3 Fūchā Invades Qí Without Heeding Shēn Xū's Advice
King Fūchā of Wú, having agreed to the peace with Yuè, then extensively prepared his troops, The king was about to attack Qí. Shēn Xū stepped forward to advise, saying: "In the past, Heaven bestowed Yuè upon Wú, but Your Majesty did not accept it. The Mandate of Heaven can be reversed. Now, King Gōu Jiàn of Yuè is fearful and has changed his plans, abandoning his flawed decrees, lessening his levies and taxes, enacting what the people favor, and removing what the people hate. He restrains himself, enriches his populace, and his people are prosperous and numerous, with many soldiers and weapons. Yuè's presence within Wú is like a man with a disease in his heart. King Yuè's resolve to avenge his defeat by Wú is deep in his heart. He trains his soldiers, waiting for an opportunity. Now, Your Majesty does not plan against Yuè, but considers Qí and Lǔ as worries. Qí and Lǔ, compared to diseases, are merely skin ailments. How could they cross the Jiāng and Huái to compete with us for this territory? It is certain that Yuè will take over the territory of Wú.
"Would that the king also take heed from the affairs of men, and not just from water. Formerly, King Líng of Chǔ was not a proper ruler, and his ministers’ remonstrations and admonishments did not penetrate. Therefore, he built a terrace atop Zhānghuá, with a stone outer wall like a lacking section, and constructed embankments along the Hàn River to emulate Emperor Shùn. He exhausted and burdened the state of Chǔ, to attack Chén and Cài. He did not cultivate within the borders of Fāngchéng, but crossed beyond the various Xià states to plan for the eastern states, spending three years at Jǔ and Fén to subdue Wú and Yuè. His people could not endure the calamity of hunger and toil, and the three armies rebelled against the king at Gānxī. The king, alone and unattended, wandered anxiously and aimlessly in the mountains and forests. After three days, he finally encountered his personal attendant, Chóu. The king called out to him, saying, 'I have not eaten for three days.' Chóu hurried forward, and the king used his thigh as a pillow and slept on the ground. As the king slept, Chóu replaced the king's head with a clod of earth and left. The king awoke and saw no one. Then, crawling, he attempted to enter the thorn gate, but the thorn gate did not admit him. Thereupon, he entered the residence of Yùyǐn Shēn Hài 氏. The king hanged himself. Shēn Hài carried the king on his back to return, and buried him in the earth within his (Shēn Hài's) house. This is a matter of record. How could it be so quickly forgotten by the ears of the lords?
"Now the king has already altered the achievements of Gǔn and Yǔ, and arbitrarily elevating and demoting (officials), in order to exhaust the people at Gūsū. Heaven has deprived us of food, both the capital and the countryside repeatedly experience famine. Now the king intends to defy Heaven and attack Qí. The people of Wú are already estranged; the state is somewhat unstable, it is like a herd of beasts: if one is struck by an arrow, the entire herd of hundreds will scatter and flee. The king will have no way to gather them. The people of Yuè will certainly come to attack us. Even if the king regrets it, will there still be time?"
The king did not listen. In the twelfth year, he finally attacked Qí. The people of Qí engaged them in battle at Àilíng, the Qí forces were utterly defeated, The Qí 齊 army suffered a crushing defeat; The Wú 吳 people had accomplished meritorious deeds.
7.4 *Fūchāi* *Fūchāi*'s Victory at Àilíng 艾陵 Led to *Xī Sī* *Xī Sī* Delivering a Message of Explanation to Qí 齊.
King *Fūchāi* *Fūchāi* of Wú 吳, having defeated the people of Qí 齊 at Àilíng 艾陵, then sent the envoy *Xī Sī* *Xī Sī* to deliver a message of explanation to Qí 齊, saying: "I, the insignificant one, led my troops, utilizing the unworthy forces of the state of Wú 吳, and followed the banks of the Wèn 汶 River, daring not to deviate to the left or right, solely for the sake of good relations. Now, Grand Master *Guózǐ* *Guózǐ* mobilized his populace, and attacked the hunting party and troops of the state of Wú 吳. If Heaven does not know that this is a crime, then how could it cause a lesser state to be victorious!"
7.5 *Shēn Xū* *Shēn Xū* Commits Suicide
The King of Wú 吳, returning from attacking Qí 齊, then questioned *Shēn Xū* *Shēn Xū*, saying: "In the past, my late king embodied virtue and possessed enlightened sagacity, reaching to God on high. He was like a farmer working in pairs, using them to cut down and kill the weeds and undergrowth in all directions, and to establish his name in Jīng 荊. This was due to your, Grand Master's, efforts. Now, Grand Master, you are old, Yet he does not find peace and tranquility in it, but dwells on thoughts of evil. When he goes out, he blames us, the people, disrupts all laws, and uses demonic practices to harm the Wú 吳 kingdom. Now Heaven has bestowed its favor upon Wú 吳, and the Qí 齊 army has submitted. How dare I boast? The bells and drums of the former kings truly embody their spiritual essence. I dare to announce this to you, gentlemen."
Shēn Xū 申胥 put down his sword and replied: "In the past, our former kings always had ministers to assist and guide them, who were able to carry out doubtful and evil plans, and thus avoided great calamities. Now, Your Majesty has rejected the experienced elders and drawn near to mere children, consulting with them, saying: 'My commands are never disobeyed.' But this 'no disobedience' is precisely disobedience! This 'no disobedience' is the beginning of ruin! When Heaven abandons someone, it certainly makes them quickly embrace small pleasures and distance themselves from great worries. Wáng ruò bùdé zhì yú Qí, and thereby awaken the king's heart, then the state of Wú will still endure. My late lord obtained it, surely he had the means to acquire it; its loss, likewise, must also have a reason to abandon it. He was able to support fullness and prevent it from collapsing, and swiftly rescue the tilting in time. Now the king has no way to obtain it, and heavenly blessings arrive quickly, this means the fate of Wú is short. Yuán could not bear to feign illness and withdraw, to witness the king himself be captured by Yuè. Yuán begs to die first." Then he committed suicide. As he was about to die, he said: "Hang my eyes on the east gate, so that I can see the entry of Yuè, and the destruction of the state of Wú." The king was angry and said: "I will not let the grandee have such a view." So he ordered to take Shēn Xū's corpse, placed it in a leather bag, and threw it into the river.
7.6 *The Struggle for Supremacy between Wú and Jìn Unresolved, Gōu Jiàn Attacks Wú*
After King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吴 killed Shēn Xū 申胥, the year yielded a poor harvest. Thereupon, he raised an army for a northern campaign. He dug deep trenches, connecting them between the territories of Shāng 商 and Lǔ 鲁, extending north to the Yí 沂 River, and west to the Jì 济 River, in order to meet with Duke Wǔ 午 of Jìn 晋 at Huángchí 黄池.
Thereupon, King Gōujiàn 句踐 of Yuè 越 ordered Fàn Lǐ 范蠡 and Hòu Yōng 后庸 to lead an army along the coast, going up the Huái 淮 River, to cut off Wú's 吴 route. They defeated Prince Zǐ Yǒu 子友 at Gūxióngyí 姑熊夷. King Gōujiàn 句踐 of Yuè 越 then led the central army up the river to attack Wú 吴, entering its outer city, burning its Gūsū 姑蘇 palace, and moving its large ships.
Before Wú 吴 and Jìn 晋 could finish their dispute over precedence, a border messenger quickly arrived to report the chaos caused by Yuè 越. King Wú 吴, fearful, gathered his ministers and deliberated, saying, "Yuè 越 is acting without principle, violating its alliance. Now, our route is long and far, Now, our journey is long and the road is far. Should we return without attending the assembly, or attend the assembly but give precedence to Jìn? Which is more advantageous?" Wángsūn Luò said: "Dangerous matters are not spoken of easily; Luò dares to answer first. Neither option is advantageous. If we return without attending the assembly, Yuè will hear of our disarray. The people will be fearful and flee, and the distant regions will have no order. Qí, Sòng, Xú, and the 夷 tribes will say: 'Wú is already defeated!' They will attack us along the ditch, and we will have no chance of survival. If we attend the assembly but give precedence to Jìn, Jìn will then seize the authority of the feudal lords to oversee us. They will fulfill their ambitions to be recognized by the Son of Heaven. We cannot wait for that to happen, nor do we have the heart to leave. If Yuè hears of our further disarray, our people will surely revolt. We must attend the assembly and take the lead."
The King then walked up to Wángsūn Luò and said: "Take the lead and plan it; "What should we do?" Wángsūn Luò 王孫雒 said: "May the king have no doubts. My journey is long and far, there will certainly be no second command. How can (he) accomplish anything?" Wángsūn Luò 王孫雒 stepped forward, greeted the high officials with a bow and said: "A dangerous matter cannot be made safe, a matter of death cannot be made life, then there is no point in valuing wisdom. The people hate death and desire wealth and nobility to prolong their passing, (they are) the same as me. Although, they are close to their country, (and therefore) have the option to flee; I have cut off all thought of retreat, (and therefore) have no option to flee. How could they be willing to undertake this dangerous task with me? Courage and planning in serving the ruler, is used in this situation. Tonight, we must provoke a battle, in order to broaden the people's resolve. I ask the king to encourage the soldiers, in order to arouse their factional strength. Encourage them with high positions and great wealth, prepare punishments to shame those who are not encouraged, so that each man will take death lightly. "If they are going to preempt us without a battle, and we already hold the reins of the feudal lords, then on the grounds of a year of poor harvest, without any punishment, we should first dismiss them. The feudal lords will surely be pleased. Then, when they have all entered their territories, Wáng Ān will firmly establish his will, being watchful one day, lingering another day, to peacefully fulfill the Wáng's desires. He will surely use these people to enfeoff land between the Jiāng and Huái Rivers, and then be able to reach Wú." The King of Wú agreed.
7.7 *Wú* desires to battle *Jìn* and become the leader of the alliance.
The King of Wú, Hūn, then gave orders, commanding that the horses be fed and the soldiers be nourished. In the middle of the night, he ordered them to don armor and gird themselves, tie the horses' tongues, extinguish the fire pits, and arrange the king's soldiers in one hundred lines, making a hundred lines of marching. The heads of the lines were all officers and masters, Holding bells and raising halberds, establish thick screen walls, carry the commander's rhinoceros horn drinking vessel. Every ten rows has an attendant grand master, raise banners and carry drums, hold manuals and grasp drumsticks. Every ten banners has a general, carrying the usual drum, holding manuals and grasping drumsticks. Ten thousand men formed a square formation, all with white skirts, white flags, plain armor, arrows with white feathers, appearing like reeds when viewed from a distance. The king personally held the battle-axe, carrying a white flag and standing in the center of the formation. The left army was the same, all with red skirts, red banners, vermillion armor, arrows with scarlet feathers, appearing like fire when viewed from a distance. The right army was also the same, all with black skirts, black flags, black armor, arrows with crow feathers, Looking at them, they were like ink. They had 30,000 soldiers in armor, Attacking with force, And they were settled by the time the rooster crowed. Having been arrayed, They were one *lǐ* away from the Jìn army. At dawn, The king then grasped the drumsticks, Personally went to strike the bells and drums, *Dīngníng*, And shook the *chúnyú* and the *duó*, The brave and the cowardly all responded, The entire army shouted and struck their weapons to celebrate their advance, The sound shook heaven and earth.
The Jìn army was greatly alarmed, And did not come out. The Zhōu army decorated their ramparts. Then they ordered Dǒng Hè to request a parley, Saying: "Let both armies cease hostilities and make peace, Setting the time at midday. Now the great state has crossed the border, And arrived at the ramparts of our humble state's army, May I dare to ask the reason for this disorder?"
The King of Wú himself replied: "The Son of Heaven has given a command, The House of Zhou is weak and diminished; tributes no longer arrive; and it cannot appeal to God and the spirits. There is no revitalization from the Ji surname. You merely hastily came to inform me, the orphan. Day and night you followed in succession, crawling to come to your lord. Now, it is not that the royal house is not at peace that I worry about, but that I bear the burden of the multitude of Jìn. I cannot model myself after the various Róng, Dí, Chǔ, or Qín; and I cannot, as the elder brother, use force to attack one or two brotherly states. I wish to preserve the rank and title of my late lord. To advance, I dare not; to retreat, I cannot. Now, the day of the alliance is approaching, and I fear that the matter will not be accomplished, and I will be laughed at by the lords. My service to the lord is today, and not being able to serve the lord is also today. So that the envoy should not travel far, I will personally listen to your commands outside the fence."
Dǒng Hè was about to return, and the King called Zuǒ Qí, saying: "Have the acting Junior Minister of War, Zī, and five royal attendants sit before the King." Then they all stepped forward and said, " Let us offer wine to the guest in front of the other guests."
Dǒng Hè having delivered his message, then reported to Zhào Yāng, saying: "Your servant observed the countenance of the King of Wú; he seems to have a great worry. If it's a small matter, then a favored concubine or the heir son has died; if not, then the state has a great calamity; if it's a big matter, then Yuè has invaded Wú. He is poisonous, we cannot fight him. Approve his request first, so we won't be unprepared for danger, however, we cannot just agree to it." Zhào Yāng agreed.
Then Jìn ordered Dǒng Hè to deliver the reply, saying: "Our ruler dares not inspect the troops and appear in person, so he sends Hè to deliver the message, saying: 'Formerly, what you said, the House of Zhōu is already weakened, the lords and grandees have lost respect for the Son of Heaven. Please consult the tortoise shell in the sunlight, and gather the lords of Wén and Wǔ. I, being close to the Son of Heaven, Unable to escape blame, he questioned and rebuked him daily, saying: "Formerly, my Uncle Bó of Wú did not neglect the Spring and Autumn sacrifices, and would certainly lead the feudal lords to care for me alone. Now my Uncle is threatened by the Mán and Jīng barbarians, and the ancestral rites are not continued. I will employ my life to assist Zhōu Gōng in the manner prescribed by the ritual, so that they may see the states related to our one or two brothers, and alleviate your worries. Now you, my lord, conceal the king over the Eastern Sea, and your licentious reputation is known throughout the world. You have a low wall and you leap over it yourself, how much more so the Mán and Jīng barbarians, what respect do they have for the House of Zhōu? The Mandate on the Guī-tablet has a specific designation, indeed it says 'Uncle Bó of Wú,' not 'King of Wú.' This is why the feudal lords dare to decline your commands. The feudal lords do not have two lords, and Zhōu does not have two kings. If you, my lord, do not humble the Son of Heaven, so as to invite misfortune, and instead call yourself 'Duke of Wú,' how dare I not obey your commands!'" The younger brother ( agreed).
Wú Wáng (吳王) made a promise, and then retreated to his camp to hold a meeting. The Wú (吳) Duke was the first to smear the blood, the Jìn (晉) Marquis followed. After the Wú Wáng (吳王) had held the meeting, Yuè (越) heard of Yù Zhāng's (愈章) increased influence, fearing that Qí (齊) and Sòng (宋) would become harmful to him, he then ordered Wángsūn Luò (王孫雒) to first send Yǒng Huò (勇獲) to lead troops and pretend to be guests passing through Sòng (宋), in order to burn its northern outer walls and then pass through.
7.8 *Fūchāi (夫差) Retreats from Huángchí (黃池) and Sends Wángsūn Gǒu (王孫苟) to Inform the Zhōu (周)*
After Wú Wáng Fūchāi (吳王夫差) had retreated from Huángchí (黃池), he then sent Wángsūn Gǒu (王孫苟) to report his efforts to the Zhōu (周), saying: "In the past, the Chǔ (楚) people were unprincipled, not respectfully carrying out the king's affairs, thereby alienating us, their brotherly states. My late lord Hélǘ (闔廬) could not forgive or endure this, donned armor and carried a sword, held a long spear and a signaling bell, and fought bitterly with Chǔ Zhāowáng (楚昭王) in the central plains at Bǎijǔ (柏舉). Heaven forsook their loyalty, the Chǔ (楚) army was utterly defeated, the king abandoned his country, and eventually arrived at Yǐng (郢). The king gathered his officials, to offer sacrifices to their state altars. Their fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers could not get along. Fú Gài Wáng rebelled, and therefore he returned to Wú. Now, Marquis Rén of Qí does not learn from Chǔ. Furthermore, he does not obey the orders of King Gòng, thus alienating our few brotherly states. Fūchāi did not pardon or forbear, wearing armor and carrying swords, holding spears and inserting clappers (into helmets), he followed the Wèn River to attack Bó. Bamboo hats could be seen one after another at Ài Líng. Heaven abandoned its loyalty, and the Qí army retreated. How dare Fūchāi boast? It was truly Wén and Wǔ who abandoned their loyalty. Returning, it was not a fruitful year. I followed the Jiāng River and went upstream on the Huái River, digging moats and deepening the waters, going out from between Shāng and Lǔ, in order to communicate with the brotherly states. Fūchāi was able to accomplish these things, and dares to have Gǒu inform the lower officials."
The King of Zhōu replied: "Gǒu, My uncle sent his daughter, clearly desiring to share her with me alone; if I approve of this. In the past, the Zhōu 周 dynasty encountered Heaven sending down calamity, and met with misfortune among the people. How could I forget my worries and anxieties? Not only is the lower land not peaceful and tranquil. Now my uncle says: "Let us join forces and share the same virtue." If my uncle can do this, I alone will receive both (the daughter and the benefit) and thus be greatly blessed. May my uncle live many years and die a natural death; my uncle's adherence to virtue is already very great indeed!"
7.9 "Gōujiàn 勾踐 Destroys Wú 吳, Fūchāi 夫差 Commits Suicide"
King Fūchāi 夫差 of Wú 吳 returned from Huángchí 黃池, and allowed the people to rest without being on guard. The senior minister Zhǒng 種 of Yuè 越 then proposed a plan, saying: "I thought the King of Wú 吳 would eventually invade our territory. Now he dismisses his army and is not on guard, forgetting about us; we cannot be negligent. The sun god once divined for me, now the people of Wú 吳 are exhausted, and a great famine is repeatedly occurring, there is no red rice in the market, and the granaries are empty, their people will surely move to find shellfish on the shores of the Eastern Sea. The celestial omens are already revealed, And human affairs are also apparent. I have consulted the divining stalks and tortoise shell. If the king now raises an army to meet them, Seize their advantage, And do not let them repent. Those who are far from the borders of Wú, Are exhausted and have not yet arrived.
