*Gōngfǔ Wénbó*'s mother went to the *Jì* family. *Kāngzǐ* was in his court, and spoke to her, He did not respond. He followed him. Reaching the bedroom door, he entered without being announced. Kāngzǐ (康子) excused himself from the court and went in to see him, saying, "Feí (肥) did not hear the command, is it not a fault?" He said, "Have you not heard? The Son of Heaven and the feudal lords conduct public affairs with the people in the outer court, and conduct religious affairs in the inner court; from the ministers down, they conduct official duties in the outer court, and conduct family affairs in the inner court; Within the bedroom door, women manage their work there. Those above and below do the same. In the outer court, you will attend to the official duties of the ruler; in the inner court, you will manage the affairs of the Jìshì (季氏). These are not things I dare to speak of."
2.29 Mother of Gōngfǔ Wénbó (公父文伯) on Labor and Leisure
Gōngfǔ Wénbó (公父文伯) withdrew from court He went to see his mother, who was then spinning. Wén Bó said: "Even though your lord is from the family of Chù, you still spin. I fear you will incur the resentment of Jìsūn; will they think Chù is incapable of serving his lord?"
His mother sighed and said: "Lǔ is probably doomed! Have you been made an official even before you've heard of this? Sit down, I will tell you. In the past, when the sage kings settled the people, they chose barren land to settle them on, they made the people work hard and used them, therefore, they long reigned over the world. For if the people work hard, they will think, and if they think, good intentions will arise; if they are idle, they will become dissolute, and if they are dissolute, they will forget goodness, and if they forget goodness, evil intentions will arise. The people of fertile land lack talent, because they are idle; the people of barren land all incline towards righteousness, because they work hard. Therefore, the Son of Heaven greatly observed the morning sun, together with the Three Dukes, and the Nine Ministers, to establish the virtues of the land; at midday, he examined the administration, He manages the political affairs of the hundred officials. The Shī Yǐn (師尹) and Wéi Lǚ (維旅), the Mù (牧) and Xiàng (相), promulgate and order the affairs of the people. In the evening, under the light of the waning moon, together with the Grand Historian and the Sī Zài (司載), he carefully examines the heavenly punishments. At sunset, he oversees the nine concubines, ensuring they cleanly and respectfully prepare the sacrificial offerings for the Dì (禘) and Jiāo (郊) sacrifices, and only then does he retire to rest. The feudal lords, upon attending the court, diligently manage the affairs appointed by the Son of Heaven. During the day, they examine the duties of their states, and in the evening, they review their laws and punishments. At night, they warn the various artisans to avoid being negligent and dissolute, and only then do they retire to rest. The high officials and grand officers examine their duties in the morning, discuss their various administrative matters during the day, organize their affairs in the evening, and manage their household affairs at night, and only then do they retire to rest. Scholars receive instruction in the morning, explain and understand it during the day, practice and review it in the evening, and reflect on their mistakes at night, ensuring they have no regrets, and only then do they retire to rest. From the common people downwards, Act when it is clear [míng], rest when it is dark [huì], do not be idle any day.
"The queen [Wánghòu] personally weaves black cords [xuán dǎn], the wives of dukes and marquises add the large tassels [hóng] and streamers [yán], the wives of ministers make the large belts [dà dài], the titled women complete the sacrificial garments [jìfú], the wives of ranked officers add to them the court robes [cháofú], from commoners down, all clothe their husbands. At the community altar [shè] tasks are assigned, at the winter sacrifice [zhēng] merits are presented, men and women offer their achievements, if there are transgressions, there are punishments [bì]. This is the ancient system. Gentlemen labor with their minds, commoners labor with their strength, this is the teaching of the former kings. From above to below, who dares to indulge their minds and abandon their strength? Now I, being alone [guǎ], and you are in a lower position, handling affairs from morning till night, I am still afraid of forgetting the work of our ancestors. How much more so if there is idleness, how will we avoid punishment [bì]! I, Jì (冀), morning and evening cultivate myself, saying, "You must not abandon the ancestors." You now say, "Why not make yourself comfortable?" To inherit the office of the lord with this attitude, I fear that Mù Bó (穆伯)'s line will be cut off." Zhòng Ní (仲尼) heard this and said, "Disciples, remember this, the wife of the Jì (季) family will not be licentious."
2.30 *Gōngfǔ Wénbó's (公父文伯) Mother Distinguishes Between the Rites for Men and Women*
Gōngfǔ Wénbó's (公父文伯) mother was Jì Kāngzǐ's (季康子) collateral great-aunt. Kāngzǐ (康子) went to see her, and speaking to her at the door, he never crossed the threshold. At the sacrifice to Dào Zǐ (悼子), Kāngzǐ (康子) participated, but he did not accept the sacrificial meat. The table was removed without a feast. The full offering was not prepared, nor was it continued; when the continuation was not fully satisfied, he withdrew. Zhòng Ní (仲尼) heard of this and considered it a distinction between the rites for men and women.
2.31 *Gōngfǔ Wénbó's (公父文伯) Mother Wishes to Establish Wénbó (文伯)*
mother wanted to take Wénbó as her husband. She feasted her clan elders and had them recite the three chapters of the "Green Robe" (Lǜyī) poem. The elders requested that the clan who were in charge of guarding the tortoise shells for divination take care of the matter of the chamber. Shī Hài heard of this and said, "Excellent! Matters of a feast concerning men and women do not extend to the ministers of the clan; Matters of deliberation regarding the clan do not go beyond the members of the clan. Planning without offense, subtle yet clear! Poetry is for uniting intentions, song is for chanting poetry. Now, poetry is used to unite the chamber, and song is used to chant it; it is in accordance with the law."
2.32 *Gōngfǔ Wénbó's Death and His Mother's Admonishment to His Concubines*
Gōngfǔ Wénbó died. His mother admonished his concubines, saying, "I have heard that if a woman is fond of internal matters, she will die because of it; if a man is fond of external matters, he will die because of it. Now, my son has died young; I detest those who are known for their fondness of indoor affairs. "When two or three women share the sacrifice to the deceased first husband, please do not show a gaunt face, do not shed flowing tears, do not clutch your chest, do not show a worried expression. If you have mourning garments, wear them; do not add extra garments. Follow the rites and be tranquil. This will show respect for my son." Zhòng Ní heard of this and said: "No one knows a daughter better than her mother, no one knows a son better than his father. The wife of Gōngfù Shì is wise indeed! She wishes to make clear the excellent virtue of her son."
2.33 *Kǒng Qiū* Says *Gōngfù Wénbó*'s Mother Knows the Rites
The mother of *Gōngfù Wénbó* wept for *Mù Bó* in the morning and wept for *Wén Bó* in the evening. *Zhòng Ní* heard of this and said: "The wife of the *Jì* family can be said to know the rites. Her love is without partiality, and there is order between superiors and inferiors."
2.34 *Kǒng Qiū* Discusses a Large Bone
Wú attacked Yuè, It fell at Kuàijī, and a bone was obtained, its joints filled an entire cart. The lord of Wú sent an envoy to establish friendly relations and inquire, and also to ask Zhòng Ní about it, saying: "I will not evade my duty." The envoy distributed gifts to the officials, including Zhòng Ní, and Zhòng Ní accepted them. After removing the sacrificial vessels, they feasted. The guest held the bone and asked: "May I ask, why is this bone so large?" Zhòng Ní said: "I have heard that: In the past, Yǔ summoned all the spirits to Mount Kuàijī, and Fángfēng shì arrived late. Yǔ killed and exposed him, and his joints filled an entire cart. This is why it is so large." The guest said: "May I ask, who is considered a spirit?" Zhòng Ní said: "The spirits of mountains and rivers, those who are sufficient to maintain the order of the world, their guardians are spirits; the guardians of the altars of soil and grain are dukes and marquises. All belong to the king." A guest asked: "What office did Fángfēng hold?" Zhòng Ní said: "He was the ruler of the Wāngmáng clan, guarding the mountains of Fēng and Yú. His surname was Lái. In the Yú, Xià, and Shāng dynasties, they were called the Wāngmáng clan; in the Zhōu dynasty, they were called the Chángdí; now they are called Dàrén (Great Men)." The guest asked: "What is the extreme height a person can reach?" Zhòng Ní said: "The Jiāoyáo clan is three feet tall, the extreme of shortness. The tallest does not exceed ten, the extreme of number."
2.35 *Kǒng Qiū* Discusses Hù Arrows
When Zhòng Ní was in Chén, a falcon landed in the courtyard of the Marquis of Chén and died. A hù arrow pierced it, with a stone arrowhead about a foot and eight inches long. Duke Huì of Chén sent someone with the falcon to Zhòng Ní's residence to inquire about it. Zhòng Ní said: "The falcon came from afar! This is the arrow of the Sùshèn tribe. In the past, when King Wǔ of Zhōu conquered the Shāng dynasty, he opened roads to the nine *Yí* and the hundred *mán* tribes, ordering each to come with their local tribute, so that they would not forget their duties. Thereupon, the Sùshèn tribe offered *hù* arrows and stone arrowheads, the length of which was one *chǐ* and one *zhǐ*. The former king wished to demonstrate how far his excellent virtue had reached, to show it to later generations, so that they might forever be mindful of it. Therefore, he inscribed on the nock: "The Tribute Arrow of the Sùshèn Tribe," and gave it to Dà Jī to accompany Yú Húgōng when he was enfeoffed in Chén. In ancient times, precious jade was given to members of the same clan, to express affection; local tributes from distant regions were given to members of different clans, so that they would not forget their service. Therefore, Chén was given the tribute of the Sùshèn tribe. If Your Lordship would order the officials to search in the old treasury, it could be found." He ordered a search, and it was found in a golden chest, just as he said.
2.36 "Mǐn Mǎfǔ Laughs at Zǐfú Jǐngbó"
When the Qí envoy Lǘqiū came to form an alliance, Zǐfú Jǐngbó instructed his steward, saying: "Be exceedingly respectful." Mǐn Mǎfǔ laughed. Jǐngbó asked him why. He replied: "I laugh at your arrogance. Long ago, Zhèng Kǎofǔ compiled twelve odes of the Shāng dynasty and presented them to the Zhou grand master, with the "Nà" ode at the beginning. The concluding stanza of its collection says: 'From ancient times, the ancestors made [these songs]. With gentle reverence morning and evening, they were diligent in their duties.' The former sage kings, in transmitting reverence, still dared not be presumptuous, but said 'From ancient times,' ancient times were called 'in the past,' the past was called 'the ancestors.' Now you instruct your officials, saying 'Be exceedingly respectful,' that is the height of self-satisfaction. King Gōng of Zhou was able to shelter the shortcomings of Zhāo and Mù's deficiency was called "Respectful" (恭), King Gōng of Chǔ was able to recognize his mistakes and was called "Respectful" (恭). Now your teaching of the officials is "Respectful after falling into a pit," what use will the Dao be then?"
2.37 "Kǒng Qiū Criticizes Jì Kāngzǐ for Land Tax"
Jì Kāngzǐ wanted to impose a land tax, and sent Rǎn Yǒu to consult Zhòngní. Zhòngní did not answer, but privately said to Rǎn Yǒu: "Qiú, come here! Have you not heard? The former kings regulated the land, levied tax on cultivated land based on labor, and distinguished its distances; taxed villages based on income, and measured their possessions; assigned labor based on manpower, and considered their elderly and young. Thus, there were widowers, widows, orphans, and the sick, and when there was a military expedition, then they were taxed, otherwise not. In those years, To collect the yield of one *jǐng* (well-field) in millet and grain, to gather bundles of fodder, and *fǒu* (vessels) of rice, this is not excessive. The former kings considered it sufficient. If you, Jìsūn, wish to follow the law, then there is the land tax system of the Duke of Zhōu; if you wish to violate the law, then simply impose taxes arbitrarily, why ask about it then!"
*Qí Yǔ* (Discourses of Qí) 3.1 "Guǎn Zhòng's Response to Duke Huán on Hegemonic Strategies"
Duke Huán's father returned from Jǔ to Qí, and appointed Bào Shū as his steward. Bào Shū declined, saying: "I am a mediocre servant of yours, my lord. If you, my lord, bestow favor upon me so that I do not freeze or starve, then that is your gift. If you insist on governing the state, then it is not something I am capable of. If you insist on governing the state, then it should be Guǎn Yíwú. There are five things in which I am not as good as Yíwú: He is not as good at being lenient and benevolent to the people; he is not as good at; he is not as good at governing the state and not losing his grip on power; he is not as good at; he is not as good at using loyalty and trustworthiness to unite the people; he is not as good at; he is not as good at establishing rites and righteousness that can be a model for the four directions; he is not as good at; he is not as good at holding the drumsticks and standing at the army gate, causing the people to become more courageous; he is not as good at." Duke Huán said: "Guǎn Yíwú once shot at me and hit my belt hook, which is why I was near death." Bào Shū replied, "He was acting for the sake of his lord. If you pardon him and return him, he will still be the same." Duke Huán said, "What should I do?" Master Bào replied, "Request him from Lǔ." Duke Huán said, "Shī Bó, is the strategist of the lord of Lǔ, he knows I intend to employ him, he will certainly not give him to me. What should I do?" Bàozǐ answered, "Send someone to request him from Lǔ, saying, 'Our ruler has an unworthy subject in your state. He wishes to execute him before his assembled ministers, therefore requests him.' Then they will give him to us." Duke Huán ordered someone to request him from Lǔ, according to Bàoshū's words.
Duke Zhuāng asked Shī Bó about it. Shī Bó answered, "This is not because they want to execute him, but because they want to employ his policies. This Guǎnzi is a man of talent under Heaven. The state in which he resides will surely achieve its ambitions throughout the world. If he remains in Qí, he will surely be a perpetual worry for the state of Lǔ." Duke Zhuāng said, "What should be done?" Shī Bó answered, "Kill him and hand over his corpse." Duke Zhuāng was about to kill Guǎn Zhòng. The Qí envoy requested, "Our ruler wishes to personally carry out the execution. If he is not allowed to live and be executed by the ministers, I still would not be satisfied. I beg that he live." Thereupon Duke Zhuang had him bound and given to the envoy from Qi, who received him and withdrew.
When they arrived, he was interrogated three times, and bathed three times. Duke Huán personally greeted him in the suburbs, and sat with him, asking, saying: "In the past, my late lord Xiāng Fǔ built a terrace to create a high position, and when farming, hunting, netting, and shooting with arrows, he did not listen to state affairs, he belittled sages and insulted scholars, and only exalted women. Nine consorts, six concubines, hundreds of attendant concubines, their food was always fine grains and meat, their clothes were always embroidered. The soldiers were freezing and starving, the war chariots awaited the play chariots' leavings, the soldiers waited for the concubines' leftovers. Jesters laughed in front, while talented men were behind. Therefore, the state does not advance daily, nor grow monthly. I fear that the ancestral temples will not be swept clean, and the altars of the soil and grain will not receive sacrifices of blood. May I ask, what should be done about this?" Guǎnzi replied, "In the past, my former kings, King Zhāo (昭王) and King Mù (穆王), inherited the laws of King Wén (文王) and King Wǔ (武王), achieving great deeds from afar to establish their names. They gathered the elders, compared and examined those among the people who had the Way, establishing models as a standard for the people, using weights and measures to ensure correspondence, joining them together according to measure, establishing the root and initiating the end, encouraging them with rewards, correcting them with punishments, arranging the order according to age, to serve as a unifying principle for the people." Duke Huán (桓公) said, "How should this be done?" Guǎnzi replied, "In the past, when the sage kings governed the world, they organized their state by threes and their villages by fives, settling the people's dwellings, completing the people's affairs, líng brought it to an end, and carefully used its six handles."
Huán Gōng said: "What about the matter of completing the people?" Guǎn Zǐ replied: "The four kinds of people, do not let them live mixed together. If they live mixed together, their speech will be confused, and their affairs will be easily disrupted." The Duke said: "What about the scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants?" Guǎn Zǐ replied: "In the past, when the sage kings settled the scholars, they made them live in leisure and quiet; the artisans, they made them live near the government workshops; the merchants, they made them live near the marketplaces; the farmers, they made them live in the fields.
"Let the scholars gather in groups and live in districts. In leisure and quiet, fathers will speak of righteousness with fathers, sons will speak of filial piety with sons, Those who serve their lord speak of reverence, the young speak of fraternal duty. If they are accustomed to it from a young age, their hearts are at ease with it, and they are not swayed by seeing different things. Therefore, the teachings of their fathers and elder brothers are accomplished without strictness, and the learning of their sons and younger brothers is achieved without labor. Indeed, therefore, the sons of scholars are always scholars.
"Consider the artisans: they gather in groups and dwell in settlements, they examine the four seasons, they distinguish between ease and hardship in their work, they weigh and regulate their usage of materials, they discuss and compare, and harmonize different skills, they engage in their tasks from morning till night, they apply (their products) in all directions to instruct their sons and younger brothers, who talk to each other about their work, demonstrate their skills to each other, and share their achievements. If they are accustomed to it from a young age, their hearts are at ease with it, and they are not swayed by seeing different things. Therefore, the teachings of their fathers and elder brothers are accomplished without strictness, and the learning of their sons and younger brothers is achieved without labor. Indeed, therefore, the sons of artisans are always artisans.
"Now, consider the merchant. They gather in groups and settle in districts. They observe the four seasons and oversee the resources of their regions to understand the prices in the market. Carrying on their backs, on their shoulders, with oxen, and light carriages, they travel throughout the four directions, using what they have to exchange for what they lack. They buy low and sell high, engaging in these activities from dawn till dusk, in order to train their children. They communicate with each other about profits, show each other how to rely (on the trade), and discuss how to know the prices. From a young age, they become accustomed to it, and their hearts are at ease with it, and they do not change when seeing strange objects. Therefore, the teachings of their fathers and elder brothers are naturally successful, and the learning of their children is effortlessly accomplished. Thus, the children of merchants invariably become merchants.
"Now, consider the farmer. They gather in groups and settle in districts. Observe the four seasons, regulate their use according to the proper timing. Use plows (lěi), hoes (sì), threshing flails (jiā), and weed cutters (shān). When it gets cold, clear away the weeds and prepare the fields, to await the time for plowing. When it is time to plow, plow deeply and harrow quickly, to await the timely rains. When the timely rains have arrived, take up your spades (qiāng), sickles (yì), weeding hoes (nòu), and weeding knives (bó), and from dawn till dusk, attend to the fields. Take off your clothes and get to work, with your head covered in thatch and cattails, and your body dressed in coarse hemp clothes (bóshì), getting your bodies and feet wet with mud, exposing your hair and skin fully utilizing the agility of your limbs to attend to the fields. Having learned these skills from a young age, their hearts find peace in them, and they are not swayed by unusual things. Therefore, the teachings of their fathers and elder brothers are naturally accomplished without strictness, and the learning of their sons and younger brothers is effortlessly attained. Thus, the sons of farmers are always farmers, living in the fields and not hiding away. Those outstanding people among the populace who are capable of becoming scholars must be fully relied upon. If the officials see them but do not report them, their crime is fivefold. When the officials have finished with their duties, they are done."
Duke Huán said: "How should the dwellings of the people be settled?" Guǎn Zǐ replied: "Organize the state into twenty-one xiāng (townships)." Duke Huán said: "Good." Thereupon Guǎn Zǐ organized the state into twenty-one xiāng: six xiāng for industry and commerce; fifteen xiāng for scholars; the Duke led five xiāng, the Heir Apparent led five xiāng, Gāo Zǐ led five xiāng. Each of the three states established records, forming three administrations. Ministers established three stewards, artisans established three clans, the market established three xiāng, the marshes established three foresters, the mountains established three surveyors.
Duke Huán said: "I wish to engage in affairs with the feudal lords, Is it permissible?" Guǎn Zǐ replied, "Not yet. The state is not yet secure." Duke Huán asked, "How to secure the state?" Guǎn Zǐ replied, "Revise the old laws, select the good ones and diligently employ them; then enrich the people, give to those without wealth, and respect the common people, then the state will be secure." Duke Huán said, "Agreed." Thereupon he revised the old laws, selected the good ones and diligently employed them; then he enriched the people, gave to those without wealth, and respected the common people. The state being now secure, Duke Huán said, "The state is secure, is it permissible?" Guǎn Zǐ replied, "Not yet. If you rectify the ranks and files of soldiers, and repair armor and weapons, Then the great states will also rectify their ranks, repair their armor and weapons, and it will be difficult to quickly achieve your ambition. If the ruler possesses tools of attack, and the small states and feudal lords possess the means of defense, then it will be difficult to quickly achieve your ambition. If you, my lord, wish to quickly achieve your ambition among the feudal lords of the world, then matters can be secretly ordered, and governance can be entrusted." Duke Huán (Huán Gōng) said, "How should it be done?" Guǎnzi (Guǎn Zǐ) replied, "Establish domestic policies and embed military orders within them." Duke Huán (Huán Gōng) said, "Excellent."
Thereupon, Guǎnzi (Guǎn Zǐ) established the state system: "Five families form a guǐ (軌), and a leader is appointed for the guǐ (軌); ten guǐ (軌) form a lǐ (里), and the lǐ (里) has an officer; four lǐ (里) form a lián (連), and a leader is appointed for the lián (連); ten lián (連) form a xiāng (鄉), and the xiāng (鄉) has a liángrén (良人, a good man). These are used as military orders: Five families form a guǐ (軌), therefore five men form a wǔ (伍), Guǐ Zhǎng commands them; Ten Guǐ make a Lǐ, Therefore fifty men make a Xiǎo Róng, The Lǐ Yǒu Sī commands them; Four Lǐ make a Lián, Therefore two hundred men make a Zú, The Lián Zhǎng commands them; Ten Lián make a Xiāng, Therefore two thousand men make a Lǚ, The Xiāng Liáng Rén commands them; Five Xiāng have one Shuài, Therefore ten thousand men make one Jūn, The commander of the five Xiāng commands them. Three Jūn, Therefore there is the drum of the central army (Zhōng Jūn), There is the drum of the state heir (Guó Zǐ), There is the drum of Gāo Zǐ. In spring, they use the *sōu* hunt to organize the troops for war, In autumn, they use the *xiǎn* hunt to drill the soldiers. Therefore the ranks are well-ordered within the Lǐ, And the armies are well-ordered in the countryside. When the internal instruction is complete, Order them not to move. People of the Wǔ share blessings in sacrifices, And share sorrow in death and mourning, And share calamities. People check up on each other, Families check up on each other, They live together in the same generation, and play together from a young age. Therefore, in night battles, their voices can be heard by each other, enough to avoid separation; in daytime battles, their eyes can meet, enough to recognize each other. Their joy is enough for them to die for each other. They live together in happiness, move together in harmony, and grieve together in death. Therefore, in defense they are equally strong, and in battle they are equally formidable. "If a ruler has thirty thousand such soldiers, and travels throughout the world, to punish the wicked, and to protect the Zhōu house, then no ruler of a great state in the world can resist him."
3.2 "Guǎn Zhòng Assists Duke Huán in Governing"
On the first morning of the first month, the village elders report on their duties. The ruler personally asks them, saying: "In your villages, are there those who dwell in righteousness, love learning, are kind and filial to their parents, are intelligent, wise, and naturally benevolent, If anything notable is discovered in the villages and neighborhoods, report it if it exists. If it exists and is not reported, it is called concealing the obvious, and the punishment is of five types." The officials finished their work and concluded. Duke Huán gōng asked them again, saying: "In your villages, are there those with exceptional strength, courage, and able hands who stand out from the crowd? Report them if they exist. If they exist and are not reported, it is called concealing the worthy, and the punishment is of five types." The officials finished their work and concluded. Duke Huán gōng asked them again, saying: "In your villages, are there those who are not kind and filial to their parents, who are not respectful to their elders and siblings in the villages, who are arrogant, impetuous, lewd, and violent, and who do not obey the orders of superiors? Report them if they exist. If they exist and are not reported, it is called siding with the base, and the punishment is of five types." The officials finished their work and concluded. Therefore, the village heads withdrew and cultivated virtue and promoted the worthy. Huán Gōng personally met with him, and consequently employed him as an official.
Huán Gōng ordered officials to record meritorious deeds over a long period and inscribe them, to report and select accordingly. He selected the virtuous officials and re-employed them, (used) them, saying: "If someone occupies my office, and possesses meritorious achievements and excellent virtues, he should carefully and sincerely await the opportune time, lead the people with encouragement, pacify slanderous words, and be capable of compensating for the shortcomings of the official's poor governance." Huán Gōng summoned him and spoke with him, evaluating his character and assessing his qualities. If he was capable of accomplishing tasks, truly suitable to be established, then he would grant him a position. He presented him with the nation's troubles without making him distressed, and then inquired about his village, to observe his abilities without causing great harm. He would elevate him to be an assistant to a senior minister. This is called the "three selections." Guó Zǐ and Gāo Zǐ retreated to cultivate the village, the village retreated to cultivate the neighborhood, the neighborhood retreated to cultivate the ward, the ward retreated to cultivate the track, Guǐ retreated and rectified the wǔ (伍, military unit of five). Wǔ retreated and rectified the jiā (家, family). Therefore, if an ordinary person has goodness, it can be discovered and promoted; if an ordinary person has wickedness, it can be discovered and punished. Once the government is established, the xiāng (鄉, rural community) does not overstep the zhǎng (長, leader), the cháotíng (朝廷, court) does not overstep the jué (爵, noble rank), retired soldiers have no wǔ (伍, unit), retired women have no jiā (家, family responsibility). Because of this, the people all strive to do good. Compared to doing good in the xiāng (鄉), it is better to do good in the lǐ (里, neighborhood); compared to doing good in the lǐ (里), it is better to do good in the jiā (家). Therefore, shì (士, officials) dare not speak of the convenience of a single morning, but all have plans for the entire year; none dare use a plan for the entire year, but all have achievements for a lifetime.
Duke Huán (Huán Gōng) said: "What about the wǔbǐ (伍鄙, military-agricultural communities)?" Guǎn Zǐ replied: "Assess the land and levy taxes accordingly, then the people will not migrate; if the government does not repeatedly change old policies, Then the people will not be thieving; if the resources of the mountains and marshes are brought forth each at their proper time, then the people will not be careless; if the mounds and hills, the high and dry land and the low-lying land, the well-fields and cultivated fields are evenly distributed, then the people will not be confused; if the people's time is not taken away from them, then the common people will be wealthy; if the sacrificial offerings are not meager,
then the cattle and sheep will thrive." Huán Gōng said: "How should the dwellings of the people be settled?" Guǎn Zǐ replied: "Establish villages. Thirty families form a *yì* (邑), and the *yì* has an official; ten *yì* form a *zú* (卒), and the *zú* has a *zú shuài* (卒帥); ten *zú* form a *xiāng* (鄉), and the *xiāng* has a *xiāng shuài* (鄉帥); three *xiāng* form a *xiàn* (縣), and the *xiàn* has a *xiàn shuài* (縣帥); ten *xiàn* form a *shǔ* (屬), and the *shǔ* has a *dàfū* (大夫). There are five *shǔ*, Therefore, he established five Dàfū (大夫), each to govern one category; he established five Zhèng (正), each to listen to one category. Therefore, the Zhèng's (正) governance listens to the category, the governor's governance listens to the county, and the lower governance listens to the village." Huán Gōng (桓公) said: "Each of you safeguard and govern your area, do not be dissolute and negligent and fail to listen to governance!"
3.3 "Huán Gōng's (桓公) Government is Established"
On the first morning of the first month, the five category Dàfū (大夫) resumed their duties. Huán Gōng (桓公) selected those with the least merit and reprimanded them, saying: "Controlling land and allocating people is all the same, why is it that you alone have little merit? If teaching is not good, then governance will not be well-ordered. For the first and second time, you will be pardoned, but the third time will not be forgiven." Huán Gōng (桓公) also personally inquired, saying: "Within your category, are there those who dwell righteously, love learning, are kind and filial to their parents, "If there are those of intelligent and benevolent disposition, whose reputations have spread throughout the villages and neighborhoods, you must report them. If you know of them and do not report them, it is called obscuring the bright, and the punishment is fivefold." The officials finished their task and concluded it. Duke Huán Gōng then asked again, saying: "Among your subordinates, if there are those with outstanding strength and the power of arms, surpassing the others, you must report them. If you know of them and do not report them, it is called obscuring the worthy, and the punishment is fivefold." The officials finished their task and concluded it. Duke Huán Gōng then asked again, saying: "Among your subordinates, if there are those who are not kind and filial to their parents, who are not respectful and fraternal in their villages and neighborhoods, who are arrogant, impetuous, licentious, and violent, who do not follow the orders of their superiors, you must report them. If you know of them and do not report them, it is called colluding with inferiors, and the punishment is fivefold." The officials finished their task and concluded it. The Dàfū (大夫) in charge of the five categories of dependencies (五屬 wǔ shǔ) then retreated to cultivate their dependencies; those in charge of dependencies retreated to cultivate their counties; those in charge of counties retreated to cultivate their townships; those in charge of townships retreated to cultivate their platoons; those in charge of platoons retreated to cultivate their hamlets; those in charge of hamlets retreated to cultivate their families. Therefore, if a commoner possesses goodness, it can be discovered and promoted; if a commoner possesses wickedness, it can be discovered and punished. Once the government is established, it will be secure in defense and strong in conquest.
3.4 *Guǎn Zhòng (管仲) Teaches Duke Huán (桓公) to Be Friendly to Neighboring States*
Duke Huán (桓公) said: "I wish to engage with the various lords; is this permissible?" Guǎnzi (管子) replied: "Not yet. Neighboring states are not yet friendly to us. If you, my lord, wish to engage with the lords of all under Heaven, then be friendly to neighboring states." Duke Huán (桓公) said: "How?" Guǎnzi (管子) replied: "Examine our borders, and recover their invaded territories; rectify their boundaries; do not accept their contributions; and newly create leather currency for them, in order to frequently send envoys to the feudal lords, to pacify the four neighboring states, then the states bordering us will be friendly to us. Establish eighty traveling scholars, provide them with carriages and horses, clothing of fur, increase their wealth and currency, and have them travel around the four directions, to summon the virtuous scholars of the world. Leather currency and precious goods, have the people sell them in the four directions, to monitor what those above and below them desire, and select those who are licentious and disordered and tax them first."
3.5 《Guǎn Zhòng Teaches Duke Huán How to Have Enough Armor and Weapons》
Duke Huán asked: "Military commands are based on internal affairs, but the state of Qí lacks armor and weapons, what should be done?" Master Guǎn answered: "Convert minor offenses into armor and weapons." Duke Huán said: "How should it be done?" Guǎn Zǐ replied, "Serious crimes can be redeemed with a rhinoceros hide armor and a halberd; minor crimes can be redeemed with a leather shield and a halberd; petty offenses are punished with fines of gold; unintentional offenses are pardoned. For those seeking legal redress, three prohibitions are enforced so that neither the high nor the low can circumvent them, judgments are settled with a bundle of arrows. Fine metal is used to cast swords and halberds, which are tested on dogs and horses; inferior metal is used to cast hoes, weeders, axes, and mattocks, which are tested on soil and earth." Thus, armor and weapons will be abundantly sufficient.
3.6 "Duke Huán Leads the Lords to Pay Homage to the Son of Heaven"
Duke Huán said, "I wish to campaign in the south; whom should I make the leader?" Guǎn Zǐ replied, "Make Lǔ the leader. Return their encroached territories of Táng and Qián, provide shelter by the sea, create a barrier at the riverbanks of Qú Mǐ, and build fortifications around Huánshān." Duke Huán said, "I wish to campaign in the west; whom should I make the leader?" Guǎn Zǐ answered, "Take Wèi as the main focus. Return the territories they have encroached upon, including Tái, Yuán, Gū, and Qī Lǐ, the canals find refuge in the isles, so that the sea provides them with protection, and the mountains are surrounded by strong defenses." Duke Huán asked, "I wish to campaign in the north, what should be the main focus?" Guǎn Zǐ answered, "Take Yān as the main focus. Return the territories they have encroached upon, including Chái Fū and Fèi Gǒu, so that the sea provides them with protection, the canals find refuge in the isles, and the mountains are surrounded by strong defenses." The four neighboring states became very close. Having returned the encroached territories, and rectified their borders, the territory extended south to the southern slopes of Tài Mountain, west to the Jǐ River, north to the Hé River, and east to Jì Xī, possessing eight hundred chariots. Select the most licentious and chaotic states in the world and conquer them first.
Within a few years of ascending the throne, In the southeast, there were many who engaged in licentious disorder. Lái, Jǔ, Xú Yí, Wú, and Yuè were all subjugated in one battle, a leader bringing thirty-one states into submission. Subsequently, he marched south to attack Chǔ, crossed the Rǔ River, passed over Mount Fāngchéng, and gazed upon Mount Wèn. He sent tributes of silk to the Zhōu court and then returned. The feudal lords of Jīngzhōu dared not disobey and came to submit. Then he marched north to attack the Shān Róng, struck down Lìngzhī, beheaded Gūzhú, and returned south. The coastal lords dared not disobey and came to submit. He prepared sacrificial animals with the feudal lords, loading them onto carts, to swear an oath to the spirits above and below, and to join efforts and hearts with the feudal lords. He marched west to seize the lands of the Bái Dí, reaching the Xī River. Square boats and rafts were prepared, and he crossed the river on rafts, reaching the Stone Pillow. He suspended the carriages and bound the horses, crossed Mount Tàiháng and the ravines of Pì'ěr, capturing Xià, and subdued Liúshā and Xī Wú to the west. He constructed a city south of Zhōu, He returned the sacrificial meat at Jiang. The lords by the mountains and the sea, none dared not to submit, and he held a great audience of the lords at Yanggu. The number of war chariots was six, the number of chariots for ceremonial occasions was three, the lords did not loosen their armor, soldiers did not remove their shields, quivers had no bows, cases had no arrows. He concealed military affairs, practiced civil administration, led the lords to pay homage to the Son of Heaven.
3.7 "At the Kui Qiu Alliance, the Son of Heaven Bestows Sacrificial Meat Upon Duke Huan"
At the Kui Qiu Alliance, the Son of Heaven sent Zai Kong to bestow sacrificial meat upon Duke Huán, saying: "I, the one man (by decree) have matters concerning King Wen and King Wu, so I send Kong to bestow the sacrificial meat." Moreover, there was a subsequent decree saying: "Because of your humility and labor, I truly regard you as my Uncle, do not bow down." Duke Huán summoned Guǎn Zǐ and consulted with him, Guǎn Zǐ replied, saying: "When a ruler does not act like a ruler, and a minister does not act like a minister, it is the root of chaos." Huán Gōng was afraid, and went out to meet the guests, saying: "The Heavenly Majesty is so close to my face, Xiǎo Bái, how dare I accept the Son of Heaven's order saying 'You need not bow down,' fearing that I would fall down below, bringing shame to the Son of Heaven." Thereupon, he bowed down, ascended, and received the mandate. He was rewarded with the grand carriage, the dragon flag with nine streamers, the crimson flag at the gate, and the feudal lords all acknowledged his legitimacy.
3.8 "Huán Gōng becomes Hegemon of the Feudal Lords"
Huán Gōng was concerned about the feudal lords of the world. In Lǔ, there was the rebellion of the lady and Qìng Fù, two rulers were murdered, and the state was on the verge of extinction with no heir. Huán Gōng heard of this and sent Gāo Zǐ to preserve it.
The Dí people attacked Xíng. Huán Gōng built Yíyí to enfeoff him; men and women were not licentious; oxen and horses were selected and provided. The Dí people attacked Wèi. The people of Wèi moved from their huts to Cáo. Huán Gōng built Chǔqiū as a walled city to enfeoff them. Their livestock were scattered and without breeding, so Huán Gōng gave them 300 tethered horses. The lords of the land praised him for his benevolence. Thereupon, the lords of the land knew that Huán Gōng was not acting for his own benefit, and therefore the lords turned to him.
Huán Gōng knew that the lords were turning to him, so he made his gifts light and his ceremonies weighty. Therefore, the lords of the land used weary horses as gifts, and thread tassels as offerings, and deer hides cut into quarters. The envoys of the lords entered with drooping quivers, and returned with wagons loaded. Therefore, he bound them with profit, connected them with trust, and showed them his military might. Thus, the small states and lords of the land, having already given their approval to Huán Gōng, dared not turn their backs on him, embracing his profit, trusting his benevolence, and fearing his military might. Huán Gōng knew that many of the lords of the land were with him, so he greatly extended his loyalty. He acted for those for whom action was possible, and planned for those for whom planning was possible. He campaigned against Tán, accomplished it, but did not take possession of it; the lords praised his magnanimity. He opened up the fish and salt of the state of Qí to Dōnglái. Only by employing individuals like Guǎn Yíwú, Níng Qī, Xí Péng, Bīn Xūwú, and Bào Shūyá could hegemony be established.
From *Jìn Yǔ* 4.1, “Wǔ Gōng Attacks Yì, Stopping Luán Gòngzi from Dying”
Duke Wǔ attacked Yì, killing Marquis Āi. He stopped Luán Gòngzi, saying: "If you do not die, I will present you to the Son of Heaven, making you a Senior Minister, to control the government of the state of Jìn." He declined, saying: "I have heard it said: 'The people are born from three, and these should be served as one.' The father gives birth to them, the teacher teaches them, the ruler feeds them. Without the father, one is not born; without food, one does not grow; without teaching, one does not know. They are of the same category as one who gives birth, therefore one serves them as one. Where his duty lies, there he will meet his death. To repay life with death, to repay favor with strength, this is the way of man. If your servant dares to abandon the way of man for personal gain, how will the ruler instruct (others)? Furthermore, the ruler knows the success that follows him, but does not know that it depends on Qūwò. To follow the ruler with divided loyalty, what use does the ruler have for such a one?" Thereupon, he fought and died.
4.2 *Shǐ Sū* Discusses Duke Xiàn's Victory Over the Lí Róng Being Inauspicious
Duke Xiàn consulted divination about attacking the Lí Róng, and *Shǐ Sū* interpreted it, saying: "Victory, but not auspicious." The Duke said: "What do you mean?" He replied: "The divination omen shows, 'Grasping with a bone in the mouth, teeth and tusks are treacherous, Róng and Xià grapple.' Grappling means mutual victory, Your servant has already spoken. Furthermore, I fear that there are voices that will sway the people, and the state will change its mind.” The Duke said, “What voices are there? The voice rests with me, if I do not accept it, who would dare to raise it?” He replied, “If they can be swayed, their entry will surely be sweet, indulging without knowing, how can it be blocked?” The Duke did not listen, and then attacked the Lí Róng 驪戎. He conquered them. He captured Lì Jī 驪姬 and brought her back, she was favored, and he established her as his consort. The Duke gave wine to the senior officers, ordering the Sī Zhèng 司正 to fill the ceremonial cup for Shǐ Sū 史蘇, saying, “Drink without side dishes. In the campaign against the Lí Róng 驪戎, you said ‘victory is not auspicious,’ therefore, I reward you with the cup, Punishing a woman with the lack of provisions. "Conquering a state and obtaining a consort, what greater good fortune could there be!" Shǐ Sū 史蘇 finished his drink, bowed twice and kowtowed, saying: "The omen exists, your servant dares not conceal it. Concealing the record of the omen is a dereliction of my duty as a minister, there are two offenses, how can I serve my lord? A great punishment will befall me, it won't simply be a lack of provisions. But may the lord also rejoice in the good fortune while preparing for the misfortune, if there is no misfortune, what harm is there in preparing for it? If there is indeed misfortune, preparing for it will bring relief. That your servant is not believed is the good fortune of the state, how dare I fear punishment?"
After drinking, he left, Shǐ Sū 史蘇 told the senior officials: "If there are male Róng 戎, there must be female Róng 戎. If Jìn 晉 defeats the Róng 戎 with male Róng 戎, then the Róng 戎 will surely defeat Jìn 晉 with female Róng 戎, what will become of us!" Lì Kè 里克曰 : "What should be done?" Shǐ Sū 史蘇曰 : "In the past, Xià Jié 夏桀 attacked Yǒu Shī 有施. The people of Yǒu Shī 有施 offered Mèi Xǐ 妹喜 as a woman. Mèi Xǐ 妹喜 was favored, and consequently, she conspired with Yī Yǐn 伊尹 to bring about the downfall of the Xià 夏 dynasty. Yīn Xīn 殷辛 attacked Yǒu Sū 有蘇. The Yǒu Sū 有蘇 clan offered Dájǐ 妲己 as a woman. Dájǐ 妲己 was favored, and consequently, she conspired with Jiāo Gé 膠鬲 to bring about the downfall of the Yīn 殷 dynasty. King Yōu of Zhōu 周幽王 attacked Yǒu Bāo 有襃. The people of Yǒu Bāo 有襃 offered Bāo Sì 褒姒 as a woman. Bāo Sì 褒姒 was favored and gave birth to Bófú 伯服. Consequently, she conspired with Guó Shí Fǔ 虢石甫, deposed Crown Prince Yí Jiù 宜臼, and established Bófú 伯服. The Crown Prince fled to Shēn 申, and the people of Shēn 申 and the people of Zēng 繒 summoned the western Róng 戎 to attack Zhōu 周. Consequently, Zhōu 周 fell. Now, the lord of Jìn 晉 is deficient in virtue and cherishes a captured woman, further increasing her favor. Even if he were to match the kings of the three dynasties (Xià 夏, Yīn 殷, and Zhōu 周), would this be permissible? Moreover, the omen says: 'Holding with the mouth a bone, teeth and jaws are treacherous.' I divined about attacking Lí, the tortoise shell was consulted, and the divination reading of "Lí Sàn" (離散) answered me. If it is like this, it is an omen of treachery, not a place for me to settle, but "Lí" (離) implies acquisition. If we do not cross its borders, can it be called intimidation? If we do not capture its ruler, can we gnaw its bones? If we cross its borders and capture its ruler, even if we encounter teeth, and cunningly navigate through them, who would say they would not comply? If the various Xià states follow military action, what else but defeat will it be? Those who engage in governance cannot but be wary; destruction will come any day now!"
Guō Yǎn said: "The demise of the kings of the Three Dynasties (Sān Jì) was fitting. They were the masters of the people, indulging in delusions without remorse, engaging in extravagant indulgence without opposition, letting their desires run wild, without remorse anywhere. That is why they perished without being able to seek lessons from the past. Now, the current state of Jìn 晉, is merely that of a vassal lord (piānhóu 偏侯). Furthermore, its territory is small, and large states are on its borders. Even if it desires to indulge in folly, it cannot do so exclusively. Powerful families and neighboring states will serve as teachers and guardians. With many being rapidly established, will it not lead to a collective downfall? Even if they are rapidly established, they will not exceed five. Moreover, the mouth is the gateway of three or five. Therefore, the disruption caused by slanderous mouths will not exceed three or five. Furthermore, the "xié 挾" (a type of boil or tumor) is a small obstruction. It can cause minor harm, but cannot lead to the downfall of a state. Those who suffer from it will be harmed, but what harm will it cause to Jìn 晉? Even if it is called "xié 挾", and it uses cunning teeth and fangs, the mouth cannot bear it, what can it do? The state of Jìn 晉 will greatly fear it, but its downfall is not yet imminent. When the Shāng dynasty declined, their inscription had this to say: "Meager virtue, is not enough to achieve success, should not be boasted about, but only brings worry. Meager food, is not enough to rely on, cannot become nourishment, but only incurs blame." Even with the turmoil of Lí, they only incurred blame, how could they prevail? I have heard that those who gain power through chaos, their plans invariably fail the test of time, their people cannot avoid hardship, their rituals cannot last a year, their righteousness cannot extend their lifespan, their virtue cannot influence the world, their fate cannot escape the decrees of Heaven. Now, not relying on security, cannot be called skillful planning; acting through force and aggression, cannot be called gaining the support of the people; abandoning the state for one's own benefit, cannot be called ritual propriety; making excessive demands without consideration, cannot be called righteousness; To favor a merchant and incur resentment cannot be called virtuous. To have few supporters and many enemies cannot be called heavenly. If virtue and righteousness are not practiced, and propriety and righteousness are not followed, abandoning the people and losing counsel, Heaven will not approve either. As I observe your lady, if she causes trouble, it will be like a hired peasant. Even if they obtain fertile land and diligently cultivate it, they will not be able to enjoy it, but will only be doing it for others."
Shì Wěi said: "No warning is as good as preparing beforehand; only with preparation can one cope. The master's warning, and the two senior officials' words, both seem to have something to them."
Later, Lí Jī did not succeed, Jìn was set right through Qín, and it was only after five rulers were established that peace was achieved.
4.3 *Shǐ Sū's Argument that Lí Jī would surely bring chaos to Jìn*
Duke Xiàn [獻公] attacked the Lí Róng [驪戎]. He conquered them. He extinguished Lord Lí [驪子]. He captured Lì Jī [驪姬] and brought her back. He installed her as his consort. She gave birth to Xī Qí [奚齊]. Her younger sister gave birth to Zhuō Zi [卓子]. Lì Jī [驪姬] requested that Shēn Shēng [申生] be stationed at Qūwò [曲沃] to expedite supplies, Chóng'ěr [重耳] be stationed at Púchéng [蒲城], Yíwú [夷吾] be stationed at Qū [屈], and Xī Qí [奚齊] be stationed at Jiàng [絳], to prevent any possibility of disgrace. The Duke agreed to it.
The historian Sū [史蘇] went to court. He told the senior officials, "You esteemed ministers should be wary, the root of chaos has been planted! Now the ruler has made Lì Jī [驪姬] his consort, the people's resentment is surely at its peak. In past campaigns, he mobilized the people for the sake of the people, and thus the people were able to rejoice. Therefore, none did not exhaust their loyalty and utmost effort, even to death. Now the ruler mobilizes the people to enrich himself. The people gain no benefit from the outside, and inwardly resent his greed. Then there is already division between those above and those below. Yet another son is born, is this the way of Heaven? Heaven intensifies its poison, the people resent its demeanor, disaster will arise! I have heard that a 君子 (jūnzǐ) loves what is good and hates what is evil, delights in what is joyous and finds peace in what is tranquil, therefore he is able to have constancy. Felling trees without going to their roots will certainly cause them to grow back; blocking water without going to its source, will certainly cause it to flow again; extinguishing misfortune without going to its foundation, will certainly cause chaos to recur. Now, the ruler destroys his father and raises his son, this is the foundation of misfortune. Raising his son and furthermore following his desires, the son will think of avenging his father's shame and trusting in his desires; even if he likes beauty, he will surely have an evil heart, and cannot be called good. If you indulge his beauty, you will surely give him power. He obtains power to increase his desires, and follows his evil heart, he will surely ruin the state, and deeply cause chaos. Disorder invariably originates with women; the three dynasties were all like this." Lí Jī indeed caused trouble, killing the heir apparent and driving out the two dukes' sons. The gentleman said: "He knew the root of the trouble."
4.4 *Duke Xiàn was about to depose Crown Prince Shēnshēng and install Xīqí*
Lí Jī gave birth to Xīqí, and her younger sister gave birth to Zhuōzi. The Duke was about to depose Crown Prince Shēnshēng and install Xīqí. Lì Kè, Pī Zhèng, and Xún Xī met together. Lì Kè said: "The words of Shǐ Sū are about to come to pass! What shall we do about it?" Xún Xī said: "I have heard that one who serves a ruler exerts all his strength to serve, and does not hear of disobeying orders. The ruler decides, the minister follows; what room is there for disagreement?" Pī Zhèng said: "I have heard that one who serves a ruler follows what is right, and does not flatter his delusions. To delude them is to mislead the people; the people, being misled, lose virtue; this is to abandon the people. The people have a ruler to govern them with righteousness. Righteousness generates profit, profit enriches the people. How can one abandon the people with whom one dwells? You must establish a crown prince." Lì Kè said: "I am not talented, and although I may not recognize righteousness, I also do not cater to delusion. I will remain silent." The three senior officials then parted.
They held a winter sacrifice at the Wǔ Palace. The Duke claimed illness and did not attend, sending Xī Qí to oversee the affair. Měng Zú then said to the crown prince: "The eldest brother is not coming out, Xī Qí is at the temple, why don't you make a plan!" The crown prince said: "I heard the grand master Yángshé say: 'Serve the ruler with reverence, serve the father with filial piety.' Not changing what is commanded is reverence, Respecting and complying with what brings peace to one's parents is filial piety. Abandoning one's life and being disrespectful, acting arbitrarily and being unfilial, what else is there to strive for? Furthermore, to disrupt a father's love and still appreciate his gifts is disloyal; to abandon others in order to achieve self-fulfillment, is unchaste. Filial piety, respect, loyalty, chastity, are what a lord and father find comfort in. To abandon this peace and pursue other goals, is far from filial piety, I shall stop here."
4.5 *Xiàn Gōng Fá Dí Zū* (Duke Xiàn Attacks Dí Zū)
Duke Xiàn hunted, and saw the aura of Dí Zū. Returning to his chamber, he could not sleep. Xì Shūhǔ 朝, the duke spoke of it to him. He replied: "Is it the discomfort of your bed? Or perhaps because Lí Jī is not by your side?" The duke dismissed him. Upon exiting, he met Shì Wěi, who said: "Tonight, if you, my lord, cannot sleep, it must be because of the ruler of Dí Zū (翟柤)." "The ruler of Dí Zū (翟柤), is fond of exclusive profit and is not circumspect. His ministers compete in flattery to seek favor. Those who advance are obstructed, and those who retreat are resisted. Those above are greedy and ruthless, those below are lazy and opportunistic. There are those who indulge the ruler but no ministers who remonstrate, there are those who deceive superiors but no loyal subordinates. Ruler and ministers, superiors and inferiors, each satisfy their own private desires to indulge their wickedness, and the people each have their own agendas with no one to rely on. To manage a state in this way, If you, my lord, were to attack it, it could be conquered. I will not speak; you must speak of it." Shì Wěi (士蒍) reported this, and the Duke was pleased. Thereupon, he attacked Dí Zū (翟柤). Xì Shūhǔ (郤叔虎) was about to ascend the city wall when his followers said, "To abandon administrative duties and engage in labor is not your responsibility." Xì Shūhǔ (郤叔虎) said, "Having neither the wisdom of the old nor the accomplishments of the strong, how can one serve a ruler?" Having shields raised first, they consequently conquered them.
4.6 "Yōu Shī Instructs Lí Jī to Alienate the Crown Prince"
The jester of the Duke was named Shī, and he was intimate with Lí Jī. Lí Jī asked him, saying, "I wish to accomplish a great matter, but the three princes (and their followers) are a difficulty. What should I do?" He replied, "Deal with them early, making them know their limit. When people know their limit, few do not become arrogant; even with their arrogance, they are easily destroyed." Lí Jī said, "I wish to create difficulty; where should I begin?" Yōu Shī said, "It must be with Shēn Shēng. Qí wéi rén yě xiǎoxīn jīngjié ér dàzhì zhòng, [As] a person, he is meticulous and scrupulous, yet has great ambition and takes things seriously, yòu bùrěn rén. Being meticulous and scrupulous makes one easily insulted; taking things seriously makes one prone to stumble and be criticized; being unable to bear to see others suffer inevitably leads to self-restraint. Insults will soon follow." Lí Jī said, "Taking things seriously, is it not difficult to change?" Yōu Shī said, "Knowing insult means one can be insulted; being able to be insulted can change taking things seriously; if one does not know insult, one also certainly does not know [how to change], and will therefore hold to the constant. Now you are firm internally and favored externally, and whether things are good or bad, everyone believes you. If you outwardly exhaust his goodness and inwardly insult him, there is nothing that will not change. Moreover, I have heard it said: extreme meticulousness inevitably leads to foolishness. Meticulousness makes one easily insulted, and foolishness prevents one from knowing how to avoid difficulty. Even if one wishes not to change, how can one achieve it?" Therefore, she first slandered Shēn Shēng.
Lí Jī bribed the two officers, and had them say to the duke: "Now, Qūwò, is the duke's ancestral land; Pú and Èr Qū, are the duke's borders, they cannot be without masters. If the ancestral city is without a master, then the people will not be awed; if the border regions are without masters, then it will stir up the Rong's ambitions. If the Rong develop ambitions, and the people neglect their government, that is a disaster for the state. If you have the crown prince govern Qūwò, and the two dukes govern Pú and Qū, then you can awe the people and frighten the Rong, and also display the duke's authority." She made them all say: "The wilderness of the Dí, could become a capital for Jìn. Jìn opening up new territory, is it not fitting?" The duke was pleased, and so he fortified Qūwò, and had the crown prince reside there; he also fortified Pú, and had Duke Chóng'ěr reside there; Also, two *qū* (屈) cities, were where Gōngzǐ Yíwú (公子夷吾) resided. After Lí Jī (驪姬) had alienated the Crown Prince, she then spread rumors that he was the one who did it, and the Crown Prince was thereby disgraced.
4.7 *Xiàngōng* (獻公) Creates Two Armies to Attack Huò (霍)
In the sixteenth year, the Duke created two armies. The Duke led the upper army, and the Crown Prince Shēnshēng (申生) led the lower army to attack Huò (霍). Before the army departed, Shì Wěi (士蒍) said to the high officials: "The Crown Prince is the Duke's second; he should wait respectfully to inherit the throne. What office should he have? Now the Duke divides territory and gives him an office, which is to demote him. I will remonstrate to observe his reaction." Thereupon he said to the Duke: "The Crown Prince is the Duke's second, but to command the lower army, is this not inappropriate?" The Duke said: "The lower army Concerning the duplication of the superior army, I, the ruler, am above, and Shēn Shēng 申生 is below. Wouldn't that be acceptable?" Shì Wěi 士蒍 replied, "Inferiors cannot duplicate superiors." The Duke asked, "Why?" He replied, "Duplication is like the body; above, below, left, and right, all complement each other like heart and eyes. Employed without weariness, this is beneficial to the body. If the superior alternates in lifting, and the inferior alternates in treading, turning and changing flexibly, using them to serve the heart and eyes, then one can manage affairs and control all things. If the inferior usurps the superior, or competes with the superior, turning but not moving, defying the heart and eyes, they will, on the contrary, be used by things. What affair can be managed? Therefore, in ancient times, when forming an army, the army had left and right wings. Deficiencies are supplemented as they arise. If one succeeds without understanding why, therefore, defeat is frequent. If those below usurp those above, deficiencies will mutate, and defeats will be impossible to remedy. Mutations cannot be changed unless they are made public. If public declarations exceed their proper number, there will be a flaw. With a flaw, the enemy will enter. If the enemy enters, there will be calamity. There will be no time to remedy defeat. Who can repel the enemy? If the enemy gets what it wants, it is a source of worry for the state. One can take advantage of smaller states, but it will be difficult to conquer other states. May Your Lordship consider this!" The Duke said, "I have a son whom I can control. This is not your concern." He replied, "The Crown Prince is the pillar of the state. To control the pillar only after it is erected, is that not perilous!" The Duke said, "If one treats lightly what one entrusts, "What harm is there even if it's dangerous?"
Shì Wěi went out and, said to others: "The crown prince will not be established. He changes the rules without worrying about the difficulty, lightens the burden without fretting about the danger. The ruler has different intentions, so how can he be established? If he succeeds in carrying it out, he will be used to harm him; if he does not succeed, he will be punished because of it. Whether he succeeds or not, there is no way to avoid punishment. Rather than being diligent and not gaining favor, it is better to flee. The ruler gets what he wants, the crown prince avoids death far away, and gains a good reputation. He would be like Tài Bó of Wú, wouldn't that be acceptable?" The crown prince heard this and said: "Zǐ Yú's plan for me is loyal. But I have heard it said: For a son, One should worry about not being followed, not about lacking fame; as a subject, one should worry about not being diligent, not about lacking rewards. Now I am untalented but fortunate enough to be diligent and followed, what more can I ask for? How can I compare to Wú Tàibó?" The heir apparent then departed, conquered Huò and returned, and slanderous words increased.
4.8 "Yōu Shī Teaches Lí Jī to Slander Shēn Shēng"
Yōu Shī taught Lí Jī to weep in the middle of the night and say to the duke: "I have heard that Shēn Shēng greatly loves benevolence and is strong, is very kind and compassionate to the people, and everything he does is good. Now people say that the ruler is infatuated with me, which will surely disrupt the state, perhaps he will act forcefully against the ruler for the sake of the state. The ruler's life is not yet over, what will you do then? Why not kill me, so that a concubine does not disrupt the common people?" The duke said: "How could he be kind to the people but not to his father?" Lí Jī said: "I am also afraid. I have heard outsiders say: 'Practicing benevolence and governing a state are different. Practicing benevolence, loving one's relatives is called benevolence; governing a state, benefiting the state is called benevolence. Therefore, the leader of the people has no favorites, the masses are regarded as relatives. If benefiting the masses brings harmony to the people, how can they fear the ruler? Because of the masses, one does not dare to love one's relatives, the masses will especially favor him, he will have a bad beginning and a beautiful end, one who covers up the beginning with the end. All people are born for profit, if killing the ruler greatly benefits the masses, who among the masses would obstruct it? Killing one's relatives causes no resentment among the people, who among the people would abandon him? If it brings profit and favor, one's ambitions are fulfilled, and the masses are pleased, the desire for it is very strong, who would not be misled by it? Even if one wants to love the ruler, the delusion cannot be dispelled. Now, if the ruler is regarded as Zhòu 紂, if Zhòu 紂 had a virtuous son, But first, Zhou lost the Yin, without highlighting its wickedness, yet amplifying its defeat. Jun died, without necessarily requiring the hand of King Wu, yet his lineage was not abandoned, and sacrifices continue to this day. How could I know whether Zhou was good or not? If you, my lord, wish not to worry, is that acceptable? If great calamity arrives and you then worry, how will it avail you?" The lord, afraid, said: "What can be done?" Lí Jī said: "Why don't you, my lord, grow old and cede the administration to him? He will obtain the government and carry out his desires, getting what he seeks, and thereby release you, my lord. Furthermore, you should consider this: since Huán Shū, who has been able to love his relatives? Only by being without relatives can one be impartial and support everyone." The Duke said: "I cannot give him the government. I use military strength and authority, and thus I oversee the feudal lords. To lose power before death "It cannot be called martial; to have a son and be unable to overcome him, it cannot be called authoritative. If I give him power, the feudal lords will surely sever relations; if they can sever relations with me, they will surely be able to harm me. A government that harms the state is intolerable. Do not worry, I will plan for it."
Lí Jī 驪姬 said: "Because the Gāo Luò Dī 皋落狄 constantly harass our borders, preventing us from pasturing our fields every day, Your Majesty's granaries are certainly not full, and you also fear reducing your territory. Why does Your Majesty not order him to attack the Dī 狄, in order to observe his effectiveness in leading the multitude, and whether he can maintain harmony and concord with the multitude? If he does not defeat the Dī 狄, even if you punish him for his crime, it is permissible; if he defeats the Dī 狄, then he is good at using the multitude, and his requests will surely become more extensive, then you can plan against him more thoroughly. Moreover, if he defeats the Dī 狄, The feudal lords were alarmed and fearful. Our borders were not alerted. Granaries were full. The neighboring states were submissive. Territorial boundaries were secure. The ruler obtained his reliance. Moreover, he knew what was permissible and what was not. The benefits of this are many! Your Lordship should consider this!" The Duke was pleased. Therefore, he sent Shēn Shēng to attack Dōngshān. He dressed him in a one-sleeved garment, and adorned him with a golden ring. The servant Zàn heard of this, and said: "The Crown Prince is in danger! The ruler bestows him with the singular, the singular produces the strange, the strange produces the impermanent, the impermanent produces instability. He sends him on an expedition, first to observe him. Thus, he informs him with disloyalty, and shows him the power of steadfast endurance, then he will certainly resent his heart and harm his body. If he resents his heart, he will certainly harbor inner peril; if he harms his body, Surely, external dangers will arise. But if danger arises from within, how difficult! Moreover, this expedition, it is the expedition that a reckless man obstructs. His words say: "Exterminate the enemy and return." Even if you exterminate the enemy, what can you do about slander from within!" Shēn Shēng defeated the Dí and returned, but slanderous words arose in the court. The junzi said: "He understood the subtle signs."
4.9 "Shēn Shēng Attacks Dōngshān"
In the winter of the seventeenth year, the Duke ordered the Crown Prince to attack Dōngshān. Lì Kè remonstrated, saying: "Your servant has heard that the Gāoluò clan is about to fight. Your lord should release Shēn Shēng!" The Duke said: "He's already on his way!" Lì Kè replied, saying: "That's not right. If the lord goes, the Crown Prince stays to oversee the state; When the ruler travels, the crown prince follows, in order to oversee the army. Now the ruler stays, and the crown prince travels; there has never been such a thing." Duke Xiàn (獻公) said: "This is not something you know. I have heard that there are three principles for establishing a crown prince: if their persons are equal, consider their age; if their ages are the same, consider affection; if affection is doubtful, decide it by divination and casting lots. Do not scheme between my father and son; I will judge you based on this." The duke was displeased. Lì Kè (里克) withdrew and met with the crown prince. The crown prince said: "The ruler has bestowed on me a partial robe and a gold ring; what does this mean?" Lì Kè (里克) said: "Is the young master afraid? The robe covers only one side of the body, and grasping a gold ring indicates determination not to be negligent. What is the young master afraid of? Now, for one who is a son, he fears being unfilial, and does not fear not obtaining [wealth or position]. Moreover, I have heard it said: "Revere the worthy more than seeking favors." Young man, strive for this!" A gentleman said: "He knows well how to conduct himself in the relationship between father and son."
The Crown Prince then departed, Hú Tū drove the chariot, Xiān Yǒu served as the right-hand guardsman, wearing a one-sided garment and bearing a golden ring. Upon leaving, he asked Xiān Yǒu, "What is the meaning of the lord giving me this?" What is the meaning? Xiān Yǒu said: "The division in the middle of the robe and the authority of the golden ring lie in this journey. Young man, strive for this!" Hú Tū sighed and said: "To line a thick robe and fasten it with a golden ring, the cold must be severe. How can we rely on this? Even if we strive, can the Dí tribes be completely eradicated?" Xiān Yǒu said: "The imbalance of dress and posture, the key to wielding military power, lies in this journey. Exert yourself! Imbalance of posture without malice, the key to military power wards off disaster. If you are close [to the ruler] and without disaster, what else is there to worry about?" When they arrived at Jì Sāng, the Dí people came out to meet them. Shēn Shēng wanted to fight. Hú Tū remonstrated, saying: "That is not permissible. I have heard it said: 'If the ruler favors indulgence, the ministers will be in danger; if he favors internal affairs, the rightful heir will be in danger, and the state will be in peril.' If it would be a kindness to your father and distance him from death, a kindness to the people and beneficial to the state, could it be planned? Moreover, why endanger yourself among the Dí people only to stir up slander within the court?" Shēn Shēng said: "That is not permissible. The ruler's sending me is not out of affection, but rather to gauge my intentions. Therefore, they bestowed upon me strange attire, and informed me of their authority. Furthermore, there were sweet words. Words exceedingly sweet, within which there must be bitterness. Slander is within them, the lord will therefore give rise to suspicion. Even if slander comes like a scorpion, how can it be avoided? It is better to fight! If I retreat without fighting, my crime will be even greater; If I die in battle, I will still have a good reputation." Indeed, he defeated the Dí at Jìsāng and returned. Slanderous words arose even more, Hútū shut his door and did not come out. The noble man said: "This is a profound strategy."
4.10 *Lí Jī* slanders and kills Crown Prince *Shēnshēng*
Returning from Jìsāng, after five years had passed, *Lí Jī* said to the duke: "I have heard that *Shēnshēng*'s plans are becoming more profound. He says: 'I have always told the lord that he is gaining support day by day, and those who support him are not in favor of you, Yān néng shèng Dí? (How can we defeat the Di?) Jīn jīn Dí zhī shàn, (Now, you praise the Di's goodness,) qí zhì yì guǎng. (their ambition will grow even wider.) Hú Tū bù shùn, (Hú Tū does not obey,) gù bù chū. (therefore he does not come forth.) Wú wén zhī, (I have heard that,) Shēn Shēng shèn hǎo xìn ér qiáng, (Shēn Shēng greatly values trustworthiness and strength,) yòu shī yán yú zhòng yǐ, (and has already made a mistake in what he said to the multitude,) suī yù yǒu tuì, (even if he wants to withdraw,) zhòng jiāng zé yān. (the multitude will blame him.) Yán bù kě shí, (Words cannot be eaten,) zhòng bù kě mǐ, (the multitude cannot be pacified,) shì yǐ shēn móu. (therefore he is in deep trouble.) Jūn ruò bù tú, (If you, my lord, do not plan,) nán jiāng zhì yǐ!" (disaster will come!" ) Gōng yuē: (The Duke said:) "Wú bù wàng yě, (I have not forgotten,) yì wèi yǒu yǐ zhì zuì yān." (but I have not yet found a way to convict him of a crime.")
Lí Jī gào Yōu Shī yuē: (Lí Jī told Yōu Shī:) "Jūn jì xǔ wǒ shā tàizǐ ér lì Xī Qí yǐ, (The Duke has already promised me to kill the crown prince and establish Xī Qí,) wú nán Lì Kè, (I am troubled by Lì Kè,) nài hé!" (what should I do!") Yōu Shī yuē: (Yōu Shī said:) "Wú lái Lì Kè, (I will handle Lì Kè,) yī rì ér yǐ. (in just one day.) Zǐ wèi wǒ jù tè yáng zhī xiǎng, (Prepare for me a feast of a special lamb,) wú yǐ cóng zhī yǐn jiǔ. (so that I can drink wine with him.) "I am a court jester , my words are not to be taken seriously." Lí Jī 驪姬 promised this, and then prepared things. She sent the court jester Yōu Shī 優施 to give Rì Kè 里克 wine to drink. In the middle of the drinking, Yōu Shī 優施 rose and danced, saying to Rì Kè's 里克 wife: "The lord desires to feed me delicacies, I will teach you about enjoying leisure and serving a lord." Then he sang: "The leisure and enjoyment of my position, is not as good as that of the crow. Everyone gathers in the garden, he alone gathers on the withered tree." Rì Kè 里克 laughed and said: "What is meant by 'garden'? What is meant by 'withered tree'?" Yōu Shī 優施 said: "His mother became the First Lady, his son became the ruler, can this not be called a 'garden'? Now that his mother is dead, and his son is also slandered, can this not be called a 'withered tree'? A withered tree that is even wounded."
Yōu Shī 優施 left, Lì Kè dismissed the funeral offerings, and went to bed without eating. In the middle of the night, he summoned Yōu Shī and said: "Were you merely joking before? Or did you actually hear something?" He replied: "Indeed. The ruler has already permitted Lí Jī to kill the crown prince and establish Xī Qí, the plot is complete." Lì Kè said: "I supported the ruler in killing the crown prince, I cannot bear it. To restore the old relationship, I dare not. Can I escape through neutrality?" Yōu Shī said: "You can escape."
At dawn, Lì Kè met with Pī Zhèng, and said: "The words of the historian Shǐ Sū will soon come to pass! Yōu Shī told me that the ruler's plot is complete, and he intends to establish Xī Qí." Pī Zhèng said: "What did you say?" Said: "I responded with neutrality." Pī Zhèng said: "What a pity! It would have been better to say you don't believe him, thereby estranging them from each other, and also strengthening the position of the Crown Prince, drawing him to your side. Do more things for him, in order to change his mind. If his will is slightly estranged, then there will be opportunity to intervene. Now you say you are neutral, which only further strengthens his plan. If he succeeds, it will be difficult to find an opening to intervene." Lì Kè said: "What has been said cannot be taken back, moreover, people's hearts are set firmly on avoiding suspicion, how can it be undermined? What are you going to do?" Pī Zhèng said: "I have no will of my own. Therefore, serving a ruler means the ruler becomes my will, the decision is not up to me." Lì Kè said: "To kill the ruler, thinking it is righteous, fostering righteousness in order to indulge pride, and then using pride to control people's families, Wú bù gǎn. "I dare not." To suppress my will to follow you, or to become a useless person for my own benefit, abandoning righteousness to seek completeness, I cannot do it. I will submit!" The next day, he claimed illness and did not attend court. After three weeks, the plot was complete.
Lí Jī, using the duke's order, instructed Shēn Shēng, saying: "Tonight the duke dreamed of Qí Jiāng, you must quickly sacrifice and return the blessing." Shēn Shēng agreed, and sacrificed at Qū Wò, returning the blessing to Jiàng. At the public fields, Lí Jī received the blessing, and then placed poison in the wine, and placed poison hemlock in the meat. The duke arrived, and summoned Shēn Shēng to present it. At the place where the duke sacrificed, the earth heaved. Shēn Shēng was frightened and left. Lí Jī gave the meat to a dog, and the dog died; Drinking the small official's wine also proved fatal. Also died. The Duke ordered the killing of Dù Yuánkǎn. Shēn Shēng fled to Xīnchéng.
As Dù Yuánkǎn was about to die, he sent the small official Yǔ to inform Shēn Shēng, saying: "Kǎn is untalented, lacking in wisdom and slow to understand, unable to teach and guide, leading to this death. I failed to deeply understand your heart and intentions, abandoning favor to seek vast lands and hiding away; I was cautious and narrow-minded, daring not to act. Therefore, my words reached you but had no means to be advocated, hence I fell into great difficulty, and was seized by slander. Yet Kǎn dares not cherish life, but only considers being equally vile as the slanderers. I have heard that a virtuous man does not abandon his true feelings, nor retaliate against slander. If slander leads to death, so be it, he will still have a good reputation. To die without changing one's feelings is strength. To preserve one's feelings and speak on behalf of one's father is filial piety. To sacrifice one's life to accomplish one's will is benevolence. To not forget one's ruler even in death is respect. My child, strive for these! To die and leave behind love, to die and be remembered by the people, is that not acceptable?" Shēn Shēng agreed.
People said to Shēn Shēng: "It is not your fault, why not leave?" Shēn Shēng said: "It is not permissible. If I leave and the blame is lifted, it will surely fall back on the ruler; this would be resenting the ruler. To expose my father's wickedness and be laughed at by the feudal lords, where could I go to enter? To be troubled internally by my parents and troubled externally by the feudal lords is double trouble. To abandon the ruler and escape punishment is to flee from death. I have heard it said: "The benevolent do not resent their ruler, the wise do not compound their troubles, the brave do not flee from death."
