If my crime is not pardoned, to leave would certainly compound it. To leave and compound my crime is unwise. To flee from death and resent my ruler is unbenevolent. To have committed a crime and not die is cowardly. To leave and harbor deep resentment, evil cannot be compounded, death cannot be avoided, I shall prostrate myself and await my fate."
Lí Jī saw Shēnshēng and wept for him, saying: "Even his father could bear to do this to him, how much less would the people of the state? If he could bear to harm his own father and seek to please others, who would be pleased by him? If he could kill his father to benefit others, who would be benefited by him? These are all things that the people detest, it will be difficult for him to live long!" Lí Jī withdrew, Shēn Shēng then hanged himself at the temple in Xīnchéng. When he was about to die, he sent Měng Zú to speak to Hú Tū, saying: "Shēn Shēng is guilty. He did not listen to his uncle, and it has come to this, to death. Shēn Shēng does not dare to cherish his life. However, our lord is old, the state is full of troubles. If my uncle does not come forth, what will become of our lord? If my uncle could come forth and plan for our lord, Shēn Shēng would accept this favor even in ( reaching) death. Even in death, what regrets would I have!" Therefore, he was posthumously named Gòng Jūn.
After Lí Jī had killed the heir apparent Shēn Shēng, she then slandered the two other dukes' sons, saying: "Chóng'ěr and Yí Wú knew of Gòng Jūn's affair." The duke ordered the eunuch Chǔ to assassinate Chóng'ěr. Chóng'ěr fled to the Dí; he ordered Jiǎ Huá to assassinate Yí Wú. Yí Wú fled to Liáng. He completely expelled all the dukes' sons and then established Xī Qí. He first acted as magistrate; in the state there were no ducal relatives.
4.11 "Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr and Yíwú Flee"
In the twenty-second year, Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr fled into exile, reaching Bǎigǔ, they divined about going to Qí or Chǔ. Hú Yǎn said: "Do not divine. Now, Qí and Chǔ are far in distance and great in expectations; it is not suitable to go there in distress. The roads are far and difficult to pass, the expectations are great and difficult to achieve, to go in distress will bring much regret. If distressed and with much regret, one cannot hope to achieve much. If you follow my consideration, it should be to the Dí! The Dí are close to Jìn but not connected, ignorant and full of resentment, it is easy to reach by fleeing. Being unconnected allows us to conceal our wickedness, being full of resentment allows us to share their concerns. Now, if we rest our concerns with the Dí, to observe the Jìn state, "Moreover, in overseeing the actions of the various lords, nothing will be unsuccessful." Consequently, he went to the Dí people.
After one year of residence, Prince Yíwú also fled, saying: "Why not follow my elder brother and flee to the Dí people?" Jì Ruì said: "It is not permissible. If we flee together after he already left, we will not be exempted from punishment. Moreover, it is difficult to come and go together, and dwelling together breeds ill-will due to differing sentiments. It is better to flee to Liáng. Liáng is close to Qín, and Qín is on good terms with our lord. Our lord is old, if you go, Lí Jī will be fearful, and she will definitely seek aid from Qín. Because of my existence, she will surely confess and repent, and that is how I will be spared." Consequently, he went to Liáng. After living there for two years, Lí Jī sent the eunuch Chǔ, to use the jade ring as a means of explanation. In the fourth year, he was again made ruler.
4.12 "Zhōu zhī Qiáo of Guó, soon to perish, led his clan to migrate to Jìn"
The Duke of Guó dreamed he was in the temple, and there was a spirit with a human face, white hair, tiger claws, holding an axe, standing on the western hill. The Duke was frightened and ran. The spirit said: "Don't run! The Emperor commands: 'Cause Jìn to attack your gate.'" The Duke bowed and prostrated, woke up, and summoned Shǐ Yín to interpret it. He replied: "According to your words, it is Rùshōu, the god of punishment of Heaven, Heaven's affairs and officials completed." The Duke had him imprisoned, and also had the people of the state congratulate him on the dream. Zhōu zhī Qiáo told his clan: "Everyone says Guó will not last long, and now I know it. The ruler does not consider and congratulates himself on a great state attacking him—what good is that? I have heard it said: "When a large state acts according to principle, small states submit upon being attacked, calling it submission. When a small state is arrogant, large states attack them, calling it punishment." The people are resentful of their ruler's extravagance, and therefore comply with rebellious orders. Now, Jiā (嘉) dreams of extravagance being fully realized. This is Heaven taking away his discernment and increasing the people's resentment. The people resent his behavior, and Heaven further deludes him. When a large state comes to punish him, he issues orders that are met with defiance. His ancestral state is already weakened, and the lords distance themselves from him. With no internal or external support, who will offer to save him? I cannot bear to wait for it!" He was about to leave and took his clan to Jìn (晉). Six years later, the state of Guó (虢) was destroyed.
4.13 "Gōng Zhīqí (宮之奇) Knows that Yú (虞) is About to Perish"
In the campaign to attack Guó (虢), The army was dispatched from Yú. Gōng Zhīqí remonstrated but was not heeded. He left and said to his son: "Yú is about to perish! Only those who are loyal and trustworthy can hold off foreign enemies without causing harm. Eliminating darkness to respond to external threats is called loyalty; setting one's self right in conduct is called trustworthiness. Now, the ruler inflicts what he hates on others, so darkness is not eliminated. He uses bribes to destroy his own relatives, so his own person is not set right. A state cannot stand without loyalty, nor can it be stable without trustworthiness. Since he is neither loyal nor trustworthy, yet holds off foreign enemies, the enemies will know his weakness and plan to attack. He has already uprooted his own foundation; how can he last long? If I don't leave, I fear being involved." He took his family and went to the Western Mountains. In the third month, Yú was destroyed.
4.14 Xiàn Gōng asked Bǔ Yǎn in which month to attack Guó.
Xiàn Gōng asked Bǔ Yǎn, "In which month should we attack Guó?" He replied: "There is a children's rhyme that says: 'On the morning of Bǐng (丙), the Dragon's Tail is in the position of Chén (辰), the uniforms are rustling, seize the banner of Guó (虢)! The Quail constellation is bright, the Heavenly Whip (constellation) is blazing, a fire-borne army is formed, Duke of Guó (虢) will flee!' 'In fire and at dawn' Does this refer to the turn of the ninth and tenth months?"
4.15 *Zǎi Zhōu Gōng* Discusses the Qí (齊) Marquis's Fondness for Display
At the meeting of Kuíqiū (葵丘), Duke Xiàn (獻公) was about to attend the meeting, and met Zǎi Zhōu Gōng (宰周公), who said: "Your lord need not attend. The Qí (齊) Marquis is fond of display, he focuses on exerting strength and giving benefits but does not focus on virtue. Therefore, he easily summons the feudal lords but generously sends them away. He makes those who arrive encouraged and those who rebel envious. He cherishes them with classical speeches, he reduces the importance of their agreements but enriches them with virtue, in order to show his trustworthiness. He bound the feudal lords three times (to his cause), Three states that were on the verge of extinction were used to demonstrate his benevolence. Therefore, he campaigned north against the Shān Róng, and south against Chǔ, all for the sake of this western alliance. It is like a house; once the ridgepole is secured, what more needs to be added? I have heard that kindness is difficult to extend universally, and favors are difficult to repay. If kindness is not universal and favors are not repaid, it will end in resentment and hostility. If the Marquis of Qí intends to bestow kindness while demanding obligations, and fails to receive dutiful service, and instead indulges Jìn's aspirations, even if there is a later alliance, it will be in the east. My lord, have no fear; there will be those who work diligently!" The Duke then returned.
4.16 *Zǎi* Zhōu Gōng Discusses the Imminent Death of the Marquis of Jìn
Zǎi Kǒng said to his charioteer, "The Marquis of Jìn is about to die! He uses the Jǐng Huò mountains as a city wall, and the Fén, The Hé River, Sù River, and Huì River were used as canals, and the Róng and Dí tribes truly surrounded them. Wāng is just earth, if one violates what should be violated, who can fear him! Now the Marquis of Jìn does not measure whether the virtue of Qí is abundant or not, nor does he assess the power of the feudal lords, abandoning his closed-door cultivation, and acts recklessly in traveling, he has lost his mind. When a gentleman loses his mind, few do not die young or become muddled." In this year, Xiàn Gōng died. In the eighth year, there was a meeting at Huái. In the ninth year, while Huán Gōng was in his coffin, the people of Sòng attacked them.
4.17 Lì Kè Kills Xī Qí and Qín Installs Huì Gōng
In the twenty-sixth year, Xiàn Gōng died. Lì Kè was about to kill Xī Qí, and first told Xún Xī, saying: "The followers of the three sons are about to kill the young son, "What will you do?" Xún Xī said: "To cause the death of my lord and then kill his orphan, I only have death as my recourse. I will by no means follow such a course!" Lì Kè said: "If you die, and the young prince is established, would that not be acceptable? If you die, and the young prince is deposed, what use is your death?" Xún Xī said: "Formerly, my lord asked me about serving a lord, and I answered with loyalty and uprightness. My lord said: 'What does that mean?' I answered: 'To benefit the ducal house, and to do everything within my power, without refraining from anything, is loyalty. To bury the dead, and to care for the living, so that the dead do not regret being resurrected, and the living are not ashamed, is uprightness.' My words have already been spoken. How can one desire to implement my words, and yet cherish my own person? Even if it means death, how can one avoid it?"
Lì Kè told Pī Zhèng, "The followers of the three sons intend to kill the young boy, what will you do?" Pī Zhèng said, "What does Xún Xī say?" Xún Xī said, "I will die for him." Pī Zhèng said, "You should strive to do so. What two such distinguished men of the state plan, nothing will fail. I will carry it out for you. You lead the officers of the seven chariots and await me. I will use the Dí people to stir things up, and seek aid from Qín to shake things up. Establishing the weak one, you can obtain great bribes; if you establish the strong one, you can prevent them from entering the country. Whose state is it anyway!" Lì Kè said, "That will not do. I have heard that righteousness Profit is sufficient, but greed is the root of resentment. Abandoning righteousness prevents profit from being established; indulging in greed causes resentment to arise. How could a mere child incur the wrath of the people? It was all because Lí Jī misled and bewitched the ruler, falsely accusing the people of the state, slandering the many princes and seizing their advantages, causing the ruler to become confused and disoriented, trusting her and losing the state as a result, killing the innocent to be laughed at by the feudal lords, causing the common people to harbor resentment in their hearts, fearing that it would be like damming a great river, that would burst and become impossible to control. Therefore, they were going to kill Xī Qí and install a son who was abroad, to stabilize the people and quell their worries, and moreover to have support among the feudal lords, hoping that: the feudal lords would treat the state with righteousness and support it, the common people would gladly serve it, and the state could be secure. Now to kill the ruler and rely on his wealth, is to be greedy and act against righteousness. If you are greedy, the people will resent you; if you act against righteousness, wealth will not be something to rely on. To rely on wealth while the people resent you will throw the state into chaos and endanger yourself, and I fear you will be condemned by the feudal lords, "It cannot be a constant." Pī Zhèng promised. Thereupon, they killed Xī Qí, Zhuō Zi, and Lí Jī, and requested a ruler from Qín.
After killing Xī Qí, Xún Xī intended to die for him. Someone said, "It would be better to establish his younger brother and assist him." Xún Xī established Zhuō Zi. Lì Kè then killed Zhuō Zi, and Xún Xī died for him. The gentleman said, "He did not break his word."
After killing Xī Qí and Zhuō Zi, Lì Kè and Pī Zhèng sent Tú Àn Yí to inform Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr in Dí, saying, "The state is in chaos and the people are disturbed. Gaining a state lies in chaos, governing the people lies in disturbance. Why don't you enter? We ask to be your weapons." Chóng'ěr told Jiù Fàn, "Lì Kè wants to bring me in." Jiù Fàn said, "That won't do. A firm tree is established at the beginning; if the beginning is not firmly rooted, the end will surely be withered and fallen. He who governs a large state only understands the regulations of sorrow, joy, happiness, and anger, thereby guiding the people. To seek the state without mourning, is difficult; to enter by taking advantage of the chaos, is perilous. If one obtains the state through mourning, then one will surely delight in mourning, and delighting in mourning will surely grieve at life. If one enters by taking advantage of the chaos, then one will surely delight in chaos, If the regulations of sorrow, joy, happiness, and anger are so easily changed, how can you guide the people? If the people do not guide me, who will be the leader?" Chóng'ěr 重耳 said: "If not because of mourning, who will replace him? If not because of chaos, who will accept me?" Jiù Fàn 舅犯 said: "Yǎn 偃 has heard that mourning and chaos have small and large scales. The sharpness of great mourning and great chaos is not to be violated. The death of parents is great mourning, Slander among brothers leads to great disorder. Now is precisely the time for it; therefore, it is difficult." Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr came out to meet the messenger, and said, "You favor the fugitive Chóng'ěr, but while my father lives, I cannot serve as a servant to prepare and sweep, and after his death, I dare not attend the mourning to add to my guilt. Furthermore, it would be humiliating to the Great Officer; I dare to decline. For those who secure a state, it lies in befriending the populace and being good to neighbors, in relying on the people and complying with them. If it is what the populace benefits from, and what neighboring states support, then Great Officer, please follow it. Chóng'ěr dares not disobey."
Lǚ Shēng and Xì Chēng also sent Pú Chéngwǔ to inform Gōngzǐ Yíwú in Liang, saying, "The Son is giving lavish bribes to the people of Qín to seek entry; we support you as our lord." Yíwú told Jì Ruì, "Lǚ Shēng wants to install me." Jì Ruì said, "Strive for it, Son. The state is in turmoil, the people are disturbed, the Great Officers are fickle, It must not be lost. If it's not chaotic, how could we enter? If it's not dangerous, how could we find peace? Fortunately, he is the son of the ruler, and they are only seeking him. While things are chaotic, we can stir them up; who is capable of resisting us? The high officials are not steadfast; they will only place whomever the majority wishes. Who can dare not to follow? Why don't you exhaust the wealth of the state to bribe those both within and without? Do not begrudge empty prestige to seek entry. After entering, then you can plan to gather resources." Gōngzǐ Yíwú came out to meet the messenger, bowed twice and kowtowed, promising his agreement.
Lǚ Shēng came out and told the high officials: "To establish oneself as ruler immediately after the ruler's death would be audacious. If we delay for long, I fear the plotting of the feudal lords, directly summoning a ruler from abroad. Then the people will each have their own desires, and I fear even greater chaos. Why not request the ruler from Qín?" The high officials agreed. Then they sent Liáng Yóumí to report to Duke Mù of Qín, saying: "Heaven has sent misfortune upon the state of Jìn. Slanderous words are rife, Extending to the continuation of the descendants of my late lord, in hidden sorrow, scattered and exiled, relying on the wilderness, without anything to depend on. Furthermore, compounded by the death of my late lord, calamities and chaos arrive together. By your spirit, the spirits and deities bestow their favor, the criminals are able to be brought to their deserved punishment, the assembled ministers dare not settle in peace, but await your command. If you, O lord, would give regard to the state, and not forget the goodwill of our former lord, deigning to take in his fugitive descendants and establish them, to preside over his sacrifices, and moreover to pacify and comfort his country and its people, even if the neighboring feudal lords were to hear of it, who among them would not be awed and fearful of your might, and rejoice in your virtue? Ultimately showing your deep affection, receiving your generous gifts, and the assembled ministers receiving your great virtue, who in the state of Jìn would not be your collective servants?"
Qín Mù Gōng granted his assent. He sent back the envoy, and then summoned the grand officers Zǐ Míng and Gōngsūn Zhī, saying: "Regarding the turmoil in the State of Jìn, whom should I send first if I were to establish one of the two young lords? This is a matter of immediate urgency." The senior minister Zǐmíng said, "Your Lordship should send Zhí. Zhí is quick-witted and knows propriety, and his reverence allows him to perceive subtleties. His quick wit allows him to keep secrets, and his knowledge of propriety makes him suitable for missions; his reverence ensures he won't fail the mission, and his understanding of subtleties enables him to discern what is permissible and what is not. Your Lordship should send him."
So, he sent Gōngzǐ Zhí to offer condolences to Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr in Dí, saying, "Our ruler has sent Zhí to offer condolences for the grief of the young lord, and now to offer renewed condolences for the funeral. I have heard it said, 'Gaining a state often happens during a period of mourning, and losing a state often happens during a period of mourning.' The opportunity must not be missed, and the mourning cannot be prolonged. The young lord should consider this!" Chóng'ěr told Jiù Fàn. Jiù Fàn said, "That's unacceptable. A fugitive has no relatives, To consider trustworthiness and benevolence as intimate is why those who act based on it will not encounter danger. shì gù zhì zhī zhě bù dài. If one's father has died in the hall but still seeks profit, who will consider me benevolent? If others possess something rightfully, and I try to obtain it through luck, who will trust me? Without benevolence and trustworthiness, how can one have lasting profit?" Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr came out to see the envoy and said: "My lord graciously condoles with his dead servant, and further bestows a solemn command. Even if Chóng'ěr were to die, with my father dead, I was unable to participate in the mourning rites, how dare I have other ambitions to disgrace my lord's kindness?" He bowed twice, not touching his head to the ground, rose and wept, and withdrew without privately discussing matters.
Gōngzǐ Zhí withdrew and condoled with Gōngzǐ Yíwú in Liáng, with the same commission as he had condoled with Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr. Yíwú told Jì Ruì: "The people of Qín are being diligent toward me!" Jì Ruì said: "My lord, strive for it. The exiled person does not have integrity; integrity is not effective. Heavy bribes are matched with virtue; let the young lord exhaust them. Do not be stingy with wealth! Others truly possess such things; I will obtain them through fortune; is that not acceptable?" Gōngzǐ Yíwú 出見使者, bowed twice and kowtowed. He rose without weeping, and withdrew to privately speak to Gōngzǐ Zhí 曰: "Senior minister Lì Kè is with me; I will grant him a million *mǔ* of fields in Fényáng. Pī Zhèng is with me; I will grant him seven hundred thousand *mǔ* of fields in Fùcài. If you, my lord, truly assist me, I will defy the decree of Heaven! If the exiled one enters and sweeps the ancestral temples, and secures the altars of the soil and grain, what state will the exiled one share with you? You, my lord, will truly possess commanderies and counties, and moreover, enter five cities arrayed beyond the Yellow River. How can it be said that you have nothing? Also, it will be the means for you, my lord, to travel east across the ferry bridge; there will be no difficulties or emergencies. What the exiled one has with him, carried and held close, with which to await your dust and dirt [your arrival], Forty *yì* of gold, six pairs of pendants made of white jade, "I dare not accept this from the duke, please accept them for those around you."
*Gōngzǐ Zhí* returned, and reported this to Duke *Mù* of *Qín*. Duke *Mù* said: "I am dealing with *Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr*, *Chóng'ěr* is benevolent. He bowed twice without touching his head to the ground, he does not wish to be made a successor due to his exile. He rose and cried, he loves his father, that is filial piety. He withdrew and did not act in self-interest, he is not driven by profit." *Gōngzǐ Zhí* said: "Your words are mistaken. If you seek to install the ruler of *Jìn* and support him, install a benevolent one, wouldn't that be acceptable? If you seek to install the ruler of *Jìn* to achieve fame throughout the world, then it's better to install an unbenevolent one to manipulate things, and then you can advance or retreat as needed. I have heard it said: 'Benevolence has a place, might has a place. Benevolence puts virtue in place; military force puts submission in place.』" Therefore, they first placed Gōngzǐ Yíwú; he indeed became Huì Gōng.
4.18 《Jì Ruì's Answer to Duke Mù of Qín's Question》
Duke Mù asked Jì Ruì, saying: "Which person does the young lord rely on in Jìn?" He replied, saying: "I have heard that a fugitive has no party; if he has a party, he will surely have enemies. When Yíwú was young, he did not like playing; he did not exceed what was restored to him; his anger did not reach his face; and when he grew up, he did not change. Therefore, his fleeing did not cause resentment in the state, and the people were at peace with him. If not, Yíwú is not glib; on whom could he rely?" The gentleman said: "It is good to advise subtly."
4.19 《Duke Huì Enters and Turns His Back on the External and Internal Bribes》
Duke Huì entered into power and reneged on the bribes he had offered to both the internal and external parties. The common people sang a song that said: "When flattery meets flattery, one will surely lose their land. When deceit meets deceit, one will surely lose their bribes. Getting something and becoming complacent, one will eventually meet their downfall. Not learning from losing land, misfortune and chaos will arise." Later, Lǐ and Pī died in a calamity, and the Duke met his end in Hán. Guō Yǎn said: "Excellent! The voice of the people is the gateway to both fortune and misfortune. Therefore, a wise ruler carefully considers the opinions of the people before acting, examines warnings before planning, measures and contemplates before acting, and thus accomplishes everything. Planning internally and measuring externally, examining and reflecting tirelessly, examining and practicing daily, preparations will be complete."
4.20 "Duke Huì Reburies Shìzǐ Gòng"
After Duke Huìgōng 惠公 ascended the throne, he exhumed the former crown prince and reburied him, and the stench spread abroad. The people of the state sang: "Loyalty receives no reward. What sort of person is this who emits such a foul odor? Loyalty is ignored, Trustworthiness is deemed insincere. The state has no laws, Living idly, hoping for luck. Not changing his loyalty, The great fate will soon collapse. O awe! O tenderness! Each of you gather your possessions, to await where you shall return. O alas! O discord! My heart is filled with sorrow. Twice seven years (fourteen years), It will surely disappear. If there were a Dí 狄 prince, I would rely on him. To pacify and protect the state, To be the king's consort." Guō Yǎn 郭偃 said: "How difficult it is to do good!
The ruler reburies the former ruler thinking it glorious, And evil will grow more apparent. When a person is beautiful within, it will surely spread to the outside, and extend to the people, who will truly support them. Evil is also like this. Therefore, one's actions must be cautious. Someone will surely know it. In fourteen years, will your lord's heir be replaced? This calculation has been announced to the people. Will Gongzi Chóng'ěr enter? His spirit is revealed to the people. If he enters, he will surely become the hegemon among the lords and meet the Son of Heaven, his light will shine brightly upon the people. Calculation is the record of words, spirit is the technique of intention, light is the brilliance of clarity. Record words to narrate it, describe intention to guide it, make clarity shine to illuminate it. If it doesn't arrive, what are we waiting for? Is the one who wishes to lead going to act? He will arrive soon!"
4.21 "Duke Huì Regrets Killing Lìkè"
After Duke Huì killed Lì Kè, he regretted it. He said, "Ruì was the one who caused me to mistakenly kill the pillar of my state." Guō Yǎn heard this and said, "The one who offered unsolicited advice was Jì Ruì. The one who killed without planning was the ruler. To offer unsolicited advice is disloyal; to kill without planning is inauspicious. Disloyalty incurs the ruler's punishment; inauspiciousness brings heavenly disaster. Incurring the ruler's punishment means death and execution; bringing heavenly disaster means no descendants. Those who pursue the right path should not forget this, for it is about to happen!" When Duke Wén entered (the state), the people of Qín killed Jì Ruì and exposed his corpse.
4.22 《Huì Gōng Shā Pī Zhèng》
After Duke Huì (Huì Gōng) ascended the throne, he reneged on the agreement with Qín and offered bribes instead. He sent Pī Zhèng as an envoy to Qín, ostensibly to express gratitude. However, he then killed Lì Kè, saying: "You killed two rulers and one grand master; would it not be difficult to serve as a minister for your lord?"
Pī Zhèng, while in Qín, used delaying tactics regarding the tribute, and then said to Duke Mù (Mù Gōng): "If you summon Lǚ Shēng, Xì Chēng, and Jì Ruì with sincere inquiries, then detain them, and use an army to escort Gōngzǐ Chóng'ěr; with internal actions from my faction, the ruler of Jìn will surely flee." Duke Mù sent Léng Zhì to respond to the inquiries, and also to summon the three grand masters. Zhèng was about to proceed with the plan with the Qín envoy, but Jì Ruì said: "Zhèng's mission was meager, yet the response is generous. He must be speaking ill of us to Qín, surely attempting to lure us. If we don't kill him, he will certainly cause trouble." Therefore, Pī Zhèng and the seven senior officials were killed: Gòng Huá, Jiǎ Huá, Shū Jiān, Zhuī Chuǎn, Léi Hǔ, Tè Gōng, Shān Qí. These were all members of the faction of Lǐ and Pī. Pī Bào fled to Qín.
When Pī Zhèng returned from Qín, having heard of the death of Lì Kè, he saw Gòng Huá and said, "Is it possible to enter?" Gòng Huá said, "The other gentlemen are all abroad and cannot be reached. You are an envoy to Qín, it is possible!" Pī Zhèng entered, and the ruler killed him. Gòng Cì said to Gòng Huá, "Will you flee? It will reach you!" Gòng Huá said, "My lord's entry was my plan, will await." Cì said: "Who knows this?" Gòng Huá said: "It cannot be. To know and betray him, is untrustworthy; to plot and entrap others, is unwise; to be trapped and not die is unheroic. To bear three great evils, where will you go? You should go, I will await death here."
The son of Pī Zhèng, named Bào, fled to Qín, and said to Duke Mù: "The ruler of Jìn has greatly lost his followers, betrayed his lord's gifts, killed Lǐ Kè, and is jealous of those in high positions, Jiā Fù rebelled, but failed and died. The duke then pursued the rebellious bandits, and said to Yáng Bì: "From Duke Mù to the present, the chaos of war has not ceased, the people's will is not satisfied, and disasters have been endless. Separating from the people will quickly attract enemies, and I fear it will extend to my own person. What should I do?" Yáng Bì replied, "If the roots are still planted, the branches and leaves will grow more luxuriantly, and the roots will become even more lush, which is why it's difficult to stop. Now, if you were to enlarge its trunk, remove its branches and leaves, and sever its roots, you could have a short respite."
The duke said, "You should really plan this." He replied, "The plan lies in clear instructions, clear instructions lie in authority and power, and authority and power lie in the ruler. If the ruler selects the descendants of worthy people who have permanent positions in the state and establishes them, Also, those who indulge their ambitions, harm the ruler and disrupt the state should be removed, thus establishing authority and distancing power. The people will fear his authority, and cherish his virtue, none will be able to disobey. If they obey, then the hearts of the people can all be nurtured. Nurture their hearts and understand their desires and dislikes, who would steal life? If they do not steal life, then none will think of rebellion. Moreover, the Luán clan has been falsely accusing the state of Jìn for a long time, Luán Shū indeed overthrew the clan temple, murdered Duke Lì to enrich his family, if the Luán clan is destroyed, then the people will be in awe. Now, if I were to raise up the descendants of Xiá, Yuán, Hán and Wèi and reward them, then the people would be grateful. Authority and gratitude each in their proper place, then the state will be secure, the ruler will govern and the state will be secure, who would want to rebel then?"
The ruler said: "Luán Shū established my late lord, Luán Yíng did not incur guilt, how can this be done?" Yáng Bì said: "In governing a state justly, one cannot be intimate with power, and the exercise of power cannot be concealed by personal motives. If one is intimate with power, the people will not be guided; if the exercise of power is concealed by personal motives, the government will not function. If the government does not function, how can one guide the people? If the people are not guided, it is as if there is no ruler. Thus, this intimacy and concealment are doubly harmful, and also exhausting to oneself. Your Lordship should consider this carefully! If you care for Luán Yíng, then clearly pursue the band of thieves, and understand the principles of the state. Reprimand and send them away, provide thorough admonitions and plans, and wait for him. If he seeks to fulfill his ambitions and retaliate against the ruler, what crime could be greater? To destroy him would still be too little. If he does not dare and flees far away, then strengthen your diplomatic ties with him and encourage him, to repay his virtue; would that not be acceptable?"
The Duke (Jìn Píng Gōng 晉平公) granted his permission and completely drove out the bandits, sending Qí Wǔ 祁午 and Yáng Bì 陽畢 to Qūwò 曲沃 to pursue Luán Yíng 欒盈. Luán Yíng 欒盈 fled to Chǔ 楚. Thereupon, he issued an order to the people of the state, saying: "Since the time of Duke Wén 文公, those who have contributed significantly to the previous rulers but whose descendants have not been established will be granted establishment. Whoever reports such a person will be rewarded." After three years, Luán Yíng 欒盈 entered Jàng 絳 during the day and committed acts of banditry. Fàn Xuānzǐ 范宣子 escorted the Duke into the palace of Duke Xiāng 襄公. Luán Yíng 欒盈 was unsuccessful and fled to Qūwò 曲沃. He then assassinated Luán Yíng 欒盈 and exterminated the Luán 欒 clan. Thus, for the rest of Duke Píng's 平公 life, there were no internal rebellions.
4.88 *Xīn Yú 辛俞 Flees with the Luán 欒 Clan*
When Luán Huáizǐ 欒懷子 fled, the governing ministers ordered the retainers of the Luán 欒 clan not to follow him. Severe punishments would be imposed on those who followed the Luán 欒 clan. Xīn Yú 辛俞, a retainer of the Luán 欒 clan, set out. The officers apprehended him and presented him to the Duke. The Duke said: "There is a great decree in the state. "What is the reason for offending them?" He replied, "I am obeying them, how could I dare to offend them? The regent said, 'Do not follow the Luán Shì, but follow the ruler,' this is a clear order to certainly follow the ruler. I have heard it said, 'For three generations serving a family, it is the ruler's; for two generations or less, it is the master's.' Serve the ruler with death, serve the master with diligence, this is the ruler's clear order. Since my grandfather, without great support in the Jìn state, has been attached to the Luán Shì for generations, it has been three generations now, therefore I dare not but serve the ruler. Now the regent says 'Those who do not follow the ruler will face great punishment,' how dare I forget my duty to die and betray my ruler, thus troubling the Minister of Crime?" The Duke was pleased, earnestly stopped him, but he would not, and offered him lavish gifts. He declined, saying: "Your subject has already presented his words. My heart is set on upholding my principles, and my words are the means to carry them out; this is how I serve my lord. If I were to accept your lord's gift, it would be a betrayal of my previous words. Your lord asked for my words, I presented them, but before I have withdrawn, he contradicts them. How then can I serve my lord?" The lord, knowing that it was impossible to persuade him, then sent him away.
4.89 *Shū Xiàng*'s Mother Said the Yángshé Clan Must Be Destroyed
When Shū Yú was born, his mother looked at him and said: "He has the eyes of a tiger and the snout of a pig, the shoulders of a kite and the belly of an ox. Ravines can be filled, but he will never be satisfied. He will surely die because of bribes." And so she did not look at him again. When Yáng Shíwǒ was born, Shū Xiàng's mother heard of it. She went to the hall,
he then turned back, and said: "That voice, the voice of a jackal, the one who will ultimately destroy the clan of the Yángshé lineage, must be this child."
4.90 *Shūsūn Mùzǐ's Discourse on Dying Without Decaying*
Duke Xiāng of Lǔ sent Shūsūn Mùzǐ on a diplomatic visit. Fàn Xuānzǐ questioned him, saying: "People have a saying: 'to die without decaying', what does it mean?" Mùzǐ did not answer. Xuānzǐ said: "In the past, the ancestor of Gài, from Yú and before was the Táotáng clan, in the Xià dynasty was the Yùlóng clan, in the Shāng dynasty was the Shǐwéi clan, in the Zhōu dynasty was the Táng and Dù clans. When Zhōu declined, Jìn continued it, becoming the Fàn clan, is this what it means?" He replied, "According to what Bào has heard, this is called hereditary privilege, not immortality. Zāng Wénzhòng 臧文仲, the former senior minister of Lǔ 魯, his body is dead, but his words stand in later generations, this is called dying but not decaying."
4.91 "Fàn Xuānzǐ 范宣子 Contends for Land with the Grand Master Hé 和"
Fàn Xuānzǐ 范宣子 contended for land with the grand master Hé 和, and after a long time, nothing was achieved. Xuānzǐ 宣子 wanted to attack him, and asked Bó Huá 伯華. Bó Huá 伯華 said, "There are military matters outside, and domestic affairs inside. I, Chì 赤, deal with external affairs, and dare not encroach on official duties. Moreover, there is something in your heart, my lord, that has come out, which can be investigated." He asked Sūn Línfǔ 孫林甫, Sūn Línfǔ 孫林甫 said, "A guest, is how I serve you, my lord, I only wait for orders." He asked Zhāng Lǎo. Zhāng Lǎo said, "I, old as I am, serve you in military matters. If it is not about warfare, then it is not something I know." He asked Qí Xī. Qí Xī said, "The lack of respect among the members of the ducal clan, the perversity within the ducal house, the wickedness in internal affairs, and the greed of the high officials, these are my faults. If I were to use the lord's office to pursue your personal affairs, I fear your troubles would only increase." He asked Jí Yǎn. Jí Yǎn said, "I follow Zhāng Mèng with my axe and halberd, obeying his orders daily. Those orders are like your orders, how can I have two masters? To abandon your orders and act on my own is to betray you." He asked Shū Yú. Shū Yú said, "Wait for me to kill him for you."
Shū Xiàng heard of this and saw Xuān Zǐ, saying, "I heard that Zǐ Yǔ is not at peace with Hé. I have asked all the senior officials, but still cannot make a decision. Why not consult Zǐ Shí? Zǐ Shí is truly upright and learned; his uprightness enables him to make clear distinctions, and his learning enables him to compare matters across different levels. Moreover, he is an elder of your family. I have heard that when a state has major affairs, it must follow established laws, and consult experienced elders before acting." Sīmǎ Hóu met with him and said: "I heard that you, sir, are angry with Hé, which I did not believe. All the lords have divided loyalties, and this is what you should be concerned about. To be angry with the senior officials instead, is not your responsibility." Qí Wǔ met with him and said: "Jìn is the leader of the lords, and you, sir, are the chief minister. If you can stabilize the lords and make them obey the orders of Jìn, who in the state of Jìn would not follow you? Why must it be Hé? Hé mì hé, dà hé yǐ píng xiǎo hū!"
Xuān Zǐ asked Zī Shí, Zī Shí replied, "In the past, Xí Shū Zǐ avoided the difficulties of the Zhōu dynasty in the state of Jìn, and his son Zǐ Yú was appointed to manage affairs, in order to rectify the court, so there were no treacherous officials in the court; he became Minister of Works, in order to rectify the state, so the state had no failed enterprises. The position was passed down to Wǔ Zǐ, who assisted Wén and Xiāng as lords of the various states, so the various lords had no divided loyalties. And when he became a senior minister, to assist Chéng and Jǐng, the army had no failed policies. And when he became the commander in battle, and lived as grand tutor, straightened out the criminal law, and compiled the training ordinances, the state had no treacherous people, and later people could emulate him; therefore, he received Suí and Fàn. And when Wén Zǐ finalized the alliance between Jìn and Jīng, Make the states of your brothers abundant, so that there are no rifts between them. It was for this reason that you received Xún and Lì. Now, you, my son, have inherited the throne. In the court, there are no treacherous actions; in the state, there are no wicked people. Thus, there are no troubles from all four directions, and no internal or external worries. You rely on the merits of your three sons to enjoy your rank and position. Now that there are no troubles, yet you do not appease Hé, but instead increase your favor towards him. What kind of governance is this?" Xuānzǐ was pleased and increased Hé's land and gave it to him.
4.92 "Zī Shí Dies, Fàn Xuānzǐ Encourages Fàn Xiànzǐ"
Zī Shí died. Fàn Xuānzǐ said to Xiànzǐ: "Alas! In the past, I had Zī Shí, whom I looked to morning and evening, to assist the state of Jìn, and also for my family. Now, when I observe you, you are unable to be decisive, and you have no one to consult with. "What should be done with him?" He replied: "Yāng in his conduct is respectful; he does not dare to be at ease, reverently studies and loves benevolence, is harmonious with the government and loves its ways, consults with the masses and does not seek personal gain, though his private opinions are sincere, he does not dare to say they are correct, but follows the lead of elders." Xuān Zǐ said: "He can escape punishment."
4.93 "Shī Kuàng's Discourse on Music"
Duke Píng was fond of a new kind of music. Shī Kuàng said: "The ducal house will surely decline! Your sagacity, my lord, is a sign of decay. Now, music is for opening up the airs of mountains and rivers, for spreading virtue to the distant and vast. It spreads virtue so as to broaden it; it influences mountains and rivers so as to make them distant; it influences things so as to have them heeded; it follows the *Shi* to sing of them; it follows the *Li* to regulate them. Now, if virtue is broad, distant, and has proper timing, Shì yǐ yuǎn fú ér ěr bù qiān."
Therefore, those far away are submissive, while those nearby do not move away.
4.94 *Shū Xiàng Jiàn Shā Shù Xiāng*
*Shū Xiàng's* remonstrance against killing *Shù Xiāng* Píng Gōng shot a quail, *Píng Gōng* did not die, and ordered *Shù Xiāng* to seize it, but he failed. The Duke was angered and detained him, intending to kill him. *Shū Xiàng* heard of this. In the evening, the ruler told him about it. *Shū Xiàng* said, "Your lord must kill him. In the past, my former lord, Táng Shū, shot a rhinoceros in the Tú Forest, killed it, and used it to make a great armor, and was enfeoffed in Jìn. Now, you, as successor to my former lord Táng Shū, shot a quail that did not die, and could not seize it. This is making a public display of our lord's shame. Your lord must kill him quickly and not let it be heard far away." The ruler was ashamed and then quickly ordered him to be pardoned.
4.95 *Shū Xiàng Lùn Bǐ Ér Bù Bié* He stroked him and wept, saying: "From now on, after his father's death, I will have no one to compare with in serving the lord! In the past, his father began it, and I finished it; I began it, and the master finished it; there is nothing that cannot be done." Jí Yǎn was at his side and said: "Does a gentleman have partisans?" Shū Xiàng said: "A gentleman has associates but does not discriminate; he associates with virtue to assist in affairs. To associate means to draw in a faction to enrich oneself, to benefit oneself and forget the lord; that is discrimination."
4.96 "Shū Xiàng and Zǐ Zhū Bùxīn contend with force but compete with strength"
Duke Jǐng of Qín sent his younger brother Zhēn to seek peace, Shū Xiàng ordered that the envoy Zǐ Yuán be summoned. The envoy Zǐ Zhū said: "Zhū is here." Shū Xiàng said: "Summon Zǐ Yuán." Zǐ Zhū said: "Zhū should be the one to receive him." Shū Xiàng said, "Xī also wants Zǐ Yuán to answer the guests." Zǐ Zhū angrily said, "All are the ruler's ministers, their ranks and salaries are the same, why do you degrade Zhū?" He stroked his sword and approached him. Shū Xiàng said, "Qín and Jìn have been at odds for a long time, today's event is fortunately successful, and our descendants will enjoy it. If it is not successful, the soldiers of the three armies will be exposed as bones. Fū Zǐ Yuán, he guides the speech of the host and guests without partiality, you often make it easy. Those who use treachery to serve the ruler, that is what I can prevent." He flicked his sleeves and followed him, and entered to rescue him. Duke Píng heard of this, and said, "Jìn is probably in good standing! What my ministers contend for is great." Shī Kuàng was in attendance, and said, "The ducal house fears being demeaned; its ministers do not compete in heart, but contend in strength."
4.97 Shū Xiàng Discusses Loyalty and Trustworthiness as the Foundation
The grand officers of the various lords were in alliance in Sòng, Chǔ's Commander-in-Chief Zǐ Mù wanted to attack the Jìn army.

p.seg: In the most severe punishment one uses armour and weapons,
in the next serious one uses axes,
in the next serious one uses knives and saws,
in the next one uses mutilation of the knee-cap or branding
as mild punishment the used the whip and caning
in order to assert their authority
